Name: A Gallon of Blood
Instructions: Stormpike Soldier's Blood (5)
Progress: You must strike down our enemies and bring to me their blood.
Comment1: This is how it works. In the Frostwolf village is a small cave just to the left of the blacksmith. The primalist there accepts turnins of Stormpike Soldier's Blood, and once she gets enough she will begin walking towards the middle of the map. She's a level 60+ elite and has an entourage, so she CAN handle herself, but it's important to stay with her and keep her healed, because the Alliance wants her dead. Anyway, once she gets to the middle of the map, she will begin a summoning ritual. Once she and her assistants complete the ritual, a swirly pattern will appear at her feet. Now this is the important part: Ten Horde players must be there when this happens to right-click the swirly thing on the ground and stand still while the ritual completes. Think of it liked a warlock summon, where people have to right click the portal. This works the same way. If the primalist makes it to her spot and summons, and if ten Horde players assist her in summoning, she will summon Lok, who basically looks like a pale blue earth elemental. He will go to the center of the map and chill (pun intended) for ten minutes. During that time, he will attack any Alliance that get too close. He's VERY strong, but be careful that you don't let the Alliance kite him away. Each time he defeats an Alliance player, he will grow in size and power. After the allotted ten minutes, he will begin going on a rampage and destroying everything in his path. The Alliance will attempt to kite him, so it's very important that warriors, druids, mages.. anyone with an intercept stays with him. Lok is VERY powerful but he's rather stupid. As soon as one person has aggro from him, he will stay on that person until they're dead no matter where they take him. So, it's important to keep the Alliance from defeating him or letting him get pulled to some random corner of the map.

Name: Enemy Booty
Instructions: Bring 20 Armor Scraps to Smith Regzar in Frostwolf Village. Armor Scraps (20)
Progress: How goes the hunting, <name>. Do you have any armor scraps for me?
Comment1: If one is attempting to use Alterac Valley as a way to increase your rep for any of the Horde factions, then doing the repeatable turn in quests like this one are a must. This particular quest leads into the [url='http://classicdb.ch/?quest=6741']'More Booty!'[/url] repeatable version. The rep reward for that is 10 rep with Orgrimmar per 20 [url='http://classicdb.ch/?item=17422']armor scraps[/url] turned in. This might not seem like a lot of rep at first, but keep in mind that armor scraps are some of the most abundant drops off of your fallen enemies, often dropping ~20 armor scraps apiece. If you are constantly in the heat of battle and remember to loot the ones who are killed, you can quite easily pick up several hundred armor scraps to turn in. Additionally, turning in numerous stacks of armor scraps to [url='http://classicdb.ch/?npc=13176']Smith Regzar[/url] will allow him to upgrade the guards that protect your territory and graveyards from veterans to champions all the way to elite. Turning in armor scraps also will reward you with a 30 minute 'Polished armor' buff that increases your armor by 10% One last thing to remember. Getting 'Orgrimmar' rep from any of these quests also gives rep across the faction board, so if you are looking to get to exalted with everyone in the faction, Alterac Valley is your most cost-and-time effective option as opposed to buying/farming runecloth and turning them in at 75 rep/stack of 20 Tonight while AVing off and on over a four hour period netted an increase of 1200 points of rep from this and the other repeatable turn ins

Comment3: I just solo'd this quest as a 66 Affliction Warlock. Of course, everyone in the 61-70 bracket is too busy telling you how long ago [i]they[/i] finished the quest to actually help you complete it. So, a few failed battlegrounds later, I finally mastered the art. I assume most classes with mass CC could use this method (i.e., Priests with Psychic Scream, potentially a Frost Mage's Frost Nova, etc.) Basically, just zerg rush into the entrance of the cave. Rush straight between the two big groups on your left and right, fire off a Howl of Terror (if you have it on instant cast) once you've got a group behind you, fall off the ledge and head right. You'll come across a narrow passage with a couple decent-sized rocks against the right wall in the center of the passage; try to die as close to those rocks as you can. Once you're dead, release, and [b]don't resurrect at the graveyard.[/b] Run back to your corpse in the cave, and try to resurrect by that rock, preferably closer to the entrance of the cave, and hug the wall. Check ahead of you to make sure you won't aggro the knoll that's standing farther back in the passage when you resurrect. Now, there's a gnoll that patrols the ledge immediately above the rocks I'm speaking of. If you keep an eye on him, you can resurrect just as he's walking away and you'll have plenty of time for a Voidwalker before you make your second zerg rush. Not at all necessary to summon a Voidwalker here; I didn't use one for the entire run. Just make sure he's far enough down his partol that you don't aggro him when you resurrect, or it will screw up your second rushS bigtime. Once you've resurrected, catch your breath and rush straight down the passage, and take a hard right. You'll see the banner in the back on the passage, on an island in the middle of a frozen pond. The gnolls will likely kill you before you get there, so just die close enough that you can resurrect on top of the banner. Die again, and make one last corpse run, making sure your mass CC is completely cooled down. As soon as you resurrect, gather up the five gnolls in the area of the banner (1 on the island, and 4 around it), try to get these as close to the center island as you can, and fire your CC. At my level, Howl of Terror lasts for 8 seconds; I was able to loot the banner in what appeared to be 6 seconds. So, I had about enough time to fire the CC, jump on the island and loot. So, even with lower-rank Howl of Terror, you should be able to take the banner with just barely enough time to spare. Just be careful not to do this too close to any of the groups beyond the icy pond, or you risk grabbing an add and spoiling the attempt. So, assuming you don't mess up, you can easily get this banner in 3 deaths, assuming you let the gnolls kill you the last time rather than escaping. Try to do this as early and as quickly as you can; if you Allies capture your graveyards in the south and your team is already up north, you could end up running the length of the instance back to your corpse in the cave. I attempted this a few times and didn't even have a change to finish my attempt simply due to the fact that the game ended too quickly. It may take a few instances before you get the cave down, but once you do, you should have no trouble. Good luck getting your Insignia!

Progress: You've come back with news from the front, <name>?
Comment1: Not much you can really say about this quest, it's pretty much point blank. However, I would highly recommend, depending on your group makeup as well as whether or not you are a preformed or not, putting a few on defense (Hunters and Rogues) and have your tanks and healers and CC on Offense. SOmetimes your defense can stop the carrier if he is alone, otherwise they are there to slow them down and announce to the raid the direction the flag is going in order for your offense to get the flag back once the opponents flag is safely at home base. Good hiding spots are in abundance, just ensure you rotate these places to throw off potential onslaughts. And whether you agree or not, Free Action potions, health potions, Mana potions and even the occassional Swiftness potion are highly recommended in order to gain advantage.
Comment2: The main problem is that the horde rarely show up alone. Most games I'm in see the main forces of both armies just rush by one another. One or two or even three defenders isn't going to survive fighting the whole team. Mostly we get steam-rolled over before we can get a warning into /bg.
Comment3: half the team controls mid field. The other half goes for the flag. Once the flag team comes to mid field, move as a team to intercept the other team and return your flag. This works well if the other team is a pug. One big problem with WSG is gear. The better your gear, the better your advantage is over the other team. And healers, CC and pallis. Just my 2cents
Comment4: I agree, but it is always good to leave a few behind on D in the beginning. Why? Because regardless of whether or not they send in their whole force, the rezzers can get to the main group within seconds to help get the opponents flag BACK across the field. It's usually about 70% of the time they all go Offense and the other 30% they leave a few behind as well. It's trial and error, there are several strategies for any of the situations. The big thing is trying to get a PuG team to not stay midfield farming honor kills and get them to participate in running the flag, which has always been the problem with PuG groups. Preformeds are easier, you are in vent usually and everyone knows their job. But yes, you are correct for most games. Having someone in the Flagroom calling out the direction the flag is going makes it easier to get it back though.
Comment5: As far as the gear, yes, it does play a bit of a factor, however, I watched a preformed team in greens steamroll a PuG in Full T2. Gear doesn't make the player, the player makes the gear)

Comment1: Few things: First, I found this to be a very helpful website: http://tkasomething.com/avatarfaq.php Second, watch those videos. They help so much more than a picture or text ever could. In doing these demons, be prepared to spend ALOT of time and a good deal of gold if you're not an alchemist. Shadow protection potions go for 20g per stack on my server, and you'll use three in the last fight. Also, be prepared to die alot. It happens, don't get fustrated. But one of the bigger needs for every fight is [b] MANA POTIONS [/b]. I picked up alchemy for this reason, and made stacks and stacks of the level 25 potions. Obviously it wasnt as effective as the major mana pots, and I got pretty low in mana after every fight, but I again, wasnt feeling like supporting a fairly inflated alchemy market. I usually popped a 25 mana pot at 75% and it restored me to about full, and had one or two more in the fights. [ul] [li] You'll spend a bunch of attempts on it. For the first boss (Doombringer in WS), you could take off your armor completely if you want. This boss is easy kiting (even though i'll take a few tries to get used to it.) You dont need a party or someone to clear the area on their mount, either, you can just clear a path of hostile units, [i]fight a demon on the road&nbsp [/i] (which I did alot. It made it so much easier, and demons would pretty much destroy any moron who tried to disrupt the fighting) [/li] [/ul]
Comment2: I found this to be very helpful for the WS demon and a new Strat for the Burning Steppes demon. If you do this Quest post BC. the winterspring Demon you do not have to even Talk to him, Just Stand on the rocks at 58,20 Wait for him with Cheetah on, and the Area clear, as you see him get close(max range) just hit Serpent Sting and Start your run, Strafe shooting as you go, 1 rank 1 arcane shot at the end of the cooldown. hes easiest this way, and you can still loot the head of the demon. Burning Steppes demon has changed drastically from the way it once was. you can no longer use Scorpid sting, it has no effect on him anymore. they changed the way the Sting works, this will be an Endurance fight for any hunter. as you will burn Alot of mana laying traps and trying to keep him away, I suggest MM for Scattershot, and Aimed shot. All i did was this, speak with him to start the fight back away from him and lay a trap(freeze), doing the fight along the road is easiest get to max range, wait till you have about 12-14s on the trap cool down then Aimed shot him, use conccusive to slow/Stop him when your trap is up drop another freeze, rinse and repeat. it took me about 8 attempts this way and 2 unstable mana potions but i managed to do it. -- Dor
Comment3: By far the most difficult quest I have ever done. Some quick tips are: Be dueling a warlock that you trust immensely while fighting Solenor, if you can keep him wing clipped, have aspect of the cheetah up at all times, you don't have to kill beetles. The reasoning for the warlock is for Curse of Recklessness (no fearing from Solenor). Simone's pet doesn't need to be killed, but you need to loot her head before he kills you. For Klinfran, if you are specced for Scatter Shot, you can kite to different ends of the Burning Steppes then use Scatter Shot and go the other way. He is leashed to only Burning Steppes, so no Redridge/BRM.
Comment4: Solenor - A nice little tip for Solenor is when he starts off, drop a explosive trap and have him run into that. Then wing clip him and bolt outta there. The trap should to AoE damage to everything around him, and if you have curse of Recklessness on you, you shouldnt need to worry about the fears, so for the time the explosive trap lasts, you should have no problem with the bugs either. Just unload into him for when you can, but be sure you have a few mana pots on you and a shadow protection pot on you to keep the damage off you. Once the bugs start poping, and your trap wears off, when he's wing cliped git up volley rank 1 when you have all the bugs in a group. this should finish off the little suckers with use of the least mana as possible. This guy was the biggest pain for me personally, but that really just depends on what you're good at. Artorius - The main problem you WILL run into here, is getting around corners, and mana. So, when you start a turn, any turn at all, be sure to hit him in the face with a concussive shot, but dont get too far ahead of him in the process. Also, keep rank 1 arcane shot out like Kaenos said, and hit him with that every now and then between serpent stings to stay on his aggro list. I only shot him with the sting once every 3-5 seconds, because if you spam him, it will only stack up to 5 times, and your just wasting mana. The main thing to remember here besides the wait time on serpent sting is that rank 9 serpent sting DOESN'T work. One of my guildmates found this out the hard way, and only did minimal damage to him. This may have been updated in 2.0.1, but to the best of my knowledge, stick to sting rank 8. Simone - Basically easy to kill, i got her pet down first, and the killed her, but as long as you have nature protection pots and some mana pots on you just in case, you should be able to kite her around, even without killing her pet if you want to. Having another hunter follow you around with aspect of nature on is really good, because that allows you to keep aspect of the hawk on, which can really add to your DPS. Klinfran - Best thing to use here is rank one for wing clip. It gets the job done without wasting mana. The strat here can really be based on your weapon speed. Since each weapon has a specific attack speed (2.4s or whatever) once you scorpid sting him, you run up and attack him for 10 seconds. Your weapon can help time this, because if you have a 2.0 second attack speed, just hit him 5 times, wing clip and start running away. Try not to use raptor strike, because this fight is gonna be the longest one, and you will need the mana. When the fight starts off, hit him with concussive shot, frost trap, whatever you got to slow him down, and once he enrages hit him with scorpid. Then, start the attack cycle of running up, hitting him so many times, wing clip, run away, wait for enrage, and hit him with scorpid sting again. From there rince and repeat for roughly 7-10 minutes. Keep some mana pots with you for this fight specifically, and be sure to have a tuber or two for some health incase you slip up and he nails you once or twice. when you get far enough away from him after wing clipping him, you can hit him with an auto shot or two to add to some damage, but never try to aimed shot him. Also, don't use counterattack if it comes up. Imp wingclip can be helpful, but keep in mind you need to wait 10 seconds after you wing clip him for the enrage to come back up, and if you counterattack him, hes only stuck in place for 4 seconds, so he will be charging at you for 6 seconds, until he enrages, which most likely means hes gonna enrage within your minimum range. The most useful thing to use if this does happen though is scatter shot, then get away from him and hit him with a scorpid sting. You might get hit once or twice, but you should be able to survive 2-3 hits, and then just pick up where you left off and learn from your mistakes.
Comment5: You cannot have any sort of help at all. If a player besides yourself either buffs, heals, or attacks while your in combat with the demon he will call you a coward and despawn. Comment2: Few pointers for the new pet owners :) Do the taming quests before training. You do not have to use all 3 rods, one sucessful tame and if you open your quest window you will see the completed notation, travel back you your npc and get the next quest. For the elves the 3 tames were spider, bird and cat. The type of spider you need can be found right outside of Dolnaar, the cat and bird however are found closer to the gates of Darnassus, I found mine right outside the gates. Make sure there are no 'helpful' people around. Do not move while you are taming or attack in any way. Choose your pet based on what is available to you by way of food for your pet, nothing is worse then a pet you can't find food for in your zone. Birds only want fresh meat, cats however will eat meat and fish. You will need to feed your pet immediatly,until you have a green smiley face or he will have a mind all his own. Have his food in your inventory and ready for him immediatly after you tame him. FYI they will not thank you for offering them bean soup :P Keep them fed up to the green smiley face level and they will quickly gain loyalty and be the companion you hoped for. And yes, they do level up with you, you do not have to throw away pets every time your level goes up. Keep in mind the type pets that at one time delivered the worst butt whopping to you, and it's a good bet you'll get a nice pet out of one. FYI for some reason the cats in the beginning do not hold aggro as well as say a bird or bear, I'd say you can consider your kitty more a rouge then a tank for you, so choose based on what you want your pet to be able to do. Good luck :) and Chester the kitty and I wish you happy hunting :)

Progress: I see wisdom in your eyes, <name>. Has your hunt ended?
Comment1: When it comes to your reward choices there are a couple of things to consider. In my opinion, the Hunting Spear is probably the least useful of the three items. Weapons themselves will eventually become outdated, to begin with, as people level up, especially with the upcoming expansion. Also, if one truly wants a decent spear, many hunters go and get the Ice Barbed Spear (https://classicdb.ch/?item=19106) which is a reward if you win ONE battle in Alterac Valley. This spear has better overall stats, in my opinion, than the Hunting Spear, as it has an abundance of agility as well as stamina. This brings it down to the last two items. Now if you are a Marks or Surv hunter, the Devilsaur Eye is clearly the best choice for you. However, I'm not certain if there are other trinkets more useful than this for Marks/Surv hunters, so please make a comment if you believe there is. Being a BM hunter, I instinctively went for the Devilsaur Tooth. I have no doubt in my mind that this trinket is one of the best for hunters with this spec. It's highly useful for opening attacks, especially if one has a cat. A cat put into Prowl, with the Devilsaur Tooth buff, as well as triggering Bestial Wrath the moment before it reaches the intended target means a strong critical opening attack that will proc Frenzy instantly. This will become especially useful when the expansion pack is released. One of the new BM abilities is Ferocious Inspiration. It means that when your pet scores a critical hit, all party members have their damage output increased by 1-3% for 10 seconds.
Comment2: For levels 50-55 these are actually quite nice rewards. The polearm is very nice, does good damage, restores mana, and adds +1% crit. I myself use 2 Dawns Edges which give me +2% crit, so this one is useless for hunters that have those. The Tooth is nice. But i see little use for it. A BM hunter will most likely have the +15% extra crit chance for the pet making it a 20% crit chance machine. Using this trinket might tell it to crit when your beast was already about to crit. Comment1: ***DISCLAIMER*** This information may change at one point, this is current as of the final beta. The end reward for this is a handful of Beast abilities which personify Hunter: Tame, Dismiss, Call, Train, and Feed Beast. The quest itself can be received in Razor Hill for the Horde at level 10. [b]First Quest[/b] The hunter trainer in Razor Hill gives you a special item and commands you to find and charm a specific creature with it (my beast was Dire Mottled Boar). The item has 3 charges which charm only that specific creature for 10 minutes. These beasts are found just outside of Razor Hill, and you must hold their attention for the entire charming process or it will break (you will be taking damage. There's no escaping it, but if someone pulls aggro away from you, it will break the spell). Once you have the beast controlled, you can either hunt for a short time, or simply return to the trainer for a xp boost and the second part of the quest. [b]Second Quest[/b] The difference between this quest and the first is simply in the choice of beasts. As with the first quest, you are given an item with 3 charges that can charm a specific mob type for 10 minutes, and told to use it. My target for this second time was a Surf Crawler (NOT a Pygmy Surf Crawler, both types can be found east of Sen'jin). As with the first part, once you have successfully charmed a crawler you can return to the trainer for an xp boost and the continuance of the quest. [b]Third Quest[/b] You are, for the last time, given a charm item for a third specific mob. For this portion, I was given the target of an Armored Scorpid, which can be found near Razor Hill. Steps are the same as the first two quests, repeat them and return to razor hill. Completion of this quest gives you the Tame Beast command, as well as Call and Dismiss. You are then sent to Hunter's Hall in Orgrimmar to learn how to train a beast (do note, there are several Raptor-type monsters en route to the city which make decent pets) [b]Final Quest[/b] The easiest of the four, you are sent to Hunter's Hall (Valley of Bravery, west of the Colliseum, ask any Grunt for the hunter class trainer and it will be marked). All you need to do is speak to the trainers there and you will be granted the Feed and Train Pet abilities - feeding your pet raises its happiness...an Unhappy pet does 75% of its normal damage, and steadily loses Loyalty points. Unhappy pets can turn on you if they are low enough loyalty level. Content pets get no Loyalty Point addition or subtraction, but do 100% of their normal damage. Happy pets do 125% of their normal damage, and their loyalty increases whily happy. Each pet has different food types they prefer, so experiment. Train Pet uses points that accumulate as you and your pet fight to buy abilities...your pet starts with the ability to learn 2 talents, Growl and Growl 2 (1 and 5 points respectively, Growl 2 requires the pet to reach level 10, which will happen as you xp). This ability increases the threat perception of your pet, allowing it to hold hate from a mob even when you do large amounts of damage (at level 2, growl can often hold aggro regardless of your damage). Once you receive these abilities, and another xp bonus, the quest ends and you are given full access to taming.

Comment1: Few pointers for the new pet owners :) Do the taming quests before training. You do not have to use all 3 rods, one sucessful tame and if you open your quest window you will see the completed notation, travel back you your npc and get the next quest. For the elves the 3 tames were spider, bird and cat. The type of spider you need can be found right outside of Dolnaar, the cat and bird however are found closer to the gates of Darnassus, I found mine right outside the gates. Choose your pet based on what is available to you by way of food for your pet, nothing is worse then a pet you can't find food for in your zone. Keep in mind the type pets that at one time delivered the worst butt whopping to you, and it's a good bet you'll get a nice pet out of one. FYI for some reason the cats in the beginning do not hold aggro as well as say a bird or bear, I'd say you can consider your kitty more a rouge then a tank for you, so choose based on what you want your pet to be able to do. Comment1: How to solo: Stay on the steps (top of the steps is fine) and right click on the scroll. One ghost will spawn closer to you than the others. Do your frost nova so you ONLY get one in the trap. Then run, the other 3 will follow you a very short way, then they will disappear. Capture it in the containment coffer (by right clicking on the box in your stash), it will suck the spirit into the coffer, and you right click once more on the coffer on the floor. Repeat twice more. Pretty easy once you get the hang of it. Just make sure you only trap one.

Inch closer to where Algernon (the shopkeeper) is standing, casting Arcane Explosion as you go. Eventually you will catch one of the Rift Spawns in the AOE, it'll aggro. Just do the standard mage thing - Fire Blast, Frost Nova, Ice Bolt, Fireball, Fire Blast again - quite easy when it's alone. Once it's stunned, throw down a coffer and you're 1/3. Rinse and repeat. (If you're unlucky and your AOE hits more elementals than you can handle, just drop a Frost Nova and run away. Or proceed to use one of the strategies outlined above.)

Comment4: I was confused by this chain and the one that leads to 'Celestial Power', so I posted here and under that quest to differentiate which quests go with which chain. First, there's a quest that leads you to Tabetha in Dustwallow Marsh - it starts with the mage trainer in Ogrimmar for Horde, and is just like the Alliance-side 'Journey to the Marsh' listed here. Tabetha is on an island southeast of Brackenwall Village in Dustwallow, almost to the coastline. For Alliance, Tabetha is almost due west of the docks in Theramore, but it's tough to get to her from the bay because of the low- to mid-40's mobs in the water. It's easier to go up and around (partway on the road) because the mobs are lower level (high 30's). Tabetha's hut is due north of the 'EM' in Stonemaul Ruins on the Dustwallow map. 2. Tabetha gives you 'Hidden Secrets' quest to go get a book by talking to Magus Tirth at the racetrack in 1000 Needles Shimmering Flats. 3. Tirth gives you 'Get the Scoop' quest to talk to his 'assistant', Plucky Johnston, who is a chicken. As posted here in that thread, /beckon the chicken and he will become a human, talk to you and send you back to Tirth. Comment4: A couple of points that I don't think were very clear from everything above.&nbsp But great information from everyone... 1. AoE spells will not be reflected back at you, but the EFFECTS (stuns, slows) that proc off those spells might be reflected.&nbsp So if I hit him with a Flamestrike, I won't take any damage because I'm not in the AoE, but I MIGHT be stunned if I have that Talent and it procs.&nbsp Same with Blizzard and slowing. That being said, I've never seen him reflect Frost Nova. 2. Reflection happens about 50% of the time, but only on aimed spells.&nbsp CoC can't be reflected, however the damage from Blastwave CAN.&nbsp These are just my observations, feel free to contradict me, but I have combat logs to back this up. 3. The Guardians that splinter from the Sentinel ALSO have the spell reflection property.&nbsp They are level 35, non-elite, and go down pretty quickly. The Obsidian Sentinel is lvl 42 Elite. 4. Sometimes when you leave the instance and return, the Sentinel and his splinter will not have gone back, they will be right there.&nbsp Make sure you go in with Mana shield up, and Frost Nova ready. 5. THE MOST IMPORTANT PART After he splinters about 4 times, and you have done the run in, run out to heal and mana up, you will now have the long fight in front of you.&nbsp If you have to leave at this point of the fight, you will be resetting all the damage you have done. With him splintered so many times, he is very small, and does very little damage. You can stand there with mana shield up, have him hitting you constantly, and your mana regen will be greater than the damage he does to your shield.&nbsp You can sit there and just regen mana if you don't want to produce a new splinter, and just refresh your mana shield every 60 seconds. Otherwise, you want to be wanding him the whole time until he produces a new splinter.&nbsp At which time, Frost Nova, back off, Flamestrike, CoC, then either Blastwave or Blizzard or wand until the splinter dies.&nbsp Then go back to mana shield and wanding the Obsidian Sentinel while your mana regens.&nbsp If you need health, next time your Frost Nova is ready nova the Obsidian Sentinel, back off and bandage. During this fight, his new splinters will NOT reduce the Obsidian Sentinels health any more.&nbsp Once he gets to a certain size he just won't get any smaller or weaker. GREAT BUFFS TO HAVE Mighty Trolls' Blood potion, regens health. Scroll of Spirit to increase your mana regen. Any stamina buff, any armour buff. Keep Ice armour up. NOTES: When he is splintered down as far as he will go (after about 4 splinters) he has about 8500hp. If you have a wand that is doing on average 50 per hit (he does resist a fair number of hits), and let's say a 2.0 speed, it will take you about 6 minutes of uninterrupted wanding to take him down.&nbsp However, it IS interrupted each time there is a splinter, so you have closer to 10-15 minutes of just you and the Sentinel to look forward to. And if you run low on health and have to leave the instance, he will heal up, and you will have to do it ALL over again.&nbsp Once you know he's not getting any smaller, you HAVE to stay the whole fight, dealing with the splinters as they appear. As mages we're used to very quick, high-DPS-burst- damage kinds of fights. Break that habit quickly, it will get you killed in this fight...and it's a long run from the GY. Oh, and the last part of the quest where you fight the mana surges is a piece of cake.&nbsp Just stand on the pier and pull them one by one.&nbsp They're ranged, but don't do too much damage.&nbsp Just have Dampen Magic up, and if you need to, stop and drink and eat.&nbsp You've got plenty of time.
Comment5: I have always run into problems with finding Uldaman groups in general. When I did find a group that wanted to do it, they never wanted to swing by the area with the obsidian sentinel so I had pretty much given up on this quest. I am now a level 49 frost mage, and decided to try to solo it. I followed the comments on this page and mixed some of the suggestions. Here's how I did it. (you can get all of this from above - I'm just being very specific.) 1. Make sure you have your mana gem ready to go. 2. Start off by putting up mana shield. (I also used ice barrier to save mana it worked very well for me) 3. Drink up to full mana. 4. Frost nova the sentinel. 5. Start wanding him. Continue until your shield breaks from his damage. Cast mana shield again and keep wanding. 6. Continue to frost nova whenever the cooldown is ready. 7. When he splinters and gets a guardian, leave the instance. 8. Food and drink up outside. 9. Go back in - the sentinel and his buddy will be standing in the original place. 10. Repeat the same process, but wand the buddy first. 11. Once the buddy is dead, you can leave the instance again if necesssary to heal, but I never had to. 12. Keep repeating this, and you'll eventually end up with a dead sentinel. :) I only used one superior healing potion, and I didn't really even have to I was just doing it to be safe. Good luck.

I also created a Mana Jade. I then activated the quest. While Tabitha was walking outside, I cast Mana Shield on myself. If you build up enough of a lead, he won't be able to hit you. When Frost Nova is ready, use it again and do another Fireball/Fireblast combo. Just keep repeating this and he should go down. I beat him with 50 health and 30 mana left, and about 25 seconds on the clock.

Name: Blessed Arcanite Barding

Progress: <name>, you're back! Were you able to successfully deal with Merideth Carlson and Tendris Warpwood? Honestly, I'm not sure which one is a greater threat at times...
Comment1: The paladin epic mount quest in a nutshell: 1: 150 gold to get censor for exorcising spirits in Terrordale. You get this from the priest trainer in Ironforge in the Mystic Ward. 1a: Exorcise 25 spirits in Terrordale. There are green glowing circles around in the ruins of Terrordale (near the Terrorweb Tunnel exit). Use the censor within these circles and 1-3 spirits will spawn. Simply kill them until you have killed 25 of them. The green circles spawn relatively fast. I soloed this portion and took approximately 30 minutes. 2: 150 gold, 40 Runecloth, 10 Arthas' Tears, 6 Arcanite Bars and 5 Stratholme Holy Waters. Turn all this into Grimand Elmore who is in Stormwind's Dwarven District. He is located in the far SW corner. He will walk to the forge in the center of the Dwarven District and create the barding for you. After this he will run back to his normal standing spot where you can then speak to him again to get the Barding. 3. 50 gold and 20 Enriched Manna Biscuits. Travel to Southshore and speak with Merideth Carlson the Horse Breeder in the stables. She will give you Manna-Enriched Horse Feed. I would personally suggest actually reading this quest because it gave me a chuckle. 4. Now you need to go to Dire Maul West to get the barding blessed. This part is easy and quick. Make sure you have the barding and Manna-Enriched Horse Feed on you and someone with the crescent key with you. Go into Dire Maul West and simply run past all the mobs. We did this with a level 55 in the group without grabbing agro. We ran around the right. Tendris Warpwood is in a room opposite of the park from where you enter the instance. When you get to the other side of the park, go down the long ramp to his room. He's easy to kill. I tried to solo him for fun just to see if it's possible for a paladin with the key to do this alone, and I personally was not able to. I simply didn't have the DPS to take him down fast enough. I was using Seal of Command with Seal of Wisdom released on him for mana regen. If any paladin is successful in actually soloing him, please let me know how you did it because I wouldn't mind being able to farm him for my Foror's. :) Anyway, once he's dead, an Ancient Equine Spirit appears (a ghost horse) and will start walking or running around. It took me a second to catch him, but once you do, you complete the quest and get the Blessed Barding. 5. Now for this part you will need to talk to Lord Grayson (the Paladin trainer taking you through this line) with a Pristine Black Diamond and an Azerothian Diamond to get The Divination Scryer. Now you're ready for the last part of the quest a run into Scholomance. 6. Once in Scholomance you want to go down to Rattlegore's room. Kill Rattlegore and clear the room. Place the Scryer in the middle of the room and spirits will appear in different locations. The names will be Banality, Malice, Corrupted and Shadow. You must use the Seals of Wisdom, Justice, Righteousness and Light respectively. When you release the seal you will do damage and stun in an approximately 10 yard radius. It is important for your group to stay close together and is extremely helpful to have two or more Paladins with improved Judgment. You will get several waves of each type of spirit and they will appear in different areas around the room. After taking out so many of a certain wave, an Aspect (i.e. Aspect of Banality) will spawn. That is the 'mini-boss' of that wave and the next wave will spawn after you kill him. There will be times when you may stop and eat or drink while fighting these waves. I strongly suggest you do that when possible. The Corrupted spirits are scary because they came in one wave and there was something like 10 of them. So be extra prepared for them. Once you take care of all the waves, the Death Knight Darkreaver spawns. He is a 62 elite, but is easy to kill. He does mind control and I think fear, which are the only notable abilities that he used while we fought him. Once you kill him, you loot the Charger's Lost Soul from his corpse. There will also appear a paladin epic mount in ghost form. Use the Charger's Lost Soul in your backpack to redeem it. At that time, you'll be able to complete the quest by talking to the epic mount ghost. So here's the total list of cash and items required for the Paladin Charger Mount: 350 gold 10 Arthas' Tears (Herbalism) 6 Arcanite Bars (Mining/Alchemy) 40 Runecloth 5 Stratholme Holy Waters (Boxes in Stratholme) 20 Enriched Manna Biscuits (Must be friendly with Argent Dawn to purchase) Here's a quick guide: 150 gold, 10 Arthas' tears, 6 Arcanite, 40 runecloth and 5 strat holy waters for the barding to Grimand in SW's Dwarven district. 150 gold to priest trainer in IF for censor. Go kill 25 spirits in Terrordale, using the censor to summon them. Take 20 Enriched Manna Biscuits and 50 gold to Merideth Carlson in SS to get Manna-Enriched Horse Feed. Run DMW to kill Tendris Warpwood to get the barding blessed. Bring an Azerothian Diamond and a Pristine Black Diamond to Grayson in SW for the Scryer. Go to scholo's ossuary and summon the Darkreaver to get the charger's redeemed soul. Welcome to epic mount land. :) Baradier 60 Paladin Thunderhorn

Comment3: Completed this quest today as a lvl 61 protection pala, with help from a lvl 70 fury warrior. The final stage was relatively simple, as long as you run for a corner after placing the Scryer. From here you won't pull the entire room of ghosts at once, and can instead fight smaller groups of them using the correct judgement every time it's available. Also, be aware that simply attacking the ghosts with the correct seal applied appears to have a small chance to proc the AoE effect as well so don't leave everything to the people helping you. The effect cannot be refreshed though, so wait until it wears off before judging your seal if you get a proc from normal hits. Each wave of ghosts is followed by an Aspect, which is a larger and significantly tougher single ghost with similar vulnerabilities and attacks to its counterparts. The death of the Aspect of Shadow triggers Darkreaver to spawn, and both the Aspect and Darkreaver himself wil aggro on spawning no matter where you try to hide in the room. Because of this, your rest stop before Darkreaver should be taken before you pull the last of the regular Shadowed ghosts as once you spawn the Aspect you're in combat until Darkreaver is dead. Be ready to bubble if Darkreaver uses his mind control ability successsfuly, you don't want to get killed by accidental (or, of course, purposeful - some people love to take those kind of opportunities ;)) whirlwinds, cleaves and so on or get beaten down by a controlled part member. My level 70 counterpart resisted it once, and I bubbled out when he used it on me. Darkreaver will also use Blessing of Protection on himself just before he dies in true paladin style, but he won't heal himself so all you have to worry about is living a little longer. This shouldn't be too taxing, as Darkreaver is a bit of a pansy as far as bosses go.

Comment1: Was first to finish it on Al'Akir and I will try to list the tips here: [b]Best combo[/b] The best combination for completing this quest is: 4 Paladins, 1 Priest (harder to get to event, but easier to complete) 3 Paladins, 1 Mage, 1 Priest (easier to get to event, but harder to complete) [i]Don't bring warriors for the sake of 'warrior holds aggro from mage' crap or 'rogues have very good dmg output' crap[/i] You need good Paladins for this quest, as unleashing correct seals will do Area Effect damage to all ghosts withing 10 yards[/i] [b]You need highest ranks in following Seals:[/b] [ul] [li]Seal of Wisdom (rank 3) -> Banality [/li] [li]Seal of Justice (rank 1) -> Malicious [/li] [li]Seal of Righteousness (rank 8) -> Corrupted [/li] [li]Seal of Light (rank 4) -> Shadowed [/li] [/ul] [b]Don't spam Judgements[/b] Wait for stun effect fade from ghosts between unleashing next Judgement (takes about 4 seconds). [b]Stay in North-East corner until boss comes[/b] Stay in North-East corner until boss comes and refresh as much as possible (drink mana potions, heal, resurrect, buff). Comment2: Just did it a second time last night, so have done it successfully with both 3 pallies, warlock, priest as well as 4 pallies and a priest. Followed the advice here to great effect, but I'll write-up everything we did in case it helps even if there's some repetition. [b]Getting to the event:[/b] [ul] [li]Big trouble we had with four pallies and priest was the room with the summoners, as the summoner would run off and get to close to the next group and then summon skeletons til we wiped, which happened a few times. Without a mage for counterspell or shadow priest for silence or whatever, make good use of your hammers of justice and if the next group gets pulled, concentrate on at least taking down the original summoner before wiping/divine interventioning. Might be slow going, but with a bit of stubborness you'll get through. [/li] [li]Rest is fairly simple. Without a warlock/mage, the whelp room can be cleared by pulling them out into the next room and having one pally tank the Handler while the rest take a whelp or two each. Consecrating pulls too much damage on one person really. [/li] [li]Risen constructs and Rattlegore, easier now post patch, should be able to pull them all alone without trouble with a bit of patience. One pally tanks with a shield, seal of fury, judged fury and consecration while being healed by the priest and the rest just do damage.[/li] [/ul] [b]Before the event:[/b] [ul] [li]We were all positioned in the SW corner both times, which worked fine. When the third wave happens, some spawn on top of you here, so be ready. [/li] [li]Judgement order is of course Wisdom, Justice, Righteousness, Light. It's a good idea to have all the pallies arrange them in that order on their action bar to keep the order easy to remember and quick to access. [/li] [li]Make sure everyone has health pots, mana pots, bandages etc if possible and the like, always good to have in reserve if things are getting cut close. Make sure all the pallies have a Symbol of Divinity, and is up to speed on how Divine Intervention works too. Using this, I was able to stop a wipe on the fourth wave as the priest was safely tucked away in the corner (course, it was my pull that nearly wiped us, but anyway...). [/li] [li]Pallies shouldn't be doing anything but applying the seal, judging it when it's their turn, and meleeing. As long as the spirits are kept stunned, they're not a problem. Things like exorcism are a waste of mana. After judging, it's good to reapply the seal immediately to have it ready and also get its benefit in the fights, especially on the last wave. [/li] [li]Keep devotion, concentration and shadow resistance auras on.[/li] [/ul] [b]The waves of spirits[/b] [ul] [li]In general, stay hidden in your corner (priest at the back), all bunched together and deal with the spirits that are immediately on you each wave. Pallies should have an order established for the judgements so one is in effect all the time on the spirits. Once a particular fight is done, take the time to drink a bit and see if any more spawn in aggro range. After a while, if none are forthcoming, have someone run out and pull some of the far off ones with an exorcism. [/li] [li]The aspect is slightly bigger than the other ones, watch out for when he appears. Some of the time, he doesn't aggro immediately, letting you shackle at your leisure while finishing off groups. If he gets to close to your corner, might be an idea to leave him shackled there then run out and finish the others before coming back to him. [/li] [li]First wave: Easy. Non-elites and gives everyone a chance to practice their judgements. Basically the warm-up round. [/li] [li]Second wave: Little tougher. Elites this time, but pretty much the same as before. Only thing to watch out for is that they look similar enough to the first wave to be confused for them, make sure everyone knows to switch seals for judging. [/li] [li]Third wave: Harder now, big swarms. In the SW corner some spawn directly on top of you, be ready for them. Best to wait and see what heads towards you and drink up when you can. [/li] [li]Fourth wave: The hardest part really. Casters, so they can damage you from a distance. After the initial ones, when you're getting ready to pull the next batch yourself, there's one that likes to run out to the west side on its own that looks like a tempting pull. This is the one I nearly wiped our group on, because he's linked to some others and they're then split apart when they attack. Bite the bullet, and pull a central one when they're collected together, so you can use the judgement stuns to your advantage again. And, of course, make sure the aspect is shackled while everyone gets their health and mana back up for the Deathknight fight. You'll need it.[/li] [/ul] [b]The Deathknight:[/b] [ul] [li]It's debatable whether he's hard or easy to take down, but one thing he certainly is is tough. He can really take a beating and also pack a respectable punch when he wants to, a string of hard hits can take a fair chunk off anyone's health. [/li] [li]The thing to watch out for on him is that it's going to be a long fight, you'll win by outlasting him and eventually grinding him down. Don't blow your mana too early, you'll need it for the long haul on this guy. Happily, beyond the endurance game, he isn't too bad really. Just stick it out and don't despair if his health doesn't seem to be going down all that fast. [/li] [li]Put away the two-handers and leave the consecration button alone, you'll want a couple of pallies or more with shields on using seal/judgement of wisdom/light to keep their health and mana topped up for heals. It might be an idea to have someone tank him as before, though this may be troublesome if the designated tank gets possessed. [/li] [li]Keep blessing of wisdom and salvation on the priest. [/li] [li]His possession trick kind of messed me over in terms of leaving me somewhat disorientated. Still, pallies are never known for the dps at the best of times, so with my one-hander and shield on I was more of annoyance than a threat when I turned on a team-mate, and at least he was nice enough to keep me healed. Drained all my mana though. :\ [/li] [li]Try not to die, you only get one shot at this. Keep your health fairly well topped up at all times and if you're in trouble pop a potion or shield and bandage. Blessing of Protection the priest if he's in trouble, if he runs out of mana too he may need to take a sit down break to regenerate some. Have your Lay on Hands button within easy reach. Again, use seal of wisdom to claw back some mana when you need it.[/li] [/ul] [b]Post-fight[/b] [ul] [li]Revel in the glory of victory a while, you earned it. You complete the quest by looting the charger's soul from the deathknight's corpse, then running over to the placed scryer and using it in your inventory (right-clicking) to redeem it. Then run over to the ghost horse and complete the quest. After doing this, you should have a new spell in the holy section of your spellbook, 'Summon Charger', next to the old 'Summon Warhorse' one and with a similar looking but yellow in colour logo now post-patch. This is what to look for to know everything has been completed as it should have been and to ensure you've got your shiny new mount. Getting caught up in the excitement of getting your mount makes it easy to get confused if you try and rush this part without reading everything carefully of course. :)[/li] [/ul]

Comment4: The paladin epic mount quest in a nutshell: 1: 150 gold to get censor for exorcising spirits in Terrordale. There are green glowing circles around in the ruins of Terrordale (near the Terrorweb Tunnel exit). Use the censor within these circles and 1-3 spirits will spawn. Simply kill them until you have killed 25 of them. The green circles spawn relatively fast. I soloed this portion and took approximately 30 minutes. 2: 150 gold, 40 Runecloth, 10 Arthas' Tears, 6 Arcanite Bars and 5 Stratholme Holy Waters. Turn all this into Grimand Elmore who is in Stormwind's Dwarven District. He is located in the far SW corner. Comment5: I now know why some people say the quest is a cakewalk and others say it is not do-able. Both are correct. The quest is buggy! I have experienced both so I know. You will either complete this without trouble or fail miserably. Please do not flame me with corrections. If you have something to add to help great! Please keep it constructive. I found the lack of advice/help on this quest frustrating and wish to make it easier for people who follow me. I will now recount the problem areas and how we overcame them. This quest is very do-able and you can have your mount on the first attempt if you follow the advice below. I am not saying this is the ONLY way to complete it. It is how we did and what I learned in the process I think can help others. [b]Composition of Party[/b] [b]Number of Paladins:[/b] Paladins are required to complete the end sequence. 3 is your sweet spot of balance between getting to room without trouble and ease of completing the end sequence. 4 makes the end sequence do-able even if they things go buggy on you. But with 4 Paladins, the trip to the room will be harder and longer (It is do-able). If you want to be sure you complete the quest, 4 Paladins would guarantee you complete the Judgements portion. You should have a priest. Not only do you get heals you get crowd control with shackle. This is invaluable in end sequence (see below). [b]Rest of Party:[/b] Slot 1: Paladin Slot 2: Paladin Slot 3: Paladin or Warrior or Rogue Slot 4: Paladin or Mage or Warlock Slot 5: Priest [b]Journey to the Rattlegore room[/b] There is nothing special to note here it’s just kind of slow. Take your time and you will get to the room. The only thing worth mentioning is the room with the whelps. They have a nasty damage over time that can easily kill you within 3 to 4 seconds if you do not cleanse. You will be spamming cleanse. Be ready for it or take the durability hit when you die. [b]Rattlegore room[/b] The risen constructs hit hard! No big deal but without a tank the healer has to be on it healing the Paladins. Some Paladins in my group had a shield and one-hander and two of us used two-handers. What worked best was alternating stuns and alternating tanking. Really the Risen constructs are just time consuming and no fun. You should pull them one at time into the hallway outside room to fight. The puller and the priest go to doorway together for the pull. There are a couple of them that are real close and unless you time it just right you will pull two. Better to shackle one and fight them one at a time. Rattlegore will come with a little buddy. Just shackle his buddy then finish Rattlegore alone then his buddy. The risen constructs are capable of killing the cloth wearer in one hit (I have seen it) so have priest in a safe place and have a good mage not pull agro. [b]Judgement Sequence[/b] Now that the Rattlegore room completely empty of any mob. You can begin the end sequence “Judgements”. Everyone needs to stand in one corner (see diagram). You will enter the room and turn right. The party should stay in that corner the entire time. Some people suggested placing the Divination Scryer in the opposite corner. You can’t do that. It must be placed in the center. [b]Aura’s to use:[/b] devotion, shadow and concentration. If you don’t have three Paladin’s use devotion and concentration on the first three waves and switch to shadow and concentration on the fourth wave. The fourth wave are caster that do shadow damage. So make sure that the priest has given the party “Shadow Protection”. [b]Coordinate Paladin’s Judgments:[/b] You must have a good group of Paladin’s that are willing to work together. Our judgments do more damage than the mage can do and it has a good chance of stunning for 5 seconds. Work out a sequence of Paladin 1 judge wait 5 seconds Paladin 2 judge wait 5 seconds Paladin 3 judge and repeat. Most parties fail this quest for one of three reasons. (1) They panic and don’t coordinate their judgments or (2) They pull the entire third wave (3) They kill the fourth ghost sub-boss to soon (more on this in a minute). The order of judgments is as follows. [b]Wave one:[/b] Judge Seal of Wisdom [b]Wave two:[/b] Judge Seal of Justice [b]Wave three:[/b] Judge Seal of Righteousness [b]Wave four:[/b] Judge Seal of Light [b]Ghost Mini-boss:[/b] This is important. To get time to eat and drink between waves of ghosts, have your priest shackle each wave’s mini-boss. That is what triggers the next event. This is not true between the first three waves, but it might be good to practice because [i] when you kill the fourth wave mini-boss you will summon Death Knight Darkreaver![/i] If you have some ghosts left to kill and you are low on health/mana you could wipe with the Death Knight is summoned early. Others have. [b]What to do:[/b] Your party is at full health and in the correct corner (point x on map). You run to center of room and plant the Divination Scryer in center of room (point D on map) and run back to group. You will agro ghosts so when you get back to group the fight will already be started. The first wave is easy. Good chance to practice your judgments and loosen up. When a group that has been killed relax and wait for next group. You don’t need to pull. The second wave is a little harder but not hard. You will begin to use up some mana so be ready for third wave. Eat and drink. [b]Third Wave:[/b] You are all in the correct corner and the ghosts are not coming so its time to pull as everyone is buffed and has full health/mana. The ghosts to the left look like the perfect group to pull (there are only three of them) DON’T! This will bring all 9-11 ghosts. Instead go to the right and pull the ghost in position G on map. This will bring 6-7. No problem if judgments are timed. Then you will have ones and twos that come to you. [b]Fourth Wave:[/b] They will agro on their own so wait. Eat/drink. These are easier than the last wave. But be ready to shackle the mini-boss ghost. Before you release the mini-boss ghost kill all the ghosts [b](All!)[/b] Then regenerate your health and mana. You can’t eat/drink so just wait for it to regenerate. When you’re buffed and in good shape release the ghost mini-boss and kill him. Death Knight Darkreaver will be summoned immediately! No time to rest. Some tricks the Death Knight has is some sort of lay on hands to heal himself when he is low on health. The Death Knight Darkreaver will/can mind control one of your party. For us he MC’ed the mage who smited me and killed me instantly (I was low on health and in process of getting a heal). He is really pretty easy. But, if you kill the 4th mini-boss early you could have your hands full! [b]Darkreaver is dead now what?[/b] Loot “Charger's Lost Soul”. Every Paladin on the quest can loot it! All will complete their quest regardless of who used their scryer. You must go to the planted Divination Scryer and [i]right click on “Charger's Lost Soul”[/i]. It will turn into “Charger's Redeemed Soul” You have now completed your quest. Go to Charger’s ghost and turn in your quest. You now have your Epic Mount! Comment4: I cannot stress how important it is to tell your gruop, especially mage and priest to literary hug the wall. They should not move during the whole fight, because they risk pulling all aggro on themselves. Mobs that spawn have nasty agro range, so it is pretty much best if the whole gruop was as close to the wall as possible. Also, warn mage not to nuke when fresh mobs come - paladins must be the first to judge them, and mage will finnish them off once they're at low HP. This will ensure aggro is on paladins, not soft targets. [b]The fight[/b] One paladin should run to the middle of the room and plant the scryer on the floor, imediatelly running back to the corner where his gruop is. He will pull some mobs, but nothing too bad. Let paladins do their undead spells on them and judge once there's few of them in the range. Mage can finnish off with nukes once they're at low health. After each wave of mobs comes a mini boss. Sometimes it comes alone, other times he has 2 on his side. Your priest will identify the boss by its name: 'Aspect of ...' and shackle him at safe distance. It's very important to shackle the boss further away from the gruop because judged seal could wash over him too and break the schakle. Death of each mini boss triggers the next wave of mobs, and death of last mini boss summons the Death knight himself. Use that shackle time and regenerate - you can't drink in combat, but wait for your hp and mana to fill up over time. It is very good to get some scrolls with spirit for this occasion, also crystals from Un'goro pylon quest that increase spirit by 30 will be a nice touch since you'll regen significantly faster with +60 spirit.

This is the technique I used for this whole instance 1) Aggro 2 mobs 2) Run to exit of instance 3) Kill one mob 4) Exit instance 5) Heal and regen 6) re-enter instance 7) Kill second mob 8) Rinse and repeat! Once you�ve killed the Wolfguard and Worg in the room on the right, go up the stairs and use the above techniques to kill the rest of the mobs on the landings, just remember to run to the instance exit once you�ve aggro�d them. Ok, once you�ve turned left at the end of the hall and killed the mobs in that room, go down the stairs, into the jail room. Once the way is clear you�ll be tempted to run into the stables and grab the hammer, but once you enter the stables, another Haunted Servitor will jump from above and attack you, just run back up the stairs to the hallway and kill it�THEN go and grab the hammer! Comment2: [b]Shadowfang Keep Mini-FAQ:[/b] I solo'd this quest at lvl28 and I was far higher in level than I needed to be it was almost easy.&nbsp To solo this, with good equipment, I'm guessing lvl25-26, and it won't be too hard. You'll want to start off in Menethil Harbor, and take the long walk up past Dun Modr and through Thandol Span.&nbsp Cross Arathi Highlands and take a break in Refuge Point (/tloc 44,52) to link to the Gryphon Rider.&nbsp If you get killed you can just fly back here.&nbsp Proceed down the road, West to Thoradin's Wall.&nbsp There are NPC guards along most of this route so all you need to worry about is PvE for the most part.&nbsp Continue West to Southshore, where you can link another Gryphon Rider. From here out there's a lot of NPC guards so you're still going to be fairly protected, but the mobs that spawn around here are sometimes into lvl33 iirc so be [i]very[/i] cautious. Once you enter Silverpine Forest (West again from Southshore) the PvE is cake because the mobs are below lvl20 on average.&nbsp This is also Horde Territory, which isn't so bad considering most Horde in the area are around lvl20 and don't even have their PvP flags on so they won't bother you.&nbsp Continue West until you reach Pyrewood Village, a lvl18+ elite area for Horde which is useless unless you're dying to use a forge or anvil.&nbsp Really, I wouldn't step foot in there because there might still be some irritable Horde who will pick a fight with you on general principle.&nbsp Besides, the road to Shadowfang Keep is the Northern side of the fork in the road just before Pyrewood (/tloc 49,72) so head up the hill to your right. [b]PROTIP:[/b] Do this quest early in the morning.&nbsp There's a high chance of being ganked by Horde on the way to Shadowfang Keep, but that chance lessens when there's less people playing, obviously. Shadowfang Keep is an instance, so once you enter you're safe from PvP gankers.&nbsp So relax the hardest part is behind you. During the quest in Shadowfang Keep you'll have the option of freeing an Alliance prisoner in the first 'section' of the keep.&nbsp Doing so will open a sealed door which leads into the Keep's courtyard.&nbsp The stables are directly in front of that door. Now what you'll want to do, if soloing, is lure mobs one at a time onto the steps leading down into the courtyard.&nbsp This is a good way to control aggro and lessen the chance of linking.&nbsp If needed, drag a mob all the way up back through the door.

Comment3: I'm a 25 Ret Pally (I was a twink at 19 so not everything will be just as easy for you), and i'm flying to IF to turn the quest in as I write this.&nbsp This is how you get each piece: The first section, where you have to defend Daphne Stilwell from the Defias is not too hard, and not too easy.&nbsp It's really yourself that you have to look out, since she has a very good amount of hp, and regains it after each 'wave'. For the Smithing Hammer, Get to Southshore (Run there if you do not have the flightpaths), and then run east along the road until you reach Silverpine Forest.&nbsp Follow the road up the hill and into SFK.&nbsp You may need a group for this, but since you're a pally, you might have Turn Undead.&nbsp See if you can sneak upstairs and past as many pats and mobs as possible.&nbsp You will arrive into a courtyard.&nbsp Jump out and run to the stables to get the Hammer (On a log inside). For the Kor Gem, you have to go to Auberdine, in Darkshore.&nbsp Take the boat in the Wetlands, and talk to Thundris Windweaver.&nbsp He'll give you a quest.&nbsp Run south until you reach Ashenvale, and then run west when you reach a path.&nbsp Keep running northwest from there until you reach the Instance, and swim under the little barrier.&nbsp Pop up in the otherside, and kill the Naga in there one by one until it drops.&nbsp Return to Thundris, and then Return to IF to complete the quest.

Comment1: I did this solo at level 20 with green gear and 11 points into Holy. I failed it the first time but managed to do it on my second try. I have a few tips: First, use Retribution Aura. The Defias Raiders don't have a ton of HP, and it will weaken the rest down while you concentrate on one. The first time I tried and failed was with Devotion. Second, use Consecrate to grab initial aggro on the wave, and use it once or twice more during each fight. Same idea as Ret aura it will beat all the Raiders down so by the time you get to the last one they will die in 1 or 2 hits. Third, fight close to Daphne. If you fight close enough to her she will run up and melee with you. Between Ret aura and Consecrate she won't pull aggro, but you could use Righteous Fury just to be safe =) Finally, bring some Melon Juice. You do get time to drink between waves but your time is limited. PS - Can't hurt to make sure LoH is up! Good luck to all =)

Comment5: I'm a 25 Ret Pally (I was a twink at 19 so not everything will be just as easy for you), and i'm flying to IF to turn the quest in as I write this.&nbsp This is how you get each piece: The first section, where you have to defend Daphne Stilwell from the Defias is not too hard, and not too easy.&nbsp It's really yourself that you have to look out, since she has a very good amount of hp, and regains it after each 'wave'. For the Whitestone Oak Lumber in Deadmines, I can solo until the ogre, but since you need ranged to pull him, I suggest a group.&nbsp You just have to get to the goblins, and they should drop it the very first kill. For the Jordan's Refined Ore Shipment, you have to go to Loch Modan, in Thelsamar, into the house with the Tailoring Supplies guy on the porch.&nbsp Talk to Bailor Stonehand, and take his quest.&nbsp Then go Northeast across the lake until you start seeing the ogre encampment.&nbsp Go in, and keep going until you reach a tree with the item you need under it.&nbsp Grab it and finish the quest for the shipment. For the Smithing Hammer, Get to Southshore (Run there if you do not have the flightpaths), and then run east along the road until you reach Silverpine Forest.&nbsp Follow the road up the hill and into SFK.&nbsp You may need a group for this, but since you're a pally, you might have Turn Undead. See if you can sneak upstairs and past as many pats and mobs as possible.&nbsp You will arrive into a courtyard.&nbsp Jump out and run to the stables to get the Hammer (On a log inside). For the Kor Gem, you have to go to Auberdine, in Darkshore.&nbsp Take the boat in the Wetlands, and talk to Thundris Windweaver.&nbsp He'll give you a quest.&nbsp Run south until you reach Ashenvale, and then run west when you reach a path.&nbsp Keep running northwest from there until you reach the Instance, and swim under the little barrier.&nbsp Pop up in the otherside, and kill the Naga in there one by one until it drops.&nbsp Return to Thundris, and then Return to IF to complete the quest.

The entrance to Black Fathoms Deep is found somewhere amongst the Roman columns of the ruins found on the northwestern area of the beach. I've been down there twice but both times I had knocked a couple back and wasn't exactly a vacuum for details. Comment2: My priest finished his Benediction quest yesterday (2/22/06) with ease after struggling a bit with the quest.&nbsp Here are a few tips, including a few not mentioned in previous posts that turned this quest from frustrating and difficult into easy as pie. 1) Bring a druid friend and have them cast thorns on all party members just before you begin.&nbsp Being able to have your passive aggro group members deal damage is a huge plus.&nbsp 2) Take a trip into Stratholme and collect at least 5 holy waters.&nbsp Bring more if you want some insurance for another run.&nbsp OR&nbsp Bring some bombs if you're an engineer.&nbsp Basically, you want something that does an AoE blast for about 400 damage on a short cooldown.&nbsp Holy water has a shorter cooldown than engineering gear, but go with whichever is available to you. 3) Bring 10-20 Oils of Immolation. 4) Do a dry run or watch a vid so you know what to expect.&nbsp The biggest problem I had was [i]not getting back to the spawn point[/i] for the next group early enough.&nbsp My first few tries (totally solo) went poorly because I stayed with the group I was currently&nbsp healing too long, the next one spawned, and I wouldn't get the purple-diseased peasants cured in time and I'd lose a few too many to the skele's.&nbsp While it can be distracting that a bunch of peasants will get the green disease as they near the quest giver, don't worry too much about them.&nbsp Toss a renew or remove the disease on a few if they have low health and just forget about them.&nbsp Losing 1 to a green disease is far better than losing 4 or more to the skeletons and purple disease in the next wave.&nbsp When I focused better on positioning myself for the next wave and letting the current wave continue on towards the light, I did extremely well... to the point where I could finally see how the quest 'could' be done solo, especially with some potions. Still, to make things easier, I did the quest with two friends at the cave entrance: a bear-form feral-geared druid and a hunter with his pet on passive.&nbsp Since all had thorns, they did a nice amount of damage and aggro-holding while I concentrated on healing and removing diseases.&nbsp Whenever I noticed a crowd of skele's whittling down my party's health, I tossed a Holy water at them.&nbsp This instantly killed the skele's and allowed my 'target dummies' to survive the entire fight (except for the hunter's pet... he used a cat instead of his more-AC-than-some-60-Warriors pet).&nbsp Whenever I didn't get all the skele's with the holy water or if it was on cooldown, I just popped an oil of immolation and shielded if I needed to do so.&nbsp Using this method, I don't think I lost 2/3 of my mana or health for the duration of the quest.&nbsp Note:&nbsp This quest has little-to-nothing to do with your skills as a priest.&nbsp Think of it as a test in micromanagement without being able to have a useful interface.&nbsp If you're like me and you never really used the health bars above the heads of mobs (v key), then you might want to turn it on for a while to get used to how the healthbars jump around in a crowd.&nbsp Or, go into the battlegrounds and don't use your party/raid interface... work on healing without it.&nbsp If you can do that well at all, you'll do this quest just fine, since that is what is really being tested here. Gonnek, Earthen Ring Approx 7300 Mana with an AI/Druid buff I only used Renew - Rank 8, Abolish Disease, and PowerWord:Shield - Rank 8 for the entire quest.&nbsp I didn't use any health or mana potions. Good luck!

Instructions: Steal Silixiz's Tower Key from Foreman Silixiz, then kill two Mutated Venture Co. Drones, two Venture Co. Patrollers, and two Venture Co. Lookouts. Comment1: * To get the key from Silixiz, pickpocket him. If he doesn't have anything to pickpocket, kill him and wait for him to respawn, then do it again. * First floor: Mutated Drones. Ambush will instakill them. If you're alone, ambush one, run, then come back and ambush the other. * Second floor: Patrollers. Rupture works very well here and takes off an abnormal amount of life. * Third floor (outside): Lookouts. Eviscerate (even a one-point eviscerate) will transform them into green slimes that are easier to kill. * Fourth floor: Gallywix. Ambush him to lower his life to 50%, then the rest of the fight is as you would expect. If you're level 20, bring a friend -- he hits hard. After he's dead, take his head and lockpick the chest (need skill ~85 I think) and you're done.
Comment2: This is entirely doable solo at 20 if you're mildly twinked and remember to use the weaknesses of each mob. Being 22 would help of course seeing as you have access to skills like distract and vanish. Some notes of my own to add to the above post: - Part 1, Pickpocketing Make sure to approach Silixiz from behind and use pickpocket as far away as possible (5 yd range), otherwise he's sure to detect you. Kill him afterwards, both as a courtesy to the next rogue coming to do the quest and in order to avoid him aggro'ing on you in case you have to run away during the rest of the quest. - Part 2, Mutated Drones This seems to be the hardest part. Be very careful and only approach one of them when they turn their backs to you and spam ambush till it connects (their stealth detection is insanely high). Then run till you drop aggro and do the same with the other one. - Part 3, Patrolers These mobs are weak to rupture, but they're very easy to kill even without it. Probably the easiest part, just good ol' hack n slash works on these guys. - Part 4, Lookouts Nothing else to say about them really... just get that 1 CP as fast as possible and immediately Eviscerate. Very easy to kill that way. - Part 5, Gallywix Make sure to have Evasion and healing potions ready and not cooling down before engaging. Open with Ambush to drop him to 50% health, then immediately pop Evasion (he hits very hard, you don't want to waste a moment without it up) and just hack away. Pop a healing potion if necessary. If you're close to dying, make sure he's facing away from the stairway entrance. Didn't try this myself, but supposedly if you die with him facing the stairs, he'll stay in that position when he resets making it nearly impossible to ambush him without being detected. Another note: You do ABSOLUTELY want to use Ambush in the parts that recommend it and you need a dagger in your main hand for that. If you've been using two swords up to this point, get a dagger for this quest. Even if it's a level 1 grey one, doesn't matter, you can just switch to your usual weapon right after you Ambush. Also, be sure to get your dagger skill up to a decent level, you don't want your Ambush to miss.
Comment3: I just did the quest, and some people have inaccurate information.&nbsp Just to clarify: * To get the key from Silixiz, pickpocket him.&nbsp If he doesn't have anything to pickpocket, kill him and wait for him to respawn, then do it again. * First floor: Mutated Drones.&nbsp Ambush will instakill them.&nbsp If you're alone, ambush one, run, then come back and ambush the other. * Second floor: Patrollers.&nbsp Rupture works very well here and takes off an abnormal amount of life. * Third floor (outside): Lookouts.&nbsp Eviscerate (even a one-point eviscerate) will transform them into green slimes that are easier to kill. * Fourth floor: Gallywix.&nbsp Ambush him to lower his life to 50%, then the rest of the fight is as you would expect.&nbsp If you're level 20, bring a friend -- he hits hard.&nbsp After he's dead, take his head and lockpick the chest (need skill ~85 I think) and you're done.
Comment4: Some of this overlaps with the above but I'll go into more gory detail about soloing this -- [b]Requirements[/b] If you're going to solo this, I would recommend waiting until lvl22.&nbsp I believe the others who testifed they soloed this at lower levels, but I find that vanish and distract are *extremely* helpful here for every level of the tower and particularly for Gallywix, and also being able to have a healing potion (lvl22 req, just buy one from the AH) helps a lot. Get your lockpicking skill up to 100 (or at least 80) from the ship in the 'Plundering the Plunderers' quest.&nbsp It's kinda boring repeatedly picking the lockboxes but there's no reason not to max out your skill... I just looked over my quests and read a newspaper while clicking alternately on two boxes... Be sure your equipment is repaired because you will probably die repeatedly (I died 7 times and yes I did read all the comments here beforehand so it was just a matter of execution). Get lots of flash powder for vanish. Get a few healing potions or at least lesser healing potions. Make sure ambush, eviscerate, stealth, vanish, distract, pickpocket, expose armor, rupture, evade are on your toolbar because you'll need all of them. [b]On dying[/b] One important note is that if you die in the tower, you can resurrect on any floor... not sure if this is obvious to everyone.&nbsp This allows you to bypass some of the respawned monsters that you've already killed and start right where you left off. [b]Silixiz key[/b] I had no trouble stealing the key from him using distract with my lvl22 with 2 points in Master of Deception talent.&nbsp If he has no key, kill him and then come back later, maybe do the goblin quests nearby while you kill time. [b]First three levels[/b] Ambush, rupture, eviscerate the first three levels as others have mentioned.&nbsp For the first level, distract to get them to face away from you, ambush one and then either run/vanish then ambush again, or 1on1 the other.&nbsp For the next two levels, distract, sap one then kill the other, or just take both of them on.&nbsp You can always use up your vanish or evades here because you're probably not going to get through the whole thing without dying at least once, and remember the next time you resurrect you can bypass whatever you've already killed. [b]Gallywix[/b] I had a lot of trouble sneaking up on him.&nbsp When I went up the stairs, he was staring right at me, so I couldn't even get line of sight to distract him away from me without getting aggro'd.&nbsp A trick I found is that he tends to keep looking in the direction he was facing when he killed you last.&nbsp So I just made sure he was facing away from the stairs (i.e. looking right out the tower) when I died, then the next time I could get behind him to distract and ambush. If you ambush - vanish - ambush, he's deadmeat since each is triggered to take off 50%.&nbsp Even if you only get one off (e.g. if he sees you when you're coming up the stairs before you ambush), it's still no big deal.&nbsp If you put on evasion, start off with a 4+ point expose armor, and use a healing potion, you should be able to kill him reasonably.&nbsp This means you don't really need vanish either, in case you used it up earlier -- you can just stealth up and ambush him, then fight as normal.&nbsp Note that if you try the ambush-vanish-ambush method, you don't have much time after you vanish before he pops back to max health!&nbsp Immediately ambush him once you've vanished. Of course [i]don't get the chest until after you've completed the quest[/i].&nbsp The first time I went up the stairs, someone else had killed Gallywix and I opened the chest, and got poisoned.&nbsp It at least lowers your agility, I'm not sure what else (some others above claim it lowers stealth).&nbsp So actually I had to kill Gallywix while poisoned :-b.

You have to stay up above the ravine, and you will see the cave where the cultists (an others) reside.
