Progress: N/A
Comment1: This quest is probably the most time-consuming you will face up to this point as a shaman. There is also not a lot of information regarding it's completion, so I will help out those beginning it with a walkthrough. Step One: Islen She's where other posters have placed her next to the ship near Ratchet/Northwest Keep. She will send you to see Brine, in the Southern Barrens. Step Two: Brine Brine is not the easiest NPC to find, so let me describe how to find her. Take the road back from Ratchet to the Crossroads. Now take the road leading to Camp Taraujo. Keep going straight, instead of turning right to Taraujo. You will pass the area called 'Field of Giants.' You should try to stay on the road if you're just lvl 20, there are some higher level mobs that could give you trouble if you're not adequately equipped. After you pass the Field of Giants, you will likely come upon a Tauren, named Gann. If you hail him, he will give you some info on how to find Brine. He also begins a quest in the Dwarf area not too far away that is worth doing while you are progressing/completing this quest. Gann could be past the area where Brine is at, so after you pass the Field of Giants, start looking to your right. You will eventually see a tent/camp on top of one of the foothills prior to one of the pig people areas. This is Brine's camp. You may have to fight some pig people, hyenas, lizards, and flying snakes to get there (lvl 20-23). Run up the hill to Brine's camp. She'll be waiting for you with a ? over her head. After she talks to you, she'll give you a bag to fill from the pond directly below her camp. Run down to the pond, kill whatever NPC's you have to, and click on the bag to fill it from the pond. While you're filling it, a lvl 20 pig will spawn that you will have to kill. I wasn't interrupted from filling while the pig shot a few arrows at me. Take the filled bag up to Brine and she'll talk to you about the pig you just killed and the water you gave her. She'll now give you another bag and tell you to head for Hillsbrad Foothills and Tarren Mill. If you are new to the game, and have spent most of your time in Ogrimar/Durotar/The Barrens, it's time to do some traveling. Step Three: Tarren Mill You need to get back to Ogrimar and take the zepplin in front of the city to the Undercity in the Eastern Kingdoms. When you get off the zepplin, you can either fly to Sepulcher or run/walk there. If you walk there, take the roads leading to Silverpine to get to Sepulcher. Once you get to Sepulcher, continue on the MAIN road that goes South. You will eventually come to a sign that points to the Hillsbrad Foothills and you should take a LEFT on that road and follow it. You are now entering 'Contestested Territory,' and should be in Ghost Wolf form. There may be some Alliance gankers that try to kill you. Stay on the road and keep running. You will eventually see signs directing you towards Tarren Mill. Follow them into the city. It is a Horde camp and the 'Deathguards' in front won't bother you. There is a well in the camp that you should go to and click on your bag when you are next to it to fill it. After you have filled your bag, you can either run back the way you came, or gate back to the other continent. Take the filled bag back to Brine. She will take it from you and give you another bag directing you to towards Ashenvale. A suggestion might be to gain a few levels doing other things before heading out on this and the remaining parts of this quest. You will have to fight a few alliance NPC's along the road going to Tarren Mill. They're not a problem, however. Moreso, the levels might be to give you a little more HP's if you run into Alliance gankers. Step Four: Ashenvale - Ruins of Stardust You can take Brine's directions if you want. However, be prepared to do some fighting. There's an easier way. You probably have gone into Stonetalon Mtns by now (or should have). If you are lvl 23 or better, you should not have any trouble with the route I'm going to give you. You could also do it lower level, but will have some instances with multiple 20+ NPC's. There is a tunnel that leads from the Windshear Crags area to Ashenvale, and acutally dumps you out near Mystral Lake. Mystral Lake is not the body of water you need, but it is not far off, either. You will see Mystral Lake as you exit the tunnel off to your right. Take a LEFT instead and follow the path. You will have a few 20+ bears that will aggro if you get too close. You will not need to go too far until you reach the Ruins of Stardust, and the pond there. There are elementals around the pond that range from 20-23. You will have to fight a couple to get to the island in the center of the pond, and several on the island itself. You will get a few 'shredder pages' as loot from these mobs. Save them, because they belong to another quest. After you have killed the surrounding elementals on the island, look for a birdbath. That is the fountain you need to fill your bag. Click on the bag near the birdbath. Gate back or run back to The Barrens, and Brine. Brine will take the bag from you and combine them to make water sample that you will need to take back to Islen, near Ratchet (location above). Step Five: Islen Islen will take your water sample from Brine and give you the Sapta. You will also be left with a pure water sample from Brine. You need to take both and head back to the other continent near Sepulcher. Step Six: The Shrine - Water Sapta - Corrupt Manifistation. The shrine you're looking for is along the coast directly west from Sepulcher. You will have to get down to the coast by backtracking or going a little more south. I went back North a bit and was able to work my way down. Once you reach the coast you will have to travel along the coast to the shrine. Use the arrow pointing towards Sepulcher on your mini map to guide you. The shrine will be directly west from the arrow. Travel north or south to find it, depending on which direction you used to reach the coast. I did see and didn't bother with a lvl 24 elite NPC as I was traveling to the coast. Most of the NPC's that you may have to fight will be 14-16 werewolf-type NPC's that shouldn't give you any problems. When you reach the shrine, drink the sapta. The water elementals will then appear. You will need to find/target the Corrupted Manifistation. It is the only one that will allow you to target it. Keep moving/targeting/tabbing to find it, then once you do, kill it. Loot the bracer from the mob. Head to the altar near the shrine. Click on the altar. You will now get a message to talk to another elemental/manifistation. I found this one near the back and went over and talked to it. This manifistation will speak to you and give you the crystal that you will take back to Islen. You have 20 minutes once you drink the sapta to find the corrupt elemental, kill it - loot it, go to the altar and click with the water sample from Brine and the bracers, then go and talk to the other elemental. If you don't get it done in time, there is a troll sitting on top of a rock near the shrine that will allow you to go and get another sapta from Islen. You shouldn't need to, but he's there if you do. Step Seven: Back to Islen You know where she is. Take your crystal back to her, she'll give you the water totem and also give you your healing stream totem spell. One of the longest quests you've probably done thus far in the game. It's worth several thousand points in XP, however, so it's worth it. You should be about ready to work on the quests from Gann by the time you finish it, which are worth several thousand as well, and help your Tauren faction. Good luck, and I hope this saves people time.

Comment2: Did this last night (patch 1.6.1). I found it really quite easy, considering some of the comments that were on Anonymous and Anonymous. Everybody needs to stay in one corner. We used the corner on the right as you enter the room. Our party makeup was protection warrior, mage (with instant AE of course), holy priest and two shamans with resto up to NS. Warrior had full +def tanking gear (the best ottainable outside MC), the other shaman had 7 elements + earthfury boots, the priest had full devout, I wore my +250 healing mail, and the mage had mostly magisters with a handful of other blues and greens. The first wave will be non-elites, 12 of them or so. They all aggroed us at once, so this is what you bring your mage for. AoE, with heals on the mage. We got little to no time to get out of combat after the first wave, so mash that level 55 water button, because as long as you [i]start[/i] drinking in that few seconds, you can keep drinking until the next wave of ghosts are upon you. The 2nd wave were all melee ghosts from memory, and they're elites. We kept stoneskin, earthbind, mana, health, GoA and windfury up at all times. Don't waste mana on magma and fire nova totems, it's of the utmost importance that the shaman(s) keep all their mana for when the priest goes OOM, which will happen very often. This wave wasn't particularly hard, as the ghosts for some reason didn't link all at once, meaning we could take them down almost one by one with good use of shackle. The next wave, from memory, is the hard wave. Somewhere around 9-12 elite ghosts spawn in groups of three, and they all aggro you at once. Even if you range pull them from your corner, the other groups will run (float?) over to where the group you pulled were, then head straight for you. This wave is extremely hard, bordering on impossible. I hope you brought your ankhs. Our prot warrior is very skilled, and he held aggro on all of them. If you have a rogue a secondary warrior (or you, the shaman, if you have neither) use the 'target lowest health' hotkey, which is V or B by default I think, and have everyone assist that person to kill a target. DO NOT have the mage AoE. Kill as many targets as possible, and when you're about to wipe, which is very probable, run into the corner (I mean very corner, mash yourself up against that wall) and wait to die. Self-rez, and rez everyone. The quest will not fail if you wipe. Med up (you won't get aggro if you're in the corner) and pull the last few mobs, who will again link on you. We got 5 mobs down before we died the first time, so the last 4 or so were cake. The final wave involves some caster ghosts who cast shadow bolt. Make sure the priest gives everyone shadow resist, and put down grounding totem. After each wave, a named mob will come. The name is always 'Aspect of ...'. The final wave's named, 'Aspect of Shadow' from memory, is the only one worth mentioning. He casts shadow bolt volley, and has a shield of some variety which is purgeable. He was really the only one we needed to concentrate for. What we did (cheap tactics 4tw) is to keep the nameds constantly shackled, and have our own spirit and mana/health totems regen us to full health. It takes a long time, but it can make the ensuing waves so much easier, considering you don't always get time to drink. After these waves, the Darkreaver will spawn in the middle of the room. Med up and buff up, you have plenty of time. The boss looks somewhat like Baron Rivendare, and is quite fun to fight. He has a Balnazzar-esque mind control, and he always used it on one of our shamans, burning our nature's swiftnesses and healing himself. Mind control CAN be purged (use rank 1 purge so as to not knock of another buff) and can of course be dispelled by the priest. That's really the only interesting thing he did. He has a lot of HP and hits relatively hard, but nothing a skilled warrior and priest shouldn't be able to handle, with the shaman throwing the odd heal in. Put a searing totem down, there's no more mobs after this one so you don't have to worry about aggro. After he dies, the head is lootable and can be looted by more than one shaman. [url=/npc=14516]Link to the mob with loot table[/url]. Comment1: Did this quest on my shammy and then next morning went through to take two guidie friends on it. Had read a lot about how hard or even impossible this is and also heard lots of stories since about failed attempts on this server (Thunderhorn). Had two successful runs with no wipes and so thought I would share how we did it. Class mix: Group 1: Shaman x 3 (one rest/enh, two enh/ele), mage and warrior. All well decked out in blues and odd purple. Group 2: Shamans x 3, priest and warrior (warrior well decked out in purple, rest blues) Issues with this fight are the duration requiring mana conservation, and a hard point where burst damage is needed, where most people keep wiping (see notes below on the 3rd wave, green mobs). All mobs are lvl 60-61 undead and immune to war stomps and stunning (exception being grenades which I am pretty sure did stun them). At the end of each wave an 'Aspect Of' spirit appears, which is bigger than the regular mob. Killing it triggers the onset of the next wave. We fought from the SW corner on the pile of bones both times. Apparently this fight was made harder a few patches ago. There are very few points in the fight where you get to drink and eat (and then only for a few seconds), so bring first aid and lots of mana pots! The fight lasts 20-30mins. The Waves: 1) About 10-15 non elites (?red)- moderate hps, easily taken out by a well supported mage. 3 shamans with magma totems did it easily too. Easy. 2) About 15 elites (blue) - one group spawned as a mob of 4 or so, the rest spawned alone or in pairs and headed our way. They don't do a lot of damage but have a fair amount of hps. Just keep up the damage on them, use first aid when you aren't fighting and keep your mana stores not depleted to heal the tank. They do place a curse that increases physical damage by 90 for 10mins. 3) About 12 elites (green) - this is the most difficult wave by far, and the one that people keep wiping on. They all spawn simultaneously, and although I have heard that people get aggroed by all at once, even right in the corner we got about 7 or 8 the first time run straight for us, and about 4 immediately, followed by another 3 10 secs later, on our second run. The spawn points were different each time so I don't know if you can pick the ideal corner. There may be luck involved. In any case we had to deal with about 7-8 elites that hit us all at once. A hard ask as they do hit hard and have a load of hps. Our strategy was to have the warrior do an AE taunt, shield wall and take em all while the offtank (shaman) hit one, with all the others assisting the offtank. Take one at a time and unload everything, and once you have them down to 3 or so you are back to standard aggro management. If you look like you are wiping make sure your SS priest or shaman is right back in the corner. This didn't happen to us luckily!. At the end of this wave you will no doubt have no mana so make sure you shackle the 'Aspect' and wait til health and mana are back to full. Our first group didn't have a priest so just kept popping mana pots and first aid, and moving to the next wave..... 4) About 10-15 elites (purple) - these guys keep wandering over in ones and twos, and if you get behind in killing them they pile up so you have to get a balance of killing them quickly enough but allowing time to regenerate health and mana by any means available. The fire shadow bolts from range so need to be silenced or earth shocked to come and melee like any caster. Their dps seemed higher but they had less HPs than the third wave and were relatively straightforward 5) The Darkreaver - looks like the Baron in Strath. Has a lot of HPs and possesses group members (just purge it), but is actually a straightforward fight. Our tank noticed you can disarm him although he is immunne to stunning. Ok hope that helps. Our second run was very smooth with a priest, actually I would call it easy, as we could shackle the 'Aspect of' spirits and be at full health and mana for the next wave. Have all your damage talents online and ready for that third wave and you should be ok. Difficult but with a good group and lots of healing and tankage it is possible to do it without wiping. Now to try it as an all shaman group of 5!
Comment2: [b]overview:[/b] The quest involves four waves of nine elite ghosts apiece, plus an elite boss at the end. You can't just charge in all willy-nilly and expect to complete the quest. Unless, of course, you're uber-geared to the max in which case why would you need the reward helm in the first place? :)&nbsp Here's the method my friends and I use and it's never failed. [b]Ideal group:[/b] Well, I'm a priest, so I've never done this quest without a priest. Priests play a roll in making this easier, but I'm thinking it could be done with a resto druid too, so long as they know how to make the most of thier mana pool. Other than that, you could pretty much do this with any class. [b]NOTE:[/b]&nbsp The more shammies the merrier, totems make the fourth wave of ghosts easier to deal with, as you'll see further down this post. &nbsp [b]Before you start the event:[/b] Have your entire group go the the corner that's to your right as you enter Rattlegore's room. I believe it's the south-east corner. You'll stay in that corner for the first two fights. [b]IMPORTANT![/b] STAY in that corner,NO ONE leaves. Again.. you'll see why later. Have the shammie set the summoning item in the center of the room. [b]first wave:[/b] The first wave of ghosts show up all at once. DON'T PANIC! They don't hit very hard, just pick them off one at a time. At the end of the first wave comes a 'boss' ghost, called the aspect of somethingorother. If you have a priest, have them shackle this boss. The next wave of ghosts won't show up until the aspect ghost is dead. Keep the aspect ghost shackled 'til everyone is bandaged/mana'd up. There's no time limit, you can keep him shackled for as long as you like. &nbsp &nbsp Once everyone is ready, kill off the aspect ghost and now comes the [b]second wave:[/b] The second wave is easy too. Nine ghosts, they don't show up all at once. Again, stay in the south-east corner and pull these ghosts to you as they appear. After the ghosts are all killed, another ghost 'boss' shows up, again called the aspect of somethingorother. Now for this aspect, you don't need to shackle him. In fact, don't shackle him. Kill him right off, but when you do, [b]make sure you are all in the south-east corner.[/b] This aspect lays a nasty +90 damage taken curse down on everyone, and if you don't have a mage or a druid, you'll have to wait it out. If you are all in the south-east corner, you won't aggro the [b]third wave:[/b] This is the wipe wave, and with good reason. They have a large aggro radius, and they hit pretty hard. They also have a stamina-weaking spell, which can make it hard for the healer to see just how close to death you really are :) For this wave you'll want to take these guys on three at a time. Here's how: &nbsp The third wave consists of three groups of three ghosts each. Take a look across from you, in the south-west corner. The three ghosts there move around, occasionally one will meander out to the middle of the room, and meander back to the corner. Have your tank run along the south wall into that corner, but he'll have to time it so that he gets to that corner when the three ghosts are more or less bunched togther. If he's timed it well, he'll only pull the three. Then the rest of your group can follow the south wall and finish off the three ghosts. From that corner you can pull the other two groups to you at your leisure. [b]tips:[/b] If your warrior pulls the middle group too and winds up with six ghosts, let him die. You can rez your tank and try again. He might not like that but hey.. that's what tanks are for! Another trick is to have the warrior pop a shield block when he runs into the corner. This buys the healer a little more time to move into the corner and start healing. Don't bother to shackle these guys, it takes too much time and mana, and the healer will pretty much be spam healing at this point. These guys hit pretty hard. &nbsp Another aspect boss shows up after this wave. At this point, shackle him if you need time to regenerate health and mana, the last wave doesn't come 'til the aspect ghost is killed. After the aspect ghost is dead the [b]fourth and last wave[/b] shows up. These guys are also difficult, but managable. They are casters, and they cast a multi-shot shadow bolt that can do a pretty solid amount of damage. Here's where a multi-shammie party comes in handy. Have your shammies spam grounding totems. They absord the shadow bolts and make life easier for your healer. &nbsp For this last group you don't need to stay in any particular corner. Feel free to move around. The initial group is about three ghosts, kill them off as fast as you can. The rest of the ghosts will show up on a timer. [b]tips:[/b] These ghosts are on a timer, which means it's in your best interest to kill them off as quickly as possible, don't stop to regen mana. After the initial burst of ghosts they start showing up one at a time, at which point, if you need to, you can take turns staying out of combat to regen mana. [b]conserve mana[/b] during this fight because the darkreaver shows up after this wave, and you won't get a break. (side note) There's an aspect ghost after this wave too, just kill it off right away. The reaver shows up whether the aspect is dead or not. Congrats! You've made it through all the notorius ghost waves! Now you get to contend with [b]The Darkreaver:[/b] This guy is a straightforward fight, no tricks, other than a mind control that's easily purged. He's the easiest part of the quest, really. Kill his butt&nbsp and go get your nifty new helm! [b]over-all tricks and tips:[/b] Use an MA for this event. Pick someone to be the main assist and everyone target what he's targeting. It's less chaotic, it makes life easier for your healer and tank, and it's a faster way to plow through multiple mobs. &nbsp Don't AOE! It might be tempting, 'specially in the first fight, but don't do it. Chances are, your healer is going to be busy keeping the tank and himself alive. Don't add to his burden by trying to mow down 5-8 mobs at once. &nbsp If the worst happens, and it looks like it's going to be a wipe, everyone run back to the south-east corner. You can safely rez and regroup there to try again. [b]Don't release![/b] Once the event is started, you can't get back into the room again until the instance is reset. I hope this helps clarify how to do this quest. I'm sure it's not the only way to do it, but it's seemed to work for me and my friends. Good luck!
Comment3: Before the event is triggered, the group will want to go to the corner you'll face by entering the basement and turning right 90 degrees. There are four waves. After each wave, you fight a named mob called 'Aspect of [something]'. Wave 1: As soon as the Divination Scryer is placed, 9 or so very slow moving mobs spawn. Afterwards, take out the middle group, then the far group. Kill all three groups, a third named spawns. Again, make sure you're in the corner when he dies. Comment2: Did this last night (patch 1.6.1). I found it really quite easy, considering some of the comments that were on Anonymous and Anonymous. Everybody needs to stay in one corner. We used the corner on the right as you enter the room. Our party makeup was protection warrior, mage (with instant AE of course), holy priest and two shamans with resto up to NS. Warrior had full +def tanking gear (the best ottainable outside MC), the other shaman had 7 elements + earthfury boots, the priest had full devout, I wore my +250 healing mail, and the mage had mostly magisters with a handful of other blues and greens. The 2nd wave were all melee ghosts from memory, and they're elites. We kept stoneskin, earthbind, mana, health, GoA and windfury up at all times. Don't waste mana on magma and fire nova totems, it's of the utmost importance that the shaman(s) keep all their mana for when the priest goes OOM, which will happen very often. This wave wasn't particularly hard, as the ghosts for some reason didn't link all at once, meaning we could take them down almost one by one with good use of shackle. The next wave, from memory, is the hard wave. Somewhere around 9-12 elite ghosts spawn in groups of three, and they all aggro you at once. Even if you range pull them from your corner, the other groups will run (float?) over to where the group you pulled were, then head straight for you. This wave is extremely hard, bordering on impossible. I hope you brought your ankhs. Our prot warrior is very skilled, and he held aggro on all of them. If you have a rogue a secondary warrior (or you, the shaman, if you have neither) use the 'target lowest health' hotkey, which is V or B by default I think, and have everyone assist that person to kill a target. DO NOT have the mage AoE. Kill as many targets as possible, and when you're about to wipe, which is very probable, run into the corner (I mean very corner, mash yourself up against that wall) and wait to die. Self-rez, and rez everyone. The quest will not fail if you wipe. Med up (you won't get aggro if you're in the corner) and pull the last few mobs, who will again link on you. We got 5 mobs down before we died the first time, so the last 4 or so were cake. The final wave involves some caster ghosts who cast shadow bolt. He was really the only one we needed to concentrate for. What we did (cheap tactics 4tw) is to keep the nameds constantly shackled, and have our own spirit and mana/health totems regen us to full health. He has a lot of HP and hits relatively hard, but nothing a skilled warrior and priest shouldn't be able to handle, with the shaman throwing the odd heal in. Put a searing totem down, there's no more mobs after this one so you don't have to worry about aggro. After he dies, the head is lootable and can be looted by more than one shaman. Comment5: I was able to solo this entire quest chain at level 31 and get the robe. Although there are better robes to get in your 30s, I'm pretty sure this is the best robe locks can get at my nub level. The most difficult parts are, by far, the infernal stone and the smoldering coals, respectively (infernals are way more difficult than the elementals, surprisingly), so I'll just go over those. Both of the areas you have to go to for these components are high traffic, high pvp zones, and you're liable to get ganked just for being there, so if you're on a pvp server, I'd highly recommend hiding behind a corner and busting out your eye to scout before proceeding, because you're going to be there for a few minutes. As it turned out, there were some allies out in Arathi farming my mobs and the eye kept me from wandering into trouble. OK, so first the hard part- the infernal. How do you solo a mob 6-7 levels up? Very carefully and slowly. I used my infernal for this and dropped some +health regen pots to help out, although the pots may not have been neccessary. The trick here is to make sure your v-dub keeps agro by taking one of his taunts off autocast and hitting it whenever neccessary to pull agro off yourself. If you play a warrior (60 warrior, here), then hopefully you know that your taunt ability doesn't actually add to agro, it merely puts you on the top of the agro list. It's an agro 'puller,' but not an agro 'keeper.' I don't know the details of vdub taunt, but I assumed it worked the same way as the warrior taunt. Wait a few seconds for vdub to get a firm hold on the mob, and let loose your dots. I'm affliction spec, so I have three insta-dots, and I just used those. I seem to remember infernals being resistant to fire damage (but don't quote me on that!), and didn't bother with any fire spells. I just cast the dots until they landed, waited a second, then drain life'd as neccessary so I could heal v-dub when he needed it. This is not a race- if you do too much damage, you'll pull agro and die very quickly. I didn't use a single nuke, and I think I might've died if I did. If things start getting hairy, sac v-dub, aplify curse + CoEx, pray it lands, and run. Stone dropped off the first infernal I killed. And now the easy part- the elementals in arathi for smoldering coals. Just buy a stack of cresting charms at the AH (I bought 10 for a G), and use those. Drop rate was not 100%, more like 50, and I had six charms left over. As a side note, warriors use those charms for their whirlwind weapon quest, and you could probably make a fellow nub guildie warrior happy by saving them for him/her. Farming for those really sucks, especially if you're trying to get your weapon at the earliest level possible, and the help is usually appreciated.

Comment1: Alright, after defeating Immol'thar (be aware to kill his eyes quickly!), our group - warrior, hunter, priest, paladin, warlock (me) - buffed up and I released the imp from his jar. After releasing the Imp he will start placing the bell, wheel and candle in the circle. After placing those 3 items he will disappear. As soon as the Imp leaves, Imps spawn at the edge of the summoning circle. These don't hit for more than 1 if the artifacts are all working. When an artifact goes down, it makes a loud noise and floats lower, and it can be easily identified by mousing over it (if it's broken it will have the wheel instead of the mouse pointer). Fixing it costs a soul shard, so bring plenty. I used around 10 for repairing the artifacts, and 3 more for enslaving a demon, a healthstone for the warrior and a soulstone for the pala. After a while, dread guards will spawn after each other (4 to be precise). It's wise to enslave the first one so he can attack the next dread guard that spawns. (If there are 2 warlocks in the group, you each enslave one and let the enslaved one kill the other spawns). If another one adds while the other hasn't died yet, you should banish it, since these are strong (level 60 elites). Once all four dread guards have spawned, the ritual will soon be over. You can check this by looking at the pink symbols at the floor - 9 have to be lit to create enough energy for the summoning circle. You will directly notice when the ritual is complete as around the circle is a strong energy wall with lots of purple and pinky bubbles rising from it. All demons will be banished back to xoroth almost immediately. Now it's time to rest up, drink, buff, eat and so on. After you have had enough rest and everyone is ready, you can use the xorothian glyphs to pull the dreadsteed into the circle. It's a level 62 elite horse, but it isn't very hard. It has a nice kickback and does some decent damage, but nothing to worry about, much easier than Immol'thar himself and his eyes. After a while of fighting the steed (the steed will be around 70%-50% of its health), it's master, Lord Hel'nurath (I think), will spawn. Continue killing the steed with preferably your tank, tanking the lord. Once the steed is down, talk to it to finish your quest in case your party goes down. The Lord drops some decent loot too, so the effort wasn't completely worthless for the others helping. And to be honest, this quest is one of the most exciting I ever did, and most fun to do. My party members also said this was really, really fun ) And after this event, enjoy your mount!

Comment5: I was a bit worried about this coming because of the above comments.&nbsp Turns out, this quest is extremely easy.&nbsp I bought the 3 charge thing for 6 gold and only ever used one charge of it.&nbsp When I went into Jaedenar, it was a full spawn.&nbsp I aggroed everything up to the keep entrance then just used one charge of the potion.&nbsp Ran down to the oozes.&nbsp Once you are on the high ground right before the oozes, you can see there is a lip or ledge or whatever you want to call it that you want to jump on to bypass them.&nbsp Near the left wall, there is some junk on the ground.&nbsp You can jump on that, then from that, jump onto the lip (ledge thing).&nbsp Once on that you can jump off near the wall into the sludge and bypass the oozes completely.&nbsp From there I went ahead and located the guy I was going to end up killing, then went and talked to Lord Banehollow, then went back to the guy needing to be killed.&nbsp The two mobs outside will aggro regardless of where you are when you finish talking to the guy. This fight was much more simple than I had anticipated.&nbsp I used the void as was recommended above.&nbsp Once they aggroed, I ae taunted on void and dotted the main guy up.&nbsp I then terrored and shadowbolt the named.&nbsp He died while everything else was still feared.&nbsp I then proceeded to kill the other three with ease.&nbsp I did use deathcoil on one of the last three and had to heal my void through one channel.&nbsp Finished that fight with void completely oom and about 25 percent health left and me at about 75 percent health left.&nbsp Never healed myself at all other than the deathcoil.&nbsp I then went back and talked to guy, talked to his apprentice and bought the dust for 150g then ran out.&nbsp By the time I got out of Jaedenar I still had 5 minutes left on the first charge.&nbsp So, the entire thing, including running through keep took only 15 minutes. BTW on the way out (if your hearth is down as mine was) you can bypass the oozes the same way, as there is some junk you can jump on to get up on the ledge on this side as well. Hope this helps bring everything together for those who are about to attempt this and aids you in your travels.&nbsp Good Luck!

Comment2: I got mine right when I hit 30, soloed the whole thing. Here's how to do it: 1) get the quest from the warlock trainer (stormwind for alliance, orgrimmar for horde) 2) go to ratchet. The first time I went, I went to Menethil and took the boat to Theramore, and then swam north right on the edge of the ocean. It takes a while, but unending breath makes it much easier, just&nbsp put your char on auto run and steer him once in a while. Just be sure to stay well clear of the higher lvl mobs. Once you get close to ratchet you can go to shore, there are some pirates to the south and some other lower level mobs you can avoid or easily kill. Watch for horde here if you are pvp... there are usually a few stragglers here, 2 or three horde that range from their teens up to 30's and a couple 60's once in a while. 3) find the quest guy, he's across the main street up a the hill near the little tower. if you are standing ont he dock, the tower is to the right side of the main road in ratchet. 4) Once you get the next quest, wait for the boat on the dock. if there are horde, either hide and wait for them to leave, or run to the boat and hope you make it on before they kill you. once on the boat, you'll get rezed when it goes to booty bay, so either jump off or let them kill you again and just rez at the graveyard and walk to town. Get the flight path in booty bay and fly to IF. 5) Talk to the guy in the hall of explorers for the next part of the quest (sorry horde, don't know your half of this one) 6) The first half of the tome is up in Hillsbrad, west of southshore a ways on the beach. location is 27,72. I didn't have the flight path to southshore yet, so I flew to menethil and then hopped in the ocean for another swim north. stayed at the very edge of the ocean and just put it on autorun. There's some murlocks to dodge towards the end, but mostly a really easy swim. Comment2: You should be able to solo the quest without too much trouble. The hardest part is being able to get to a good place to find a doomguard captain alone. They are to the south of where you get the quest. It would be a good idea to get a Voidwalker out now. If you have an epic mount you can just ride though all of the mobs without too much trouble. Comment3: The hardest part about this quest is getting into the necessary position. It's difficult to explain but I will try. Before doing anything, make sure to take off your gear- you can die ALOT trying this and you don't want to bother with repair bills. Basically, beginning at the entrance to the Tainted Scar (you shouldsee 3/4 elite arranged in front of you) you are going to move straight forward towards the west which will be taking you in the direction of some hills/mountains. Now you should see a narrow-ish path leading up these hills/mountains with a guard off to its left and another further off on the right- you won't need to worry about the right, just wait until the left has pathed as far as away as possible and then get up the path. Moving up the path you should see a few small hills on your left, move up onto these and start making your way South/Southwest along them. You will know if you are in the right area if there is a group of 2 Doomguards and a Dreadlord all standing together on your RIGHT side. Now, when you have the group on your right, you should be facing some steep slopes (Still being south/southwest). You can get over these but it will take some work- don't give up- just keep trying to run up the slopes as far as possible, turning slowly in either direction until you find the right path upward and over them. You should now have that group I mentioned (the doomguards/dreadlord) behind you. The rest is fairly simple. Dismount, put on WALK, and move in the same direction you have been, bearing to your left. You should make your way alongside a steep hill and shortly see a single, lonely doomguard. He has no friends to help him out. There you go. I did this by having a healthstone/pot ready, as well as being DM specced and 1. using a VW sacrifice 2. using Fel Domination -while- I had my VW shield still up and summoning a second VW to sacrifice again during the fight. Basically I had a second shield on hand. Now the DG will just stand there or even wander around normally for the first 3-4 seconds of channeling, and then come at you head on. Don't bother trying to draw off Aggro w/ your VW because it won't work. The only way the DG can interrupt you is with a war stomp- and if he does that then I'd recommend just dying and retrying because it'll be very difficult to restart channeling and begin again whe he's already in your face. If you're not DM specced that's fine, you can still sac. one VW and then summon another- you'll just have less time to go on your first VW shield, but they only last for 4-5 hits anyway. Also note: the crystal only channels for 15/20 seconds, but it will be 2-3 seconds AFTER it has finished channeling that the DG will turn into the crystal you need and can pick up. So if your crystal finishes channeling but the DG kills you in those last few seconds, don't worry and don't send in a GM ticket because nothing is wrong- it's just lame like that. Also remember to PICK UP THE CRYSTAL- it is fairly small and easily missed if you're too eager to race back to the quest giver. I hope this helps anyone out who had as much trouble as I did. =] Also to note- if you don't want to solo this quest and you don't want to find this singled-out DG then I would recommend a raid of 10 or more. Yall can say what you want about those demon elites, but a 5-man group won't likely cut it unless you are very geared out. They do blast waves for nearly 1k dmg, hit very hard and have a large amount of health. Basically the juiced up equivalent of Onyxia Warders if you've ever fought those. I tried getting a large group of 10 for them and it was slow-going. Anyway, good luck and have fun summoning the DG. It's not really practical but fun to summon randomly.

Progress: It took me many years to collect the pieces of the orb of Zargain, but it has served me well, as I am sure the orb of Soran'ruk will serve you.
Comment1: The Three small shards in Black Fathom Deeps: Ashenvale coordinates 14:15 Follow the cave all the way back to the instance, then you will have to get to the last stage right before you kill the nasty hydra boss. Special note: dont click on the alter if you decide to go ahead and kill the hydra for drops.... it will kill you and send you back outside the instance to the beginning where you drop down to go into the caves. The Large Shard in Silverpine: Silverpine coordinates 45:68 Entering instance, turn right, free the prisoner and enter the courtyard. The large shard should drop from a haunted survivor or one of the shadowfangs that are near the ramp area. Since I play alliance, and it was difficult for me to find silverpine to begin with... from Iron forge, go north into the wetlands, from there, into arathi to south shore. from south shore, go north towards hillbrad and into silverpine... 90% of the mobs along this quest are elite. bring a party, or go at a higher level (I completed this at level 33, when it was green)
Comment2: This one is not easy, esp. if you're Alliance. Why? Hard to get groups in these dungeons. And you need groups (unless the quest has gone gray to you). I did the bfd part 20 lvls ago and had this quest (and those items) on me for ages. Finally went over to SFK last night just to finish this off (at lvl 44). Sorry, I forogt what dropped the quest items in bfd - I think it was the humanoids back in the maze/temple area. Acolytes or something. In SFK you take the small door to the right after you enter and fight your way to the jail cells. Just keep going and you'll find it. Free the wizard, and he'll open the door to the courtyard for you. There you clear until you can cross, ahead and to your right, to the ramp up. Fight up the ramp, and you enter a series of rooms. Here there are Shadowfang Darksouls. These drop the large soran fragment you need, only my first time through - it never dropped. I had to exit, group w/ someone, de-group (this reset the instanc) - and fight my way back to the darksouls again. Second time it dropped. The werewolves w/ 'moon' in their name (in the courtyard) - when their hands glow green - are about to gain an 'invulnerability to magic' effect. It lasts 5 to 10 seconds, then fades. Even if you land dots before this, the dots don't harm them when this is up. If you pull w/ shadowbolts and can take the punishment, they are not immune while they charge u. U can get 3 shadowbolts into them (at least) if you pull w/ one and shoot as they close and start hitting you. The darksouls are immune to shadow damage. You have to immolate them and either melee or use a non-shadow wand on them.
Comment3: This is for those who have Cosmos' Atlas. Enter the instance and immediately turn right.&nbsp Work your way around to point 1 on the atlas, where 'Deathstalker Adamant' and 'Sorcerer Ashcrombe Rethilgore'.&nbsp Release the prisoner and he'll open the door to the courtyard. Comment1: I soloed this as a level 70 affliction / demonology warlock without too many trouble. Here's a little guide: Go to the back entrance of Dire Maul in Feralas. The location is shown on the map Burgermeal posted, and it's pretty hard to miss. Just look for a structure with the same design as Dire Maul and head through the tunnel. When you're there, either open the door with the Crescent Key or Life Tap / Hellfire and revive your spirit at the other side of the door. When inside the instance, you'll see you skipped the entire elemental area of Dire Maul East and are at the demons you need straight away. Your Voidwalker is the one you'll love in here. First, you see two plants which aren't linked. Just pull them, drain tank a bit and they'll die without too many problems. Time for the real work now. In the area you'll find a couple of patrols which you'll want to pull first. They're not much stronger than a regular level ~68 mob, so you'll hardly have trouble with them. If you've cleared some patrols, it's time for the packs. Stick your Voidwalker on one Satyr, banish the Betrayer and DoT + drain tank the other Satyr. When your mob is down, kill the mob the Voidwalker is tanking and then kill the Betrayer which should be unbanished by now. This tactic will allow you to clear most of the area you need and should provide you with sufficient Satyr Bloods to complete the quest. Judging by the comments in this thread, many people seem to think there's also packs of four demons. This, however, is [b]not[/b] the case. If you see a group of four demons, you'll see a normal group (of three demons) and a patrol. Just wait a second for the patrol to leave and do the normal routine. It might take a while for the patrol to leave, so don't bother trying four mobs at once (although it's probably possible), just head for another group or a patrol that isn't near a group. The droprate wasn't that high for me, so I actually had to reset the instance once and kill one or two more packs. It took me around 1,5 hours to complete this quest. Because I was in the demon area of DM East anyway, I figured it would be nice to try some bosses there, just for laughs. The first boss you'll encounter is Lethtendris who has an imp minion beside her. Just send your Voidwalker in, kill the imp (couple of DoT's and 1 or 2 shadow bolts should do) and then just Health Funnel your Voidwalker. If you have Siphon Life, keep it up to gain some extra health. I haven't tried drain tanking so I have no idea if that's actually possible, I just did it the safe way and do very slow DPS (the Siphon Life and sometimes a bit of wanding). You could also put an (amplified) Curse of Doom up, to speed things up a little without pulling aggro too soon of your Voidwalker. Once Lethtendris is dead, you can go downstairs and use exactly the same tactic on Hydrospawn. Both dropped a green for me, so I didn't actually profit from it, but it was quite fun, I guess... Anyway, once you're done with this quest, and the Prison's Casing quest, head back to the questgiver in Blasted Land and do the final part. Good luck!

Comment1: After much trial and much more errors, I have come upon a tactic that can help you beat this quest. 1: Find the camp. It's hard to kill Jack if you can't find him. If you need help, read all the posts above this one. 2: Kills those wolves and Defias around the camp. You do not want them to be accidently aggro'd in the fight against Jack. Trust me. It has happened to me. And make sure you kill that one guard to the right of Jack without aggro'ing him. That would be bad. 3: After you kill all those pesky guards and wolves, charge at Jack's lone guard and kill him. You might be wondering, 'Why the guard? Why not Jack himself?' Simple. I found out the hard way that Jack has an insanely fast respawn time. So fast that you can see him walk on his own corpse. While you're fighting the guard, you might want to throw in a thunder clap in there somewhere to slow Jack's attacks. 4: After you killed the guard, hamstring Jack and run the heck away. Since you already killed all those defias and wolves, nothing will interfere will your running away. Also, you might want to switch into Defensive stance here just to be safe. 5: Did you get away from Jack? You did? Great! Now rest up and go back there and kill him. 5b: Did you get away from Jack? You didn't? Oh well. At least you'll be fighting Jack one-on-one now. So get res'd and go kill him! 6: After you kill him, spit on him for making you go through so much pain and agony. Ok, this step may not be necessary, but I think everyone is going to do it nonetheless. 7: Get the key off of Jack and unlock the box. Take the badge. 8: Turn the quest in. 9: Be happy. You just beaten this annoying as hell quest.

Comment5: Had help in RFM from a lvl60 friend b/c I knew by the time I got to RFM at lvl35, the armor would be obsolete.&nbsp Prefer SM over this place anyway. The guy who wrote the directions as taking the left fork, then taking the vine bridge, and finding the quest target just past the cauldron was dead on accurate. Some tips for Alliance: Pick up Retrieval for Mauren (https://classicdb.ch/quest=1078 6 crystallized scales, as you may be killing these Basilisks that get in your way). He's in one of the curved pathways in the SW mage quarter. Basilisks drop Crystallized Scales you need for this quest. These buggers will probably get in the way, so might as well get this quest. You pass by about 4-5 before you get to the vale, might as well start killing them. While going thru Windshear Crag, follow the west side and you'll find a hut with a goblin.&nbsp Get the quest Super Reaper 6000 (https://classicdb.ch/quest=1093) and go back to the big stationary machine, climb up and kill the Operators, they should drop the plans. If no, there are other Operators in the area that will. There is a limited supply vendor just north of the goblin hut, he's standing in a crevace and it's easy to miss him. He may have something of use, otherwise you can use him to sell your vendor trash if you are grinding in the area. Turn in the quest back at the hut and get the next quest which you just talk to a goblin near the FP in Ratchet. Since I have you going to Ratchet anyway, might as well get some XP while you're getting your FP (Flight Path). When you get to the main road outside the Crag, go north to get the FP. Pick up quest Reclaiming The Charred Vale (https://classicdb.ch/quest=1057 while at the peak). It's a harpy grind/kill quest. They'll be getting in your way so you might as well knock out a quest while you are at it. There may be other quests in the Vale but I don't know/can't remember any. When I first went thru the Vale in my mage, I was wondering why those Chimera weren't part of any quest I had (It's warrior quest target). The fiery elementals occasionally drop Elemental Fire. So may be worth it to kill them instead of avoid them. The stone elementals may drop elemental earth. I believe these were the first elementals to drop that item. For Alliance, while you are in the Charred Vale, I recommend to go ahead and run the gauntlet and get your FP to Nigel's Point in Desolace so you don't have to go back thru there. The exit is at the opposite end of the Vale and you're going to be there anyway finding the Matriarch. From Nigel's Point, fly back to Stonetalon Peak [turn in your quest] then run all the way back south thru Stonetalon Mountains and enter the Barrens from the south exit of Stonetalon Mountains. Run across the Barrens going east, and get your FP for Ratchet. Take the ship across the ocean and get your FP to Booty Bay. Head back to Ratchet and start making your way down to RFM. If you have high level help, they can fly into BB or Ratchet and meet you at RFM. After flying back to Stonetalon Peak, you get another quest that sends you down into 1K Needles. Once you are done in RFM, go south down the lift into 1K Needles. The Tauren guard chased me on the lift but LOL he fell! By the time I got to the bottom he was miraculously running back up the vertical wall p&nbsp Run NW to the end of 1K needles and turn in the quest [he releases spirits, you get XP], get the FP, sell vendor trash, then back thru 1K Needles, to shimmering flats. Head south and get your FP in Gadgetzan. Yes I do love having my FPs! Once you get back to Stormwind to pick up your armor, you can also turn in your quest to Mauren. I like the XP reward, but Kind of disappointed by the armor, I have been using Shining Silver Breastplate 214 armor, +14 STR +6 STA (https://classicdb.ch/item=3502)&nbsp which I had crafted awhile ago. On my server can usu be had for 3G since there's a good oversupply. I will hang onto it as it's good tanking armor for an instance. As far as the Spider Fangs in the wetlands, mine the Incendicite Ore as you can turn that in for a quest reward, if you are a miner. The Spider's Silk you get can be auctioned for about 1G per silk [depending on market conditions]! Useful to tailors and leatherworkers. You'll get from 1-6 during the spider part of your quest, don't just vendor this off! It's worth alot more than the higher level Shadow Silk and Thick Spider's Silk, because the drop is so uncommon. For you miners, there is at least TWO veins of MITHRIL ore. Mine these first, then they will repop as you are questing. One is on the east edge of the Vale, the other is kind of in the middle on a little hill. You'll find a few iron veins while going thru 1K needles.

Instructions: Kill Big Will, then speak to Klannoc Macleod on Fray Island. Step on the grate to begin the Affray
Progress: N/A
Comment1: Nasty comments from some posters aside, this is not that easy a quest, until you figure it out.&nbsp The attackers don't behave like normal mobs, is the problem, so what you would do in normal situations is the wrong thing to do here. As noted earlier, they do run when you use Demoralizing Shout HOWEVER, it's NOT a good idea to spam DS and keep them running, because if you do, the others will spawn and attack and you'll end up fighting five at once. You may need to use this ability once, if pressed and low on health.&nbsp But don't spam it. The key is that after each fight, the next attackers won't spawn unless you're fairly close to the grate.&nbsp If you hang around on the grate in the middle of the circle after stepping on it, you can't win this fight.&nbsp (Well, unless you have a priest buddy standing by to heal you or something.) Step on the grate to activate the quest.&nbsp A few seconds go by before the first attacker spawns.&nbsp use those seconds to put a little distance between you and the circle of spectators. The first attacker is level 26.&nbsp Piece of cake.&nbsp After he's dead, eat or bandage to return to full health.&nbsp Then approach the grate.&nbsp Two attackers will go at you at once, again low levels so not too hard.&nbsp But STEP BACK after they spawn!&nbsp You want some time between this fight and the third one.&nbsp Again, return to full health before approaching the grate.&nbsp You get hit by 3 attackers the third round.&nbsp This one's tougher, although they're still a few levels below you, and this is where you might need to use the DS trick and bandage partway through. Polish off those three, and you'll see Big Will come into the circle.&nbsp This one you have to go up and attack.&nbsp As mentioned, he's level 33, but there's nothing special about him.&nbsp I beat him without using Retaliation (I'd used it against the trio earlier).&nbsp The earlier fights were actually harder. I failed this quest twice before finishing it, the first time by staying in the circle, and the second time by following the bonehead advice above and spamming DS.&nbsp But once you figure it out, it's doable solo at 30.

Comment1: Okay, here's the run down of the lvl20 warrior quest (Alliance side). There are two things you need to know about this quest, firstly is that this is a LOOOONG series of quests and will take you about a day to complete (if you do them all). Secondly is that [b]YOU CANNOT DO THESE SOLO.[/b] Unfortunately for most they only realise this when they are further down the line, the mobs that you need to kill for the Fire Hardened armor quests are lvl28+. However, if you do manage to complete all the quests then at the end you will end up with: [url=/item=6970]Furen's Favor (shield)[/url] [url=/item=6972]Fire Hardened Hauberk (chest)[/url] [url=/item=6973]Fire Hardened Leggings (legs)[/url] [url=/item=6971]Fire Hardened Coif (head)[/url] [url=/item=6974]Fire Hardened Gauntlets (gloves)[/url] Note: The only stuff really useful in the above list is the Hauberk, I myself was using it mid to late 30s because not much drops thats better than this. Green Iron Hauberk (smithy crafted) is what I upgraded to when I could make it. Also, the Fire Hardened items [b]are not[/b] a set so there are no extra bonuses. [u]Quest 1: Yorus Barleybrew[/u] Simple enough. To pick up this quest talk to Wu Shen the Warrior Trainer in Stormwind, Old Town district near the SI:7 building. From here he will give you this quest and send you to Redridge, Lakeshire Inn to talk to Yorus. [url=/quest=1699]Quest 2: The Rethban Gauntlet[/url] This quest can be easy or hard, its luck of the draw. You have to run into a cave then get back without being killed. The cave is in the North West of Redridge, head West from Lakeshire until you hit the mountains then follow them North past a Gnoll Camp. You head round the corner at a big rock and into the cave, 10 secs into the cave you come to a fork and you get the 'Complete' message and then have to run back. If you die then you have to start the quest again by talking to Yorus. Sometimes if someone has been questing then all the Gnolls in the area are dead. This IS soloable. You have an hour to do the run, which is a ridiculous amount of timem I've ran it there and back and completed the quest in 3 mins. You dont have to rush, you can kill your way to the cave instead of running past them and aggroing everything. When you've completed the quest he gives you a quick hip hip hooray and then gives you the next quest. [url=/quest=1702]Quest 3: The Shieldsmith[/url] Here you have to head back to Stormwind and talk to Furen Longbeard and give him the Cask that Yorus gave you. He's located in the Dwarven District by the main forge. When you complete the quest you will get the [url=/item=6970]Furen's Favor[/url] shield. He will then give you your next quest. [url=/quest=1701]Quest 4: Fire Hardened Mail[/url] Now comes the hard part, here you are going to need help from a guildie, a friend or a anyone who can solo Razorfen Kraul in The Barrens. Furen gives you a list of ingredients to make the Fire Hardened Hauberk: 1) [url=/item=6838]50x Scorched Spider Fang[/url] 2) [url=/item=6839]12x Charred Horn[/url] 3) [url=/item=6840]1x Galvanized Horn[/url] 4) [url=/item=6841]1x Vial of Phlogiston[/url] 1) The Scorched Spider Fangs drop from the Cave Stalker/Leech Stalker spiders (lvl 16-22) outside and inside the cave near Dun Algaz in ther Wetlands (the tunnel leading from Loch Modan to the Wetlands). This is pretty much the only part of the quest you can solo. 2) The Charred Horns drop from Fledgling Chimaera (lvl 20 - 27) and Young Chimaera (lvl 19 - 25) in the Charred Vale in Stonetalon (North West of The Barrens) near the southern point of the Vale before going into Desolace. Quite a busy are with lots of mobs. 3) The Galvanized horn drops from The Chimaera Matriarch (lvl 26 - 28) who is in the same area, she flies around on a flight path near the Chimaera so you should come across her sooner or later. 4) The Vial of Phlogiston is located on Roogug (lvl 27 - 28 ELITE) who is one of the sub bosses in Razorfen Kraul (Instance to the south of the Barrens before the Great Lift leading to Thousand Needles). [b]BE CAREFUL! There are TWO instances right across from each other, Razorfen Kraul and Razornfen Downs[/b], facing the lift you want RFK which is on your right (the West instance on the zone map). When in the instance finding Roofug can be tricky, if my directions are right then as you enter the dungeon take your first left, follow the path around and follow it over a big long vine that take you to an uper level. You should come to a place with a big cauldron, he's just around the corner. Its hard to find groups for RFK as it is (Alliance side), so you prolly are gonna need someone who can solo the instance. Note: Easiest way to The Barrens is to either get a boat from Menethil (Wetlands) to Theramore Isle (Dustwallow Marsh) then run west into The Barrens. Alternatively you can run south from Darkshirt into Stranglthorn Vale, head along the road to the very south (prolly only thing attacking you will be a few tigers and gorrillas near the paths, but nothing SHOULD kill you). Head to Booty Bay then catch the ship to Ratchett which is in the Barrens. Once you have all the ingrediants then return to Furen and he will make you the Firehardened Hauberk (he will make it then you have to talk to him again to recieve it). Now its been a while since I've done this next bit so I cant remember whether Furen tells you to go and talk to the next three people, or whether they just become activated after you complete the quest. It seems like you get given Furen's Notes for another quest giver which is determined by your chars race, either way this leads you to another three quests (which you can do in any order as long as you have completed the Fire Hardened Hauberk quest, but I have given them in order of conveniance to get to). Comment4: There are a few tricks to make this quest easier for you and your group. First, clear the trash mobs out of the yard in front of Grark's stronghold FIRST, then get in there and defeat him fast. They will not have respawned by the time you bring him out. When you are walking with him towards the mountain, do not walk directly on top of him, stay somewhat to his [b]left[/b]. By doing this, you will be able to avoid the unrelated camps of mobs he will walk through. This isn't an ordinary escort quest he WON'T aggro non-quest mobs if your party doesn't come in their range. He's one of the bad guys, he's friends with all these mobs! The only mobs you have to fight are the ones that he spawns himself. The first few groups he spawns are easy if you have a full party, because he stands still for them. But when you get up on the ramp, for the last couple of groups he will continue walking. You must pay attention to this and continue moving with him even as you're fighting the mobs. Don't get distracted. If he gets too far ahead of you, the quest will fail. If you're having a hard time and you play on a PvE server, try doing the quest during peak time when many people are hanging around the mountain. The mobs aren't particular about who they attack, and several times while we were doing the quest some of them got trained away by people trying to help, or just innocent bystanders. This will help you, not hurt you (though it will hurt the people who get jumped by the elites!).

Comment4: The quest isn't too hard to solo as a level 60 rogue. I think any other class would need a full party. I used nightscape boots to help with the stealth, I highly recommend them for this trip. Also, you'll want to have 300 lockpicking (though I don't know if you need it at 300, that's what I had) From the entrance, go straight between the two guards and into the courtyard. Be very careful, there are patrols with dogs doing circles. The guards won't see you, but if you're not careful the dogs will. The place you want to head is at your 2 o'clock position. As you get closer, you'll see the little jail cages suspended from chains. Follow the corrodor, avoiding dogs and patrols. Your minimap will show Windsor up as the little yellow dot we've all come to know and love. It should lead you to a cell that is guarded by three dwarves and a dog. Here's the tricky part. You have to get rid of the guards to pick the lock on the door to get to Windsor. The way I did it was to sap one of the guards, kill the dog and vanish. Wait for cooldowns, sap a guard, kill the other two guards (thank you blade flurry) and vanish again. Finally kill the last guard. The guards run, so use crippling poison. I had some epics in my gear which made life easier I suspect though it could be managed with just blues, just brind blinding powder and maybe a healing potion or two. When you leave the instance, make sure you don't reset it. Once you turn in the quest, the chain will continue till you get the crumpled note. That note will mean another trip back to Windsor and since the respawn rate in BRD is very, very slow, if you do them quickly you will come back and find the guards still dead. Good luck!

Basically, you go in BRD arena, and as soon as you see the yell 'your sentence is death bla bla bla', use the Banner of Provocation at the midde of the arena. Your group will have to kill the first wave, like any BRD arena. Then, Theldren will come with his friends to kick your asses, in place of regular random boss. They are 5, and this battle is pvp-ish. They are [b]IMMUNE[/b] againt Taunt, Challenging Shout, Mocking blow etc. They are still under the effect of skills like fade, feint etc. They are all elites, but their HP are equal to epic geared buffed people (so around 7-10k HP, not more), their armor are quite the same as their blue geared class. Except the aggro skills, theses guys can be afflicted with ANY sort of skills/spells (root, sheep, fear, etc) their setup is random, but there aren't more than 2 guys of the same class (the following list may be uncomplete, i shall try more than thrice and update the list soon) -Warrior : Theldren the dwarf in valor, with an arcanite reaper. -Mages : Undead (Volida) / Qilboar (Snokh Blackspine) -Chaman : Tauren (Korv) -Hunter : Centaur with a non elite Hyena as a Pet (Hunter : Malgen Longspear / Pet : Gnashjaw) -Rogues : Gnome (Lefty) / Gnoll (Rotfang) -Priest : Troll (Va'jashni) -Special : Gobelin Engineer (Reznik) Basically, it's completely random : you will always have Theldren as the warrior, but you can have 2 mages and 2 rogues with him, or 1 of each classes. (the pattern is completely random too, you can have the same guys at a second attempt, or not) Don't Underestimate them because of their HP and armor (really player-like), they can kick your asses, just like you can. *Theldren : he is pretty annoying... He spam [b]Mortal Strike[/b] (like any cookie cutter warrior), he loves to intercept your cloth buddies, and doesn't hesitate to use Intimidating shout. *Mages : they use frostbolt, flamestrike, frost nova, Blizzard [b] and even sheep ![/b]. Theses guys should be killed ASAP (you won't love them when they sheep your healers) *Rogues : pretty annoying : they love stunlock people (yes, kidney shot and all). they CAN vanish (and then use ambush/cheap shot against you). *Chaman : like any chaman would do, this guy spam totems (especially [b]earthbind totem[/b] and [b]fire nova totem[/b] -_-), and the infamous [b]frost shock[/b]... (fortunately, he doesn't seem to have Reincarnation) *Hunter : the centaur changes his target whenever he feels he has to (his range is huge). He can use Aimed shot, multi Shot, Arcane shot, and even Feign death + frost trap. His pet is tauntable, like any in pvp (the pet doesn't have anything special tough) *Priest : all of you know that priests should be killed on sight in pvp, that rule is applied here too : he has psychic scream, flash heal, greater heal, Power Word : Shield and Shadow Word : Pain. But, he is easy to kill, really *Special Gobelin : if you met already the goblins in BWL, this guy is somewhat their cousin : like any bombs maniac, he throws dark iron bombs etc to anyone within range. As a gobelin, he uses indeed the dragon breath trinket, and even the Arcanite Dragonling as a pet. he is not too dangerous, but the fireworks add more chaos in this encounter :D hints : you should have 2 sorts of Crowd Control. Use sheep on theldren : you don't want him to MS everyone and using intercept and intimindating shout (and battle shout, which increases his buddies melee damage, and that is kinda dangerous with 1-2 rogues around) If you get 1-2 rogues, try to fear/stun them. Now that you have less problems, just act like in pvp : chop the clothies up, then the chamy, following the hunter/gobelin. Finally, the rogues and finish the job by killing Theldren (he is a piece of cake alone) You have to kill [b]all of them[/b], don't espect them to not respawn if you wipe, they will. With some practice, this encounter is quite easy, but really fun (pretty weird to do some pvp, in pve. and they really seem to be real player! (except they have a lack of assist)) oh, by the way : when you beat them, there will be a chest 'arena spoils' : you will have a BOP/BOE blue (if you are lucky, you can loot an epic) and the final note : the Banner of Provocation isn't an unique use, it has a cooldown of 10 minutes. You CAN repeat that encounter, so you can farm some blue :D Have fun (hoping this little guide will help some of you) Edited, Wed Apr 5 09:07:09 2006

Comment1: After opening the cell of Commander Gor'shak, you will be able to turn in the previous quest in this chain. The commander will then offer you this quest. DO NOT ACCEPT IT until everyone in your group has had a chance to turn in the previous step. Accepting this quest will cause eight low-50 elites tospawn in the hallway, rush into the cell and begin to kill the unarmed and unarmored Commander Gor'shak, which makes you fail the quest. The best way to stop them from doing this is to never let them into the cell at all, so turn in the first quest and then go back out of the cell. Only one person has to be in the cell to activate this quest, everyone nearby will get an accept box stating 'So-and-so is starting 'What is going on?, would you like to as well?'. Everyone accept, and the person who triggered it steps outside to rejoin the party. The Elites will spawn in the hallway and begin rushing towards the cell. Have your warrior do an AE taunt, then pile on the area effect spells. A frost mage who can kite and Ice block is invaluable here, as you have a long hallway that has been recently cleared to play in. Ice traps outside the cell are needed if you choose to attempt the crowd control and tank it out route, but the sheer number of attackers makes it difficult for your 5 man group. Remember to keep Gor'shak alive and you'll be ok.
Comment2: This is a tough fight.&nbsp We tried to win this 4 times previously trying to fight _in_ the cell.&nbsp Due to close quarters, and the cleaves that all the elites use, Gor'Shak dies in seconds. Our plan was to use fears to break up the attacks. We cleared the hallway top to bottom to prevent adds. Then, our warlock started the script while the rest of us waited outside the cell. I Intimidating Shouted them first and we DPSed the 1st target. Fortunately Gor'Shak focused on this target.&nbsp By the time the rest returned, we were ready.&nbsp The warlock feared them, and Gor'Shak (thankfully), went after a lone runner. We caught up with them and DPS'ed that target quickly. Our group consisted of the following 1 Warrior 2 Paladins 1 Priest (me) 1 Warlock 3 Rogues 1 Mage 1 Hunter Almost all players had some tier 2 and a good amount of tier 1. The lock and occasionally the hunter focused on burning his mana. This is very important as when he has mana he seems to heal himself. Our mage also hit him with improved counter spell whenever possible. After 40% stage 1 ends and it is an easy fight as it is just a matter of DPSing him down and keeping the main tank up. Vent was very helpful as we could call out when we were being stunned so that no one died due to being stunned for the full 8 seconds. Even with this strat it was not easy and did not go perfectly. I died just as stage 1 ended as he hit me with a shadow bolt that did 4700 damage. Our tank died when Valthalak had about 10K health remaining as our palies were out of mana. Comment5: 1 prot tank - tanking him. 1 fury warr - dps and for staggered disarm. 2 disc/holy priests. 2 shammies. 1 hunter. 1 druid. 2 mages. Two groups, one in the SW corner, one in the SW corner. Tank and DPS warr in center. Everyone was well geared, 5 man blues, and some had epics from ZG. Took three tries, this was the first time for everyone on this and only the main priest (who was doing the quest) knew about the fight. Spent some time talking about it in vent. It would have been a lot better for more to have read about this fight first. First attempt - 46%, we had the 2 shammies doing mele dps and totems for warr. Mistake, not enough mele killing for the adds that went right for the casters, hunter had dead zone issues and our group was burning him down way too fast and mana users were going OOM. Once one of the priests went down from the adds, then the dps warr went down from the adds. Then adds all over the place, a lot of folks stunned = wipe. Good learning exp. Second attempt - 27%. Moved the shammies back with the casters, they did a good job on the adds but went OOM too fast. DPS warr killed all adds that stayed by the tank or by him (about 1/4 of the adds stay up there) - again we lost the 2nd priest. Both tank and DPS warr did disarm at the same time so we&nbsp failed to stagger it - mele dmg was too much causing OOM on remaining healer, once stage 3 hit (we were not really expecting it until 20% but we got the shadow dmg starting at 30%), the shadow dmg was crazy, dps war (me) took almost 4k in a few secs, and went down, rest of group took him down a few more percent. Another wipe. Third attempt. This time the shammies rank reduced their spells (conserve mana), use aoe totems. One wind fury totem for the warrs by them, mana spring for the casters. DPS war took care of all adds near him. Stage 1 no prob - everyone be ready to kill adds, don�t worry about max dps on him, slow and steady works a lot better. Stage 2, warriors staggered disarm, 30 secs apart worked really well. Still conserving mana - this is not the time for the all out attack, we were in good shape. Folks except tank use bandage if necessary to conserve mana. Stage 3 hit, fury war went down around at the 20% point from shadow dmg, healers caught tank just in time. It was close, tank died at 7% and remaining died as they use their last spells/abilities. 3 were left standing at end, killing blow was from mage wand with the remaining completly mana drained and almost dead. Now that we have done it, here are some notes on what we will do next time someone needs it. Start off with everyone taking shadow protection pots before fight starts - they will make a huge difference (wait a bit until you are out of the cooldown for mana/health pots). Just have tank and dps warr by him every else as far away as range attacks/healing allows. The shadow dmg appears to jump and increase so you dont want many mele near him when stage 3 hits. Have shammies/rogues ready to kill adds by casters by downranking spells and aoe totems. Hunter and lock (if you have one) keep him mana drained (hard, he has one heck of a tick regen). DPS warr must be ready to kill any adds by tank instantly, hunter kill those that stun the dps warr and/or tank. Vent is really needed to communicate stuns. Go slow, take your time, everyone but tank and healer on tank worry mainly about the adds and dps him when you can but be ready to break off for the adds instantly. The adds each have around about 450hp(?) they go down easy - you just have to do it fast. Arcane explosion from mages will work but cost mana. Mana pot early, this is a long fight, and you will most likely be able to pot again in stage 3. For the DPS warr, the adds you kill will be easy to get, they are right by ya - whirlwind works great here - once down back to dps on him. Note that I tried thunderclap and piercing howl and they don't interrupt the adds, they continue to life drain. The adds are not tauntable - they are there simply to life drain someone. Right when he gets to 50% make sure the tank and dsp warr are fully healed. PW:Shield the tank, and tank blow shield wall when you see him pull out his wep BEFORE you take the first hit. Tank and dps warr stagger disarm so you can disarm him every 30 secs. Healers will need to really focus on that tank, he is taking a lot of dmg. Tank do the tank thing, spam shield block every time it is up. A prot tank should not have any problems here holding aggro with a good group. Folks in corners no longer need to worry about adds and the dps will really start to take him down fast.&nbsp Folks can bandage if they need heals left over from the stage 1 � don�t have healers waste mana on renews if you are 1/2 health or higher � just do a fast 8 sec HR bandage. Make sure you are FULLY healed before stage 3 hits or the shadow will melt ya face. Stage 3, get ready for big time shadow dmg. Tank will need heavy healing. DPS warr now is the time for recklessness and death wish cause mostly likely you will die from the shadow soon - 2nd healer keep the dps warr up until the cooldowns are done then he is expendable. If your cooldowns pull aggro, just keep unloading until you either die or tank gets it back. Shammies can run in and mele now and shock when they have mana - healers let them die also - you MUST keep that tank up. This is an all out attack to burn him down before he kills you with his shadow dmg - thus the huge advantage shadow protection pots will give. Non mana mele, pot another shadow protection pot if the first one is gone from dmg instead of health pot. If you have the AB trinket, pop it for a free mini shield.&nbsp Prot tank do everything you can to hold aggro cause your team will be doing everything they can to take it away. Stance dance to battle for mocking blow if you have to&nbsp - you have been taking so much dmg from stage 2 you would have a full rage bar to work with. If you took care of the adds in stage 1 fast and conserved mana (via early potting) this final stage is an all out hella fun attack. Most importantly - have fun. We all had a blast, it is fun to be challenged with a hard fight and it feels great to walk away with victory (forget about the big repair bills). Heck of a great feeling with the cheers when he is down. I�m sure with practice he can be put on farm status and we are looking forward to the ones we can now summon in the other instances.
