Comment5: I just did this last night, successfuly, and figured a better walkthrough of the entire event would've helped me not waste a few hours of my life. Enjoy. 1. The very first step of creating the UBRS keys is to gather these 4 items from LBRS - Unadorned Seal of Ascension: random drop from mobs in LBRS - Gemstone of Spirestone: random drop from Highlord Omokk - Gemstone of Smolderthorn: random drop from War Master Voone - Gemstone of Bloodaxe: random drop from Overlord Wyrthmalak 2. Once you have these 4 items, you must turn them into Vaelan in LBRS. He's located at the top of the slope that is right before the first wooden bridge. If you go to the very top of that slope, look left, you'll see a single orc at the very end of that flat area. That's Vaelan in disguise. He will transform back to his normal self when you get close. Speak with him. He says a few things and eventually lets you complete the 4 item Seal of Ascension quest. You now should get another Seal of Ascension quest which sends you to Dustwallow Marsh. Vaelan gives you a box containing (1) Orb of Draconic Energy and (1) Unforged Seal of Ascension. Both of these items have 5 charges which equates to 5 chances at getting your Unforged Seal, Forged. If you fail all 5 times you will have to go Gem hunting again. 3. Get a group of 5 or so capable people and head to Dustwallow Marsh. The quest, Seal of Ascension, describes how you must find the ancient drake known as Emberstrife and use him to forge your seal. The cave that this named 59-61 elite is in is located just south of Onyxias lair at the very southern part of Dustwallow Marsh. 4. Once your party has reached the cave where Emberstrife is located, go in and position yourself across from the plateau that he sits on. There should be a shallow lake between you and him. 5. Now the fun begins. What you're trying to accomplish here is to use Emberstrife to forge your Unforged Seal of Ascension. This is accomplished by a form of mind control, and using one of his abilities that pops up for you on the Unforged Seal. I'll detail this event. - Make sure whoever is doing the Quest is not tanking. You have to do a couple things that should not be interrupted. - Have someone with a ranged attack pull Emberstrife. Fight in the shallow lake as there can be issues with LOS and forging of the Seal. - When Emberstrifes health reaches around 25%, the person who has the Unforged Seal of Ascension needs to use that item. When used you will see a purple orb type object floating a little off of the ground. This is the Unforged Seal of Ascension. It will only last for a couple of minutes, so its best to use that item when he's around 20-25% health. - When Emberstrifes health reaches 10-15% everyone will see an orange emote stating 'Emberstrife's will is faltering'. At that time, everyone must stop attacking. I say again, stop attacking the drake. At the same time, the person who has the Orb of Draconic Energy needs to target Emberstrife and use the Orb. What this does is mind control the drake. - The person who used the Orb should now have total control over Emberstrife. Position Emberstrife so that he is facing that Unforged Seal of Ascension that you placed. You should also have a minibar that pops up just above your main bar that contains 4 different abilities. You want to use the very far left one which is 'Flame of the Black Dragonflight'. Making sure that Emberstrife is facing the Unforged Seal of Ascension, use that ability. If done correctly you will see an icy blue cloud spew from Emberstrife. If you put your mouse over the Seal, if done correctly, it should now say Forged Seal of Ascension. Also note, Emberstrife can only be mind controled for the duration of the channeling bar that pops up. You do have ample time to do the event, however, once that bar is gone, you have to repeat the battle again. - Once you have Forged the Seal, you can either right click on the mind control icon to cancel mind control or let the channeling bar run out. Once you return to your character finish Emberstrike and go right click on the Seal. You will receive the Forged Seal of Ascension at that point. - The last step is to return the Forged Seal of Ascension to Vaelan in LBRS. You then are given the Seal of Ascension which opens the door to UBRS. Congrats! Edited, Tue Jun 28 09:49:08 2005

Comment1: I'm sure almost every mage wants to do this quest. 4200 mana over 30 seconds is invalueble. Here's my attempt at a detailed decription on how to obtain and complete the quest. Navigating in Dire Maul (DM): There are 3 sections of DM (North, East and West). Only 2 sections concern this quest, which is North and East. The questgiver is in the North, and the quest item is from the East. You will need a Crescent key to enter the North instance or a rog with max lock picking skill (Engineers, I have already tried blowing the doors up. Didn't work). Upon entering DM from Feralas, you just need to follow the corridor till you reach a 'T' path (you will notice a huge double wooden door at the T - Only graphics, cannot be opened). To the sides of the door, there are two slip-in entries. Go through both of them and it will bring you into a courtyard with ogres. Hugging the right wall will take into the east instance, left to west and straight across the courtyard is north. Aggro range here is very small so its easy to slip past them. Dog patrols exist and they see through invis. Step 1: Obtaining a Crescent Key https://classicdb.ch/item=35607 This is gotten from the east instance (entering from the courtyard). Immediately entering the instance, you see a non-aggro imp on your left. Speak to him and he will start running. Fight your way in the direction he ran to (right of entering the instance). Speak to him again, and he starts running. It goes on for a couple of times. By hugging the right wall and killing everything in the way, enter the 2nd corridor (1st one takes&nbsp you out of the instance). Go all the way straight down the corridor downstairs and hug the right wall, killing everything in your way. Go upstairs and you should see the imp there again. Talking to him will trigger him to fight. He spawns little imps over time, so focus your dps on him and deal with the non-elite adds after. Loot the key. Step 2: Where's the questgiver? This can be done solo without any means of invis. Upon entering the north instance, there is a group of 3 ogres to your left and 1 wandering ogre infront of you. If you see the 3 ogres, you should also see a ramp down near them. Wait for the wanderer to move away and head down the ramp. Jump off the left side of the ramp to avoid the 2nd group of ogres, and head down another ramp. This will bring you to another door that needs the Crescent key. Through that, all the way, takes you to the library. Questgiver is straight ahead of you, 1st bookshelf to your left. Step 3: Getting the Hydrospawn Essence. Eastern instance, coming from courtyard zone-in, hug the right wall, through the 2nd corridor, 1st right into a hall filled with Satyr demons and plants. Kill your way along the left wall and take the left turn below the ramp. Kill along the left wall again and this will take you to a pool with hydrospawn in it. He spawns little water elementals as well, but they despawn when Hydrospawn dies. So focus dps on him again. Immune to cold. Step 4: Back to quest giver. Sorry if this seems a little long. But I didn't do any DM runs prior to this quest. I'm sure many fellow mages are alike. I hope this gives you more help than you need.

[b]Enter DM North[/b].&nbsp There is a left-right pathway overlooking a courtyard ahead of you.&nbsp There is a mob with dogs who walks down there (in a circle, so you can go after him) and another one who walks to the ramp and back (so wait until he is heading away from the ramp).&nbsp Avoid those!&nbsp When the coast is clear, go forward toward the courtyard and turn left.&nbsp Almost immediately on your right is a ramp heading down into the courtyard.&nbsp You need to jump up on the left wall of the ramp.&nbsp To do this you need to achieve a certain velocity and angle so it may take a couple tries, but it's not too tricky.&nbsp [i]You cannot walk down this ramp into the courtyard because you will draw aggro from 4 elites.[/i]&nbsp Likewise, when you are coming back up you will definitely draw aggro unless you have some clever tricks at your disposal.&nbsp From the wall jump down on the grass and walk toward the other ramp, which heads west. This ramp has another locked door at the bottom which leads to a tunnel going to the Library.&nbsp When you open the door there's a long tunnel going straight there - no aggro at all.&nbsp [b]The NPC for Elven Legends is a skeleton on the floor next to Lorekeeper Lydros.[/b]&nbsp Interact with the skeleton, return to the quest giver in Feathermoon and you're good to go for the Libram quests. Oh, and getting out... as I said you WILL draw aggro trying to go up out of the courtyard unless you have a trick up your sleeve (stealth, invisibility potion, etc). So prepare to fight 4 elites, spirit rez or return to the instance for corpse. :) Thanks to Paelos on Proudmoore for showing me this shortcut!

Comment1: Lords & Ladies: There is a lot of whining above, but let me set the record straight. My guildmates and I have assisted in the forging of no less than half a dozen Quel Serrars in Onyxia's Lair. It is not all that hard if you know what to do. After the first two phases of the Onyxia battle have passed, let your tank be absolutely confident that he has the great wyrm under control. Get her down to bout 5% so that you know that you've got this battle within reach. Plant the blade in front of Onyxia's face next to your tank, then quickly get the heck away from her. (If the battle is going badly and you're not completely confident that you're going to win, KEEP THE BLADE in it's sheath. You can always try again after you wipe if you didn't put it down to be breathed on.) Your tank (who should have sufficent Fire Resistance to sustain a GREAT MANY breaths, duh!) can give you a shout when the blades been breathed on. Run over and pick up the blade. If you're concerned about getting killed, down a Fire Resistance potion before running over to Onyxia's face. Grab the blade and get the heck away from her. At that point you've now got 20 minutes to take her from 5% to 0%. If you can't do that, well, maybe you should have sold the book to start with. :-P Grab your blade and stick it in her corpse. Run back to Dire Maul and complete the quest. If you've pulled it off, welcome to the elite ranks of Azeroth.

Comment1: As it stands now in patch 1.12, a Libram of Rapidity can only be used for two things: a +1% increase to weapon speed (think weapon chain) when applied to a leg or head item, and +10 NR when applied to those same item slots.&nbsp They drop in every wing of DM. For both enchants, you need to make an [url=https://classicdb.ch/?i=Arcanum%20of%20Rapidity]Arcanum of Rapidity[/url].&nbsp It is a quest reward, but assuming you've completed [url=https://classicdb.ch/quest=7482]Elven Legends[/url] you can acquire all the materials before you obtain the quest, so two trips aren't needed. Comment1: Just to add to the very helpful post above, this is pretty easy to solo. I had never been to the instance, however, so I didn't know what the North entrance was or how to get there. I'll try to clarify for complete noobs like myself. As you come up to the main entrance, which is marked on the map, you'll go up a ramp which has an ogre at the top. There are walkways to the left and right, but you want to go straight through the big doorway and into a hallway that turns a couple of times ... there's only one way to go here, so just follow it. I was level 56 and I was able to go around the ogres without aggro. [b]Watch out for patrolling packs of dogs, they're pretty frequent.[/b] At the end of the hallway there's a giant door-looking thing, but you have to go around to the back of it to continue. It's pretty clear on the map. When you get around and through there's a giant open courtyard with a sunken forum in the middle and ogres all over. I stuck to the left wall and was able to get past all the ogres. Go all the way north here to find the door. At the north end there's a ramp that is guarded by a couple of ogres that are a little too close to sneak by, at least at level 56. At this point I used my pet to distract them and ran to the door, feign death. Here you either need a crimson key, which you can't solo, or you can use a powerful seaforium charge (if you're an engineer), which worked like a charm. Keep in mind that you'll need 2 of them, one for this door and one for a door in the instance. Behind this door is the start of the instance. Once in the instance it's a short run to the door you need, but it needs to be well timed. You're looking out of an alcove in the wall, and slightly to your left is a ramp down into a central area. Watch the patrols for a little to see the pattern...there's a single ogre that moves right and left. You want to go when he's to the right. There's also a patrol of an ogre with 2 dogs that seems to wander around the whole area. Once it's clear, run to the ramp [b]and jump as you're going down the ramp onto the railing.[/b] You can't jump straight onto the railing, it has to be as you're going down the ramp...angle slightly to the left. You want to land as close to the beginning of the railing as you can. The group of giants there won't aggro you, but watch out for a patrol of dogs, they will aggro if they're close. From the beginning of the railing jump down and hug the wall to the left. The door is right in front of you now. Just follow the wall around and go down into the doorwell. Another seaforium and you're in the hallway to the library...no more mobs to worry about! Remember that you have to right-click the book to start the quest, and also pick up the pattern: mooncloth robe from the vendor in there...you can make a few gold in the AH.

When the last one dies, you heard a shattering sound and you'll see the pylon 'explode' and it won't glow bright bluish-white anymore. (It'll be an ugly white afterwards). The [b]elementals[/b] surrounding the pylons are [b]immune to arcane magic[/b]. They also hit rather hard so it's best if you don't take all of them down at a time. It's possible to [b]pull 1-2[/b] from the pylon without aggroing the others. When you go in, you'll see a pylon right away. Be careful to not aggro the trees on both sides of the pylon, and watch out for the walking giant trees (But if you;'re going to kill the big tree boss, Tendris Warpwood, you should just kill the giant trees walking around. Tendris Warpwood will call them all to defend him if you engage in a fight with him.) Then, walk upstairs to where the undead are (the place is relatively small, I'll assume you can [b]see[/b] the upstairs are from the first pylon). There, they'll be two pylons, one on the left side, one on the right. Either way you go (it's like a rectangle shape, [~ == ~] the middle is a hole you cannot 'float' over and the pylons are marked here with a ~. Illyanna Ravenoak (boss) and her bear are walking around one side of the rectangle (the side away from the entrance) so you migth want to kill that side), you'll have to kill a mob of non-elite skeletons. [b] Be careful![/b] Once these skeletons are dead, they'll spawn five non-elite worms to attack whoever had the killing blow on the original skeleton. They have very little health, but should be taken down [b] a.s.a.p.[/b] as five worms hitting one person for ~50hp per hit will kill anyone pretty quickly. Also, [b]don't[/b] split up! There are invisible monsters that appear once in a while and if your healer (or someone) gets ahead of the rest of the party, they'll probably die if no one's there to defend them. Ok! Comment1: Ok if you got time and a dedicated group, this can all be done in 1 run with lotsa loot doing various quests along with this. Start with northside DM and make sure you have the mats for the ogre suit and the broken trap. Tribute's basically killing all but the named ogres, then kill the king and leave cho'rush the named ogre magi at the end alone. Once you get all of that done, check your tribute chest for extra look, talk to all the nameds you left alive for buffs (excluding cho'rush and stomper kreeg, kreeg lets you buy alcoholic drinks tho). But talk to captain kromcrush who now resides in the center area where fengus patrols. He gives you this quest. Now you have the quest you have to kill the prince in order to get the gauntlets, but if you goto DM from the northside you'll notice he's not hostile and you can't attack him. THat means you gotta go to the westside Instance. This instance imo is best done with a warlock, a priest, a good tank, a mage and whatever spare character you want to put in. The directions I state are from when you enter the actula instance and not northside to library. Work your way forward and you'll notice instantly a big white crystal guarded by mana beings, you have to kill all of the mobs surrounding the 5 pylons in this instance. After clearing pylon 1, head forward and you'll see a ramp down to Tendris Warpwood, you can kill him for drops or whatever. But head back up and proceed to the right, this is where the priest comes in and needs to shackle one of the spirits, the others must kill or disable them anyway possible. After killing proceed up the ramp, and make a u-turn left. Kill more mobs, more mana creatures (this is pylon 2), skeletons lie past it, you can skip them if or kill them your choice. Make your way down the path to the right and you'll meet the shen'drelar who gives you The Madness Within quest. Take it, proceed forward, kill skeletons, and more mana creatures for pylon 3. After that you will notice a NE hunter with a zombie type bear. Her ranged is tough but melee ain't so bad, the bear charges tho I think. Anyway kill both, and head down to the area you killed warpwood earlier. You'll notice a door to the right, open it with crescent key, proceed killing invisible stalker spirits(these guys respawn like every 10 minutes). Now your choice of left or right, but you'll have to either kill or skip the wind elementals, best to have the lock banish elementals and kill the kid wind eles 1st, then unload everything on the daddy elemental, his damage is a storm based aoe that hurts rather well so keep your healer aware. After that once you clear them, both left and right ends of that area have pylons, clear them and immol'thar is unleashed. Immol'thar an odd one, big fat weird dog that makes the beast or an ancient corehound look SEXY. Really.. Immol is more power based than anything. He spawns eyes about every 5-7 seconds that cause slowing and other fun stuff, have someone like a rogue or a hunter kill them as their job in this fight, keep the warrior healed and unload on Immol'thar. You can have your priest outside the center area and prolly get little aggro from fugly doggy. Once he dies, you move on to the prince, he's right next door. Open door, head in, then down the ramp and u-turn, you'll notice the shen'drelar treasure chest(looks just like ogre tribute one). But can't interact with it, you need to kill the prince 1st. At this point you'll see him at hostile red color. He's fast, he's nasty, and he just isn't nice. my experience: 60 sham, 60 warrior, 60 mage, 60 hunter, 58 shadow priest. We fought him, 1st time was a wipe. 2nd time went alot better but 1st time no one went offensive but warrior and we just tried to keep him alive and do almost no attacks. But the 2nd time I decided it's damage time. I unloaded on him and sorta caught my own group off guard, the priest realized it and shielded me and healed. I spammed shocks, chain lightning and everything. But the prince's aggro was mixed between me and the warrior and it went off fine, the mage, hunter and SW:P put in damage and DoTs on him and he died rather quick. We were all backed up against the wall due to his annoying knockback shot. Once he's dead, check the chest next to where he was standing originally and get the gauntlets, make your way back to the Shen'Drelar ghost, killing any enemies in your way, you complete quest, then head back down to the library and pick your treasure of 3 items, hunter helm, decent 2H mace, druid type pants. Now you have to go back to Northside to return the gauntlets, this here is the problem if you left north to goto west, the ogres will hostile you and you have to do the tribute again, but if you worked from the tunnel in north to goto the library, then west and worked 'backwards', you can get it done w/o having to do tribute again. It seems a bit more tedious but it really isn't. Nonetheless, another tribute or not, once you talk to Krom'crush, return the gauntlets to him and you get your armor specific equivalent of the gauntlets. The backwards route goes as follows from the doorway of library to west instance. Pylon to the right, pylon far in front of you. Head to the tunnel between the pylons and you'll have to fight warpwood past the tunnel. Kill him, and move up the ramp, directly forward another pylon. Now left of the ramp is a path that goes to the deadside of west DM, kill the spirits and head up the ramp. Make the u-turn to kill more undead and more mana creatures at 4th pylon. Head to the right path, talk to the ghost elf girl for the quest or whatever, head forward, you'll find pylon to the right making it the 5th. Once all 5 are unguarded, then immol is accessible and you can go back and kill him and prince etc. All in 1 run right? Hehe, enjoy. Edited, Wed May 4 08:24:00 2005

Comment1: You need to speak to Nogg in Orgrimmar and accept the quest. After you accept it, a goblin to the right of you will have a quest. He asks you to speak to Scooty in Booty Bay. Alliance has a much easier time getting into the original instance since it is in Gnome/Dwarf territory. Horde must enter via a transporter in Booty Bay. Get off the boat and head right you will see a goblin guarding a strange contraption. Inside, you will have many routes to take. You will see many little consoles where you acquire various keycards that are in binary. Basically move all around the first instance and gather these keycards. You will find the mini quest here from a female gnome. There is also an escourt mission deeper in, but we didnt want to head back towards the exit to find out what he had to offer. You will find a machine that cashes in the 'little bits' you keep getting off mobs. Reward varies from junk and ore to Iradescent Pearls and I even got a nice necklace with +agi/spirit. If you go into the next room&nbsp you will find the escort mission in one of the window type rooms on the right wall. Eventually you will start facing machines and little workers that are not elite as an earlier poster mentioned. Beware the wandering robot that starts shouting out alerts! He will spawn mobs until he is killed. Also beware the machinesmiths they will repair the machines during battle. As a rogue I was unable to sap the machines but I was able to cheap/kidney shot them into a stunned state. Work your way around and you will eventually find the bigger machine that has a key to open the door to the next instance. In the next instance its more of the same elite machinery and more of the little workers. Beyond that you will start fighting dark dwarves that will drop a trap on death, so be careful. Work your way around and you will find your quest items.

If you fight on the edge, you'll pull dozens of elites by accident. You can kill mines from the dwarves, but they have a lot of health. The best option is to back up when a mine is laid. Kill the red alarm robots before they yell more than once. If you don't, a party of robots (sometimes more than 4) will come and get you. For the boss, make sure you close all the doors before you fight. Designate 1-2 people to continue closing doors while you are fighting. The doors are closed with big red buttons at the bottom of hte pillar.

Instructions: Venture to Gnomeregan and kill Mekgineer Thermaplugg. Return to High Tinker Mekkatorque when the task is complete. Mekgineer Thermaplugg slain
Progress: Is the task complete? Did he beg for lenience? For mercy??
Comment1: A few general tips to keep in mind during a Gnomeregan run: You might consider making a macro like /target Mobile Alert System /cast Earth Shock(Rank 4) or whatever rank of whatever instant-cast damage spell you might have. Moonfire, Arcane Shot, Fire Blast, you get the idea. If you're not all about macros, just keep your eyes peeled and make sure your sound is on so you can catch them, otherwise they spawn a pair of elites. Alone, this isn't that bad, but when they come in the middle of a fight already in progress, you're probably going to wipe unless you're slightly overleveled or have a really good and organized group. A major chokepoint for many Gnomeregan groups is the tunnel with all the Dark Iron Agents. The first pull with 4 Dark Irons is just really tough, make sure you kill mines before they're armed. A little further along, there's a group of 3 Dark Irons and one Arcane Nullifier who seem like they're a linked pull. If you wait for the Arcane Nullifier to path over near you, you can pull it and one of the Dark Irons, splitting it up into two pulls of two instead of another group of 4 that can now reflect spells. As for Thermaplugg himself, just keep DPSing, have someone run around and push the buttons of the statues with open mouths to prevent being nuked with tons of bombs, and if you have a good mage, Thermaplugg can be kited with Blink and some clever maneuvering.
Comment2: 2750 XP at level 38, when the quest is yellow.
Comment3: Okay so I have a new rogue, level 20ish.&nbsp I wanted the Triprunner Dungarees for her (naturally).&nbsp Came here to check out how to get em.&nbsp I see a bunch of comments pretty much saying , 'zOMG its soo hard!' 'I had 2 60's help and we all died! zoh noez!' I went to Gnomer with my main (level 60 druid).&nbsp Nothing aggroed me, but I felt like testing it out anyway.&nbsp So I aggroed 3 or 4 groups of mobs (normal and elite mixed) and aoe'd.&nbsp Mind you, I am 51-point restoration spec for raiding.&nbsp So I have no talents in Balance (spell dps) or Feral (melee dps).&nbsp I killed the 3-4 groups of mobs with 1 aoe. I stealthed to Thermaplugg's room, opened the door, went inside.&nbsp Buffed with Mark of the Wild only, I killed him in under 30 seconds in cat form.&nbsp The bombs did about 100dmg to me, or at least it felt like it. So in conclusion, don't listen to people who blow this quest out of proportion.&nbsp It's not that hard to get to him and kill him. Now yes, I understand I am level 60, and a group of 30s would have a harder time.&nbsp But here's the thing, designate 1-2 people to hit the bomb switches and you will be fine.&nbsp For the mobs before Thermaplugg, just your basic tank, heal, and dps.&nbsp If you can't get by those you will never make it in BWL/Naxx. But seriously.&nbsp If you want this quest done, and dont want to waste time on trash mobs or the new LFG feature, just find a level 60 pal (or try and pay someone) to kill Therma for you.&nbsp Any druid, paladin, or hell, a warrior with first aid, can do it easily.
Comment4: The thing about Gnomeregan seems to be that it's the first instance that actually requires some thinking and coordination. Other low level instance you just run around and beat up everyone you see, and you'll be fine as long as the tank keeps aggro and the healer heals. Gnomeregan requires fast reaction to dropped mines and alarm bots, timing to avoid large patrols, mobs that become immune to magic damage and finally some button pressing at the last boss. Sometimes this seems like it's just too much for inexperienced players (and noobs who just refuse to learn) whom until now have been able to survive by just doing dps. In the end it comes to us experienced players *snicker* to explain to the newbies how to act, and get past certain areas. Unfortunately some people suck horribly at explaining, and rather resort to yelling insults and leaving the group, and others (noobs) just refuse to listen.
Comment5: This quest can be difficult to complete depending on your group and how good they are, but before you consider passing it up, the rewards are most definately worth the work.

Comment4: The undead beginnings upon Azeroth do not truly begin with the corruption of Prince Athas. It began long before that event. The events that brought downfall of Lordaeron were bong set in motion before that point. It began with the coming of the orcish clans and the burning legion. The orcs of Draenor (the world which they originally came from) were noble and shamanistic. They were powerful warriors strong of body and will. It was for these reasons that the burning legion sought them out. Kil'Jaeden, a demon of great power among the legion, wished to enslave the orcish clans and use them as his army against the worlds the burning legion had yet to conquer. Kil'Jaeden came to the leader of the clans, a powerful shamen named Nur'Zhul. He promised Nur'Zhul untold mystical power and knowledge if he made a pact with the demon that would enslave the clans to the Burning Legion. This pact sealed not only their fate, but that of their world forever. As time past, Nur'ZHul realized that the fate of the fate of the clans at the hands of the burning legion, and the orc shaman began to defy Kil'Jaeden. The demon angered by Nur'Zhul turned to the shaman's own apprentice, Gul'Dan who was far more corruptable than Nur'Zhul. It was Gul'dan who was responsible for the decline of shamanism throughout the clans. The promise of power and control over one's enemies made his offers even more tempting. With Kil'Jaeden's help, Gul'dan began his manipulation of the clans. The orcs, once noble, became corrupt, mindless savages. With the introduction of demon blood into their bodies, the orcs were even more rutheless and barbaric. Even though Kil'Jaeden had corrupted Gul'dan after his failure with Nur'Zhul, Kil'Jaeden hated the shaman and vowed to enforce their original pact. Kil'Jaeden captured Nur'Zhul and began an incredibly slow physical torture on the shaman. While, Nur'Zhul begged for death, Kil'Jaeden reminded Nur'Zhul that their original pact was still binding. Kil'Jaeden killed the orc, but only physically. Kil'Jaeden held the orc shaman's spirit fast before it could find its way to the twisting nether. Kil'Jaeden placed Nur'Zhul's spirit within a block of ice gathered from the twisting nether. While it was trapped in the ice, he infused into it even more power. The loss of his body and the introduction of such incredible power was the defining line in Nur'Zhul's transformation. Kil'Jaeden hurled the block of ice through dimensions back to Azeroth, where it landed in the continent of Northrend, introducing this great evil to our world. Ner'Zhul was gone forever. In his place was a throne of ice and hatred. The once respected shaman leader had become the Lich King. Because Kil'Jaeden did not trust the Lich King. He sent his dred lords to watch over the spirit and ensure that the Lich King followed his orders. The Vampiric servents came to Azeroth willingly, drawn to the destruction and power of the Lich King and the potencial genocide of a planet's entire race. Over a decade passed. During this time the Lich King used his vast powers to gain control over the minds of the creatures of Northrend, whom he commanded to erect a great citadel over his frozen throne. Now that all of Northrend was under his domination, the Lich King knew he needed to begin his infiltration of Lordaeron. Trapped within the ice, the former orc shaman began seeking more minds to manipulate and control. His call reached out across the continents. The Lich King's summons did not go unnoticed, especially by a small handful of powerful individuals. Among them was the Archmage Kel'Thuzad, who was a powerful member of the ruling body of Dalaran, the Kirin Tor. His pursuit of all types of magic violated the Kirin Tor's policies against learning dark magics. Kel'Thuzad abandoned the Kirin Tor, and all his ties to conventional thought and vowed to learn as much as he could from the Lich King. A pact was struck between the two. Kel'Thuzad would receive immortality and immense power in return for servitude to the Lich King. Kel'Thuzad's first task was to use his wealth and influence in Lordaeron to found the Cult of the Damned. The Cult promissed equality and eternal life to all its members as long as they swore and oath to Ner'Zhul, the god of the Cult of the Damned. Edited, Fri Dec 9 17:55:18 2005

Name: Doctor Theolen Krastinov, the Butcher
Instructions: Find Doctor Theolen Krastinov inside the Scholomance. Destroy him, then burn the Remains of Eva Sarkhoff and the Remains of Lucien Sarkhoff. Return to Eva Sarkhoff when the task is complete. Doctor Theolen Krastinov slain Remains of Eva Sarkhoff Burned Remains of Lucien Sarkhoff Burned
Progress: The Butcher must be stopped!
Comment1: Once the butcher is dead, look to each sides of the room, you will see piles of flesh. These are the remains of Eva Sarkhoff and her husband. Get rid of them and you will complete the quest.
Comment2: We were able to stealth all three missions in this quest chain, multiple times, with various combos of rogues and druids. Here are some tips if you want to try stealthing it. Some of these comments were mentioned above as well. [b]Group[/b] Both four rogues and one druid, or three rogues and two druids works well. I personally prefer 4 and 1 and then the druid focuses on healing. The extra druid does not add much since the bear can't hold aggro and therefore it is better to have a 4th DPS rather than a second healer. You can get away with 58 rogues if they have talent points for master of deception. I think it's best to have 60 druids since they are spotted far more often. [b]Preparation[/b] To save time, make sure everyone knows to bring lots of heals, bandages, and the druids need mana type pots etc. You will burn through a lot of them and it sucks to get half way and run out of supplies. Usually a few people get to the instance early...get the early rogues to open the four doors that lead to Rattlegore. This saves a lot of time once everyone arrives. Unlock, Vanish, Prep, repeat or die and repeat. Opening the first four doors is not hard, expecially if the people don't mind dying. We found that it saved the most time to meet back at the bridge on the start and clear the four guards...the druids get seen by them too often and it helps to have them removed when getting through the locked door. [b]Rattlegore[/b] Get to rattlegore stealthed and have one rogue do the pulling. Thin the mobs just like regular 5 man play but if the puller gets an Add, he should vanish in Rattles room and then try again. If he vanishes late, the druid is going to get targettted and die. If you try and fight Rattle and an Add, it's 98% chance of wipe, so just vanish and save time. Do not let anyone grab the key. Tell the group that YOU are the only one who is gonna take the key or your closest guildmate. People burn out fast when dying and then quit the group with the key which sucks incredibly. Anyone can take the key if people look at it and leave it...then it is visible to all. Get the key! [b]The Locked Door[/b] As stated above, there are two ways to open this door. Have the entire group come back to the starting bridge and wait. Now make a choice...try an unstealthed sprint jump to the top of the door and attempt unlocking, or two people jump down stealthed, one unstealths and runs, uses evasion and a heal to pull aggro and the other stealthed person (you since you have the key) unlocks the door. The first method sounds all fancy and cool, but it goes bad so often that it is just 100 times simpler to use the suicide pull aggro method. Even if you make the door sill jump, you often get tons of aggro from below anyways and get interupted on each open attempt. [b]Butcher[/b] Now everyone can get to the butcher room. Pull normally to the doorway to clear the room and explain to new players about the green smoke. Also tell new players that if they die during the butcher fight, do not release, so they get credit for his death. Make sure people whack the meat in the corners too. Then everyone exists, cashes in the quest and grabs Bag of Horrors aka Jandice. [b]Jandice[/b] Again you will have to make a choice, either clear one side of the hall to get to Jandice like normal 5 man, or everyone stealth to her and hide in the back of her room. We found that druids were just easier to spot and so it was hard to get them to Jandice. With 5 people, usually someone gets spotted trying to do the super mario stealth tricks, and so we decided just to clear. I think it is technically possible to stealth to her though since I attacked her solo once as a test and did not pull aggro into the room. If you clear the hall, work quickly, pulling back to the door for the group. Do not dilly dally because by the time you get to her, the room starts respawning and then it's pure hell and everyone wants to quit. When you get to her, and she splits into 10, stay calm since you don't have to beat up all ten, just find her and the extras will fade. If you are successful, again everyone exists and cashes in the quest and grabs Kirtonos and blood of innocence. [b]Kirtonos[/b] This is straight forward like regular 5 man. We find it is easiest to group in the lower left corner beside the stairs all together. Then bouncing is minimized and DPS is maximized since time is not wasted getting back too him. I used to group at the back gate until I got bounced through the gate and into the room full of angry casters. lol [b]Other Tips[/b] Stuns are your friend. You can't cheap shot every boss but you can kidney almost all of them. Have the rogues ready to stun as much as possible and to space the stuns out so you go kind of in order to maximize the frozen time of the boss you are attacking. Oil of Immulsion is very handy. Many people have never tried the oil but it is great AOE for someone who can't AOE. We like to take 10 each when trying all three quests. The four attackers use 1-2 per boss. This is 1000-2000 more damage on the target and often makes the difference if you are going to live or die in a close fight. If your armor goes yellow, you or others can run to Chillwind for fast armor repair. These quests are especially worthwhile if you are an alchemist since the spectral essence lets you buy major mana and transmute water to air on a 24 hour timer. This quest series is also important if you are a rogue wanting the darrow spike dagger quest series which follow. Hope these tips were useful for those wanting to try the three quests stealthed.

Comment1: You can get this quest without completing any other quests. Nomisin of Proudmoore
Comment2: This is one of the first difficult instances of the game.&nbsp You have packs of 3-4 20-22nd level elites to contend with and serious challenges to face before you can get to Arugal.&nbsp An experienced party can do this with care and attention to aggro range, focusing their attacks precisely.&nbsp Inexperienced groups (unless way overlevelled) will wipe again and again. Arugal himself is quite dangerous and teleports continuously during the fight within a two leveled environment that makes it difficult for melee characters to reacquire him as a target. Anyone telling you this is an easy instance is either lying, bragging or carried through by other more sensible players and blindly confusing their competence with ease.
Comment3: There is an easy way to kill Arugal. Tag him and run back to the main chamber, where you killed Fenrus. The person who has aggro stays in the Fenrus room. Everyone else goes to Arugal's room. What will happen is Arugal charges towards the Fenrus room and then whacks one or two times (at most, sometimes none at all) and teleports back to his main room. This allows the other members of the group to smack Arugal around until his aggro changes to someone else. This new person can then go to Fenrus' room and repeat as before. Everytime he teleports, he'll erase any dots on him, but he will not reset his health (as of 4/3/06). This most likely will be patched, however. A few other tips. Do not go into the room to kill Fenrus. Kill him in the hallway. Have the tank stand in the hallway to attract the mobs that spawn afterwards. If you kill a named, sometimes a new wolf-man spawns in a place that you may have cleared. For example, when you kill the Baron, a wearwolf spawns in the room adjacent to the courtyard and adjacent to the Baron's room. This can complicate pulling, so go back and kill this. The tricky pull spot is the Knight's room (up the stairs past the Baron's room). Here is a way to pull this room. Have a warlock cast Eye of Kelrog and have a priest cast the spell-shield on it. The eye can get aggro, but the mobs ignore it unless it gets too close. As a result, you can pull fewer mobs and sometimes even singles from clusters of mobs. (This works in general.) In the Knight's room, have the tank grab the ghost in the hallway. Then send the eye all the way to the right (upon entering) and grab the attention of the Knight's in the back (the side opposite of the named mob). You can clear the room in this way so that when you pull the named you only get 2 adds. Of course, you can also just send in the puller. All in all this is a challenge. Did this with 4 26s. (Mage, Warlock, Warrior, Priest.)

Comment3: The key to doing that in a 5 man is to only pull the first one, and pull it to the very back. Then when an add wanders in you let it run to the back and then shackle it. Kill the add after the first one is done. After you kill the add you rest for mana. You always let them wander in on their own in a 5 man, unless you are very comfortable about pulling. Every one of the abominations will wander in on it's own, so you only need to pull the first one. Always stay at the back of entryway by the gate. Comment1: Just to let everybody know a few things about this quest: 1. It is completely possible for a group equipped entirely in blues to complete this quest successfully.&nbsp I personally have never done it, but I have started my own timer with the Baron's and we've done it in 56 minutes and that was with a lot of scrweing around, a few 'AFK for a min', and even 1 complete wipe (luckily we had a shaman with us and she Reincarnated and we got back going in a couple of minutes). 2. You do not actually have to KILL the Baron within the 45 minute timer.&nbsp All you have to do within the 45 minute timer is have each player in your group who is on this quest 'tap' Rivendare.&nbsp After this you can wipe, corpse run, east dinner, smoke a cigarette, have sex with your girlfriend, wash your car, then come back and finish the Baron off and you will still successfully complete the quest.&nbsp Now I know some people are going to call 'bull&*!@' on me on that one, but I have a guildie who has successfully completed multiple 45 minute Baron runs and he swears this is the case. 3. A few of the people above posted about how to pull this instance and for the most part they were entirely correct.&nbsp I'll throw my 2 cents in here on that matter.&nbsp First, when you go through the gate right after receiving 'The Baron's Ultimatum' there will be an area with a lot of banshees, crypt beasts, and a 3 gargoyle patrols going back and forth.&nbsp My advice is if you can grab one of the gargoyle patrols without waiting for it, do so.&nbsp They seem to have an ungodly aggro range and for some reason you seem to get all 3 if you get 1.&nbsp Pulling with counterspell seems to be the best way to pull these mobs back to you as the banshees, crypt beasts, and gargoyles all have ranged attacks. 4. Avoid as many fights as you safely can.&nbsp The only area I strongly recommend clearing fully is around the Baroness cause she can do some crazy things to your party.&nbsp As a side note to that, if you have any abilities that are on a timer that could potentially mess over your party (read: warrior intimidating shout), use them AS SOON AS you engage the Baroness, otherwise if you get mind controlled you can be sure she'll use them.&nbsp I have had many a Baron run get messed up because I got mind controlled and feared 3 of my party members into 3 different groups of mobs. 5. I think the best way to tackle the mini-bosses is Nerub'enkan, Baroness, then the Pallid guy.&nbsp After this you will have to deal with Barthilas, Rammstein, and finally Baron Rivendare himself.&nbsp I can honestly say Rivendare might be the EASIEST boss in the instance.&nbsp Have your tank pull him to the right side of the room and have somebody ready to AOE the skeletons as soon as they appear.&nbsp If you don't have a warlock or mage in your party make sure you raid the supply crates and everybody in your party (other than the main tank) has a couple of Stratholme Holy Waters and take turns using them to get rid of the skeletons. 6. The last piece of advice I would like to give is this.&nbsp If you wipe at any point before killing the Baroness (assuming you followed my order of boss killing), go back outside and have your party leader reset the instance.&nbsp If you wipe before the Baroness chances are your party got a bad break on an add, a stupid pull, or one of Blizzard's famous 8:00 pm CDT lag spikes that royally screwed you over.&nbsp It only takes a maximum of 25 minutes to get to the Baroness (only 15 of that being on the timer) if you take the side entrance to the instance, so you won't be wasting a ton of time running the same parts of the instance over and over.&nbsp Not to mention the number of scourgestones you'll be racking up killing those pesky undead over and over. Well, I think that's all the advice I have on this quest.&nbsp As soon as I have all of the pieces of my Valor set that I need I'll be trying it out myself.&nbsp Wish me luck, and I wish you luck, even those of you who unthinkingly decided to roll alliance. =P Labiche 60 Warrior Horde side Illidan server 300 enchanter send me a /tell in game if you need anything
Comment2: ok first of all, what a rush.... must have been the most intensive 45 mins in my WoW experience. We had me (60 rogue with mostly blue items, but a good pve sword combat build), one rogue roughly same items/build as me, then an uber full epic-geared&nbsp rogue, an uber full epic-geared priest and a warrior with a few epics rest blue items. In the beginning i doubted we would make it within the timelimit. Killing the baroness took longer than usual because she first took over our priest, then our epic-geared rogue (using most of his cooldown making him a pain to take down)... however we had a good pace at killing everything else... the priest would either shacklepull or pull with dots while we were fighting. You dont have time to wait for pulls... When we reached the patch-dudes we had 15 mins left on the clock so we took it abit easy from there.... however... I died on rammstein because i got too impatient not letting the tank build up enough aggro... the plan we had on the mass-skeleton part was that me and the priest had to use our holy waters + the rest using whatever trinkets/dynamite they had... so my death could have been fatal for the mass-undead part... but thanks to a fantastic healing job done by our priest and a great tanking warrior we prevailed... the quest vanished when i died but reappeared when the Baron announced our last chance (5 mins remaining). We fought the baron with all of us standing close to him, with me and the priest using each our holy waters for the skeleton spawns, needless to say the baron died very quickly with this group setup ) Step by step, here is the route we took AND you have to be constantly moving ofcourse and know exactly where the next 'checkpoint' is to get as little downtime as possible: 1) The first arachna boss to the left down the street, avoiding the group to HIS left. 2) Baroness, avoiding the mobs to her left (back in the corner of the street), also after you've cleared that tower try to avoid the mobs standing at your groups right side as you proceed to the narrow alley to the third boss. 3) After finishing off the third boss (perhaps without aggroing the group at the far side of the stairs to that tower), try to cut through this open area taking out as few groups as possible, then hug the wall on the right side when heading towards the flesh-patched dudes. 4) The rest is about how much time you have left... we had roughly 15 mins left when we pulled the first patched horror, and two mins left on the timer when the baron died. Comment3: This is the infamous '45-minute Strat' run that many have tried and few have beaten. It's part of the Dungeon Set 2 (Tier 0.5) upgrade quest chain, so it's appropriately difficult. In order to pull this off successfully, you need to know how to cut the right corners: 1. you do not need (or want) to pull every group of mobs that you would normally pull on a Strat dead run. Walk around every group you possibly can. Battle the fewest number of enemies possible. 2. do not loot anything (except - maybe! - for the minibosses). You do not have the time to roll for random greens, but more importantly, if it takes you 3s to loot a mob and you loot 100 over the course of the run, that's 5 full minutes used. The timer is too tight to justify 5 minutes of looting. 3. start the next pull before the current mob is dead. The DPS players (specifically rogues and hunters) should basically have no downtime throughout the run. The only breaks you should take are for the casters to drink up, and even then you should only drop out of combat long enough for them to start. 4. most importantly and most obviously, remember to concentrate your firepower on a single target before moving onto the next one. That actually applies to every group, but people seem to forget easily. Unfortunately a good part of this run is luck. With that said, best of luck to you. :)
Comment4: It is not impossible. It takes practice. Those who are used to doing only 15 and 10 man's are going to have a hard time since you don't ever learn how to play your character effectively in raids. You just have to play smart and communicate a plan with the rest of your group. It would be hard in a PUG but not impossible as long as 2 people knew what they were doing. Level 60 is a must here. Don't even think of bringing a 58 or 59. I have completed this 2 times now. First time took 7 tries and then we finally got it down. Priest, pally, warrior, rogue x2. Pulled Baron with 3 seconds to go. Too many deaths caused the last second pull. Mostly blues, couple of world epics and two or three end game epics in the whole party. Second time I completed this, took some other guildies through. Priest, pally (who just sat in melee most of the time), warrior, mage, rogue. Pulled Baron with 3 min to go (even with a pally not healing and one death). Mostly blues and a few world epics. Two people had one zg epic each and 1 tier 1 piece. With a mage, it is MUCH easier. Silence pulls are key with the banshees and screechers. If you don't have any silencers, use the corners to get out of site and pull them to you. Even though this party wasn't as strong since the pally wasn't healing and pulling and listening very well and we had one accidental pull, we still finished with 3 min to spare. The key more than anything is CHAIN PULLING. You are never fighting less than 2 - 3 mobs at a time. Two healers take turns drinking while the other is pulling/healing. Mobs down to half health? SHACKLE PULL! Gargoyle incoming? Get him in the fray. Melee should be in battle for almost the full 45 min. PATH TO TAKE: ------------- **Enter second gate, timer starts (btw, if you die u lose the debuff but it will come back at 10 min and 5 min), open next gate and clear all pats and groups in the open area. **Now head to [b]Nerub'enkan[/b] (left). Pull only mobs in your way. Kill boss, clear the ziggarat. **Head to baroness. Clear ONLY what you have to. Pull [b]Baroness[/b] and hide behind a corner to pull her to the room you cleared initially. MAKE SURE WARRIOR DOES NOT HAVE AGRO for baroness fight. If your warrior gets mind controled, it will take too long to widdle him/her down to get them un MC'ed. [b]You should clear the second ziggarat with 30 min still on timer.[/b] **Head up the alley to [b]Maleki[/b]. Again pull only what is needed. **Head to abominations. [b]You should be pulling your first abominations at 15 min. No less. [/b] **After Ramstein and the masses of undead, you have a 30 - 45 second wait until the doors open and the 5 elite skelly guards come out. Take this time to rebuff, change armor, get pots ready, etc. **Defeat skellies, run in Barons room, drink quick and move in! By the way, this is by far the hardest part of the quest chain other than the final boss (from what I've heard anyway). I wish they would've put in a few more challenges like this. We are now at the last two quests before we complete our set. Most of the rest of the quests are grind farming and mat collecting. A few summoning of bosses which give out some KILLER LOOTZ tho! Got myself a ring with 7 def, 7 str, and 13 stam off of Kormok in Scholo! Good luck to all and gratz to Blizz for an EXCELLENT quest that taught me to be an even better player!

Comment3: Just finished this quest last night. I found it to be very worth the work. We breezed through it last night and put on a near flawless performance with no deaths at all. 25 priest, 25 mage, 21 druid, 21 rogue, 21 hunter As the druid, I was the tank for the big fights. For everything except the bosses I was in cat form and we just dps'd everything till it died. When we aproached the bosses I would pull the boss with fairefire, switch to bear form and tank him while the rest of the group kills the goons. I pulled the mobs when we got to the boat. Using fairy fire is very effective to pull small groups and predebuffs the mob being pulled. Tubby: wait for him to walk away from his guards, then pull, you'll single him every time. After he dies, deal with his guards. Shredder: Pull all guards before attempting the Shredder. For the guards at the far door, wait for the Shredder to path back up the ramp. Once all the guards are cleared you pull the Shredder and beat it down. When he dies the operator pops out and you have to kill him too. Engineer Room: Clear around the cog all the goblins, when you get to the door the boss is acompanied by 2 guards. One of the guards can be pulled away from the Boss adn the other guard. Pull him and kill him. When engaging the Boss, you can either sheep the guard and kill the boss, or just kill the guard while the Tank occupies the boss. First Mate: Once the dock is cleared it's very important how you pull the first mate and his rogue buddies. The tank will inch up till he agro's the stealthed rogues, this will also pull the first mate. The mobs on the deck will not agro! We had a mage so one rogue got turned into a sheep. The Tank should [b]always[/b] stay on the main boss. The rest of the party needs to kill the remaining rogue, then kill the sheep, then dps the Boss. For the first mate he will stun the party 2 during the fight. As far as I can see it is not resistable, but he runs back to his chest and pulls some stuff out. Nothing big, just some dramatics, when you're unstunned keep dpsing him down. Clearing the ship: Clearing the first deck is basically the same as clearing the rest of the instance zone. Once you get to the first ramp, everyone stays on the first deck while the puller brings the mobs down to the group. If you try and crawl up to the top deck, then once you get to the first grp on the top, you will agro the captain any all the other mobs on the ship. If you pull them indivdually then you'll be fine. I waited till the captain rounded the back of the ship, not sure if it makes a difference and I didn't want to take that chance :) Captain: Once the top deck is cleared, everyone can move up the ramps and along the deck to where the ent to the deck is. You can pull the captain or inch up to him the way you did with the first mate. Either way you pull him you'll get his two guards with him. Tank him the same way you tanked the first mate. VanCleef: VanCleef is located in the main cabin. You can see him if you peer in, but don't get too close until you're ready for him. You'll pull VC the same way you pulled the First Mate, he will have two rogue guards materialize when he's agro'd. Deal with them the same way you dealt with the First Mate's rogues. WARNING: shortly into the fight 2 more rogues will show up! We had the first two rogues dead before the second ones showed up so it wasn't a big deal, just a little surprise. We finished VC off before dealing with the rogues. But you can continue having the tank hold off VC while the rest of the group finishes the rogues. The Hunter's pet off tanked one of the new rogues so it wasn't on the priest. It's important that you have a tank who can taunt so that the boss doesn't pull off and start pounding down the rest of the party. With a decent tank and a compitent healer, there should be no problems keeping everyone alive during the boss fights. We wiped the first night we tried just as the instance was respawning so we didn't attempt it again, but the second night we went in we used this strategy and came out of it feeling it was very easily done. Hope this helps! Jonais 22 Druid Darkspear Kishan 13 Hunter Doomhammer
Comment4: Shouldn't take your group more than an hour and a half to do this entire instance. I'll lay out some working strategies as best I can. In the corridors, which is most of the zone, you just need to watch what/how you pull. I've pulled the entire dungeon as a level 22 Hunter and never gotten more than one add. You really need someone with a ranged attack to pull. If it's a caster who shouldn't be tanking, they need to use their lowest level spell to pull with, so they don't cause much initial aggro. If it HAS to be a paladin or druid, then they need to pull the mob and back up quite a bit. Runners in here will get you adds, which cause wipes. The first boss is an ogre. He walks up and down a path. If you've never done this before, watch him a couple times, and pull him when he's farthest from the door to avoid adds. There is a patrol after him, which will need to be neutralized before going through teh door. The next boss is the Shredder, and it's pilot (Sneed?). This is fairly simple, as the shredder also has a set path. Pull him just as he begins walking up the hill, but make sure all the goblins around the wood are dead. The second and final patrol is here. Next, you go down another corridor and into the Foundry. This is where most groups wipe. It is IMPERATIVE that your puller pay attention to the pathing of the goblins. Often they won't follow, but instead they will begin shooting. You will have to back out of their gun range to force them away from their friends to prevent adds. A single add in this area is difficult for a low level group, and can cause a wipe quite quickly. Also, the goblins in this area seem to have a high aggro range. Gilnik? is the boss of this area, over next to the door. He's not really too tough. Next up is another corridor which ends with a cannon pointed at the door. You'll need blasting powder from a room nearby to activate the cannon. This leads to the docks. The docks are easy until you get to the ramp leading up to the ship. There will be 2 stealthed rogues at the bottom of the ramp, and Smite, the Tauren, at the top. The main tank should engage Smite at the wide area before the turn to the plank, while the rest of the group deals with the rogues even further back. The healer should be at maximum range from the warrior to avoid Smite's stun. The reason for being farther away from the ramp is so that Smite will have to cover distance to run to his chest to switch his weapons, allowing more time for the stun to wear off. Once the rogues are dealt with, the rest of the group can engage Smite. At the top of the ramp, going right will lead to Captain Greenskin and Van Cleef. Going left will lead to Cookie, the murlock cook, and the exit. Just keep pulling slowly and keep the mobs being engaged far enough away from any potential adds. Once you reach the top platform, watch out for Greenskin. He patrols the top deck where VC is, but he will assist mobs on the platform below, so wait on him to patrol around to the other side before pulling. Once everything else is dead, pull Greenskin when he reaches the plank which leads to the top deck. He usually has 2 or 3 mobs linked to him, so this fight can be rough. Once Greenskin is down, it's time for VC. VC has 2 rogue friends who will assist him in the fight. When he reaches half life, 2 more will spawn. Use the same strategy as with Smite, with the MT on VC while the rest of the group deals with the adds. VC doesn't have an AOE stun like Smite though, but he's tougher and has more DPS, so the healer will likely need to keep attention on the MT. As a 22 Hunter, I was able to use my pet to tank VC while I healed it, while the rest of the group dealt with the adds. This helped the healer both on mana and on aggro, though in the end the pet finally died when I ran OOM, and VC proceeded to kill me. The group succeeded in finishing him off, and a rez later and we headed for the zone. Experience really helps a lot here. Once you reach the docks, if a wipe seems imminent, jump in the water, as the pirates can't swim. Ironic, ain't it? Edited, Thu Apr 21 00:15:18 2005

Comment3: Stockades is an instanced zone within Stormwind City. It's in the fort-looking building that's just NW of the trade district as you come into the city. (directly north of the enchanter's shop if you are familiar with that or just ask a guard) Stockades is populated with 23/24ish and up elites. The bosses are 27/28ish elites. The zone is essentially a T shape. As you come in you are at the bottom of the T. Along each hallway there are several rooms that lead off to the sides. These are populated with 3 or 4 elite mobs each. Be aware that runners will often turn into these rooms as they flee. So be sure to either A) stop all runners, B) be high enough to not care about the 3 adds or C) clear all rooms as you pass them. Dextren Ward can be found by heading straight in, and taking the first hallway turn to the left. Be aware that theer is a respawning wanderer that paths between the two branches of the T and could be comming up behind you at any given point. Down the Left hallway you go, until it opens into a larger room at the end. This larger room has 3 smaller rooms off of it. The large room will have 3 to 4 elites in it. Each smaller room will have approximately 3 elites in them. As you come into the large room Dextren Ward can be found in the smaller room off to the right. In there you'll almost always find 3 elites plus Dextren Ward. He's dressed as a caster but does not seem to cast when I fight him. Generally spekaing, Stockades is a very short zone for an instance and there are several quests for things inside of it. Comment4: Platinum Disc Quest Information: I read the information here and on a couple of other web sites prior to doing this quest and all the information I gathered was fuzzy at best. I have been playing this game for a long time and never completed this quest until today, with my level 45 troll priest. I will not go into the strategy that our group used to kill the final boss in there, you can read all about it here and on other sites. My goal here is to explain how to complete this quest as best I can, so that you go in there with a pretty clear idea of what you need to do to get it done. After you kill the final boss in Uldaman, all the minions collapse and a door opens into an isolated chamber. First of all, do not forget to loot the gem from the boss if you have that quest, which has nothing to do with this platinum disc quest. When you come into the chamber you will see an alter, of sorts, with a gear symbol for your mouse icon. Click it and a quest comes up. Accept the quest. Do not leave the chamber, you are not done. When you do this, a stone golem ghost appears to your left. Go over and speak with him. He will have some dialog text and a string of text at the bottom with an icon, letting you know that there is more to read. Click it. Again, there is more text and another string of text at the bottom with an icon. Click it. This is going to go on for a long time. I did not count how many times you have to keep doing this, but I would say at least 10 times maybe more. You will know when your done because on your screen you will get a 'complete' message. Do not leave the chamber, you are not done. All this was telling you to do, was to go back to the alter to retrieve the miniature platinum discs. Go back to the alter with the gear symbol and click it. There is another quest text and you click 'accept'. You will now have the miniature discs in your inventory. Do not leave the chamber, you are not done. You will notice that the alter still has a gear symbol on it. Click it. Quest text appears and choose 'accept'. Read it and make sure it tells you to take the discs to an NPC. Now, you are done, as far as the chamber and Uldaman are concerned. This final quest tells you to visit an NPC in Thunderbluff (if you are Horde). When you speak with the sage in Thunderbluff the quest is complete, but he will direct you to the NPC with your reward. After you speak with that NPC you are completely done with the quest. The sage will also tell you he needs more time to study the discs and there is probably more to the story, but that will come later. The most common mistakes made in not getting this quest completed are in leaving that chamber before you do all the things I have mentioned here in my explaination. My explaination may not be exact, but I think it will provide you with the information you need to help you get this one done.

Comment3: https://classicdb.ch/quest=886 is the start of the quest that then lead to this.&nbsp Horde only. Alliance has quests in Deadmines which are similiar to Hordes Wailing Caverns. (think Alliance gets better loot though :D ) &nbsp This instance does take some time, if you do it at the level that is recommended and not at a much much higher level.&nbsp You need to make several hours avialable to do this quest. (At level 60 by self can take a long time even, if killing every mob in the place.&nbsp Unless your an aoe demon.. :D )&nbsp Be sure to have plenty of free bag space and also mana food and health food.&nbsp Potions don't hurt, either.&nbsp Linen will drop a lot inside and you can make bandages as you go.&nbsp First-aid is your Ffriieeeeend...&nbsp :D It is do-able by a well rounded level 15 and up group. Preferrably, you have a mixed level group and not all 15.. someone in their 20's would be nice too. :D&nbsp Yes, you probably will die several times or even wipe total group, even, though.&nbsp It is not meant to be 'really' easy. Or, you might never die and never wipe.&nbsp Many things vary. A priest and a shammy are nice for the heals and self-rezz they can do once an hour, if your group wipes out and they can rezz you, too.&nbsp Shammies are not as 'efficient' as healing as priest though, but do make good offtank or tank if they can handle it. A warlock to soulstone the rezzer is also nice. :D (think you get that at lvl 18) You have to remember though, that the lower your level, the further the distance you will have monsters come and attack you and your group. So, with knowing that, you will have to decide what the minimum level of the group you take with you.&nbsp &nbsp The waters you cross going thru the cave to the Instance portal have monsters down below that come up when you cross but if you get out of water they cant attack after that. &nbsp Some of the monsters do respawn, so remember this as you are doing it.&nbsp The longer it takes, the more chance more of them will respawn.&nbsp Not all of them, but even one can kill you if you are running back from getting killed and your group is up the way. &nbsp Evolving ectoplasm's make copies of themselves as they get low on health.&nbsp Raptors screech and call help to them when low on health, and the Elf Druids run and get help when about 1/4 health.&nbsp Little plant looking monsters do some hard damage at low level, also, they are linked, if you attack one, they all come, so be forewarned. Druids can cast at you from a distance or change into snake form and melee you.&nbsp Verdan the Everliving is not required, he drops nice loot, BUT he is also HARD to kill and does LOTS of damage, that can kill your squishies quick and yourself too. &nbsp Go to one of the mod sights if you like to use mods and install a mod called Metamap.. it has dungeon maps that show you where the bosses are.&nbsp It's not a live map of the dungeon part, but it does let you see where you are and direction you need to go.&nbsp There are also several sights out there that give you guides on each dungeon.&nbsp Just do a google search to find some of sights.&nbsp Also at the top of the posts someone links a picture and a guide to WC, as well. &nbsp Serpentis and Verdan the Everliving are both.. way to the right and then down, then left.. you have to loop it around.. and jump across a ledge.. not down off cliff.. but across/down a ledge and that brings you to them when you follow it around.&nbsp If you fall, just run back around and try it again. &nbsp Make sure you loot each boss for the gems or you miss out on a nice staff or sword for this quest. &nbsp After you have killed all five boss's and are heading out.. you talk to the druid at the entrance again and he will give an escort quest.&nbsp It's not as hard as it used to be, but he stops at several points and monsters spawn.&nbsp Once he reaches the cave of the dreamer, there are a few waves of monsters that come when he is trying to wake the dreamer.&nbsp Kill them as fast as you can.. and mana and heal up.. or rezz up if needed as soon as you can before another wave comes.&nbsp I think its&nbsp 3 waves might be 2.. then.. Mutanus the Devourer comes.. this giant Murloc.. kill him.. get some nice loot .. check the bodies of the monsters in the waves too... they drop some loot too.&nbsp Everyone loot Mutanus, he has green crystal that is quest starter. &nbsp There are lots of greens that drop, lots of linen, Deviate scales, perfect deviate scales, and lot of mobs to be skinned.. the scales sell well on Auction House.&nbsp Theres some ore deposits, some herbs, and several treasure chests inside.&nbsp Several nice blues drop, too for the level.&nbsp Recently some new loot has been dropping that I have not seen before. *might be because I never got it to drop before though, not sure*&nbsp some lvl 20 drops. &nbsp Get as many of the other quests with this one before you go in.&nbsp Do a search in quest section for Wailing Caverns.&nbsp Also dont forget to share your quests with your party before you start fighting your way into the opening of the cave.&nbsp And.. there is a cave above the opening.. that you have to carefully drop down into from on top.. that you can get couple of the quests and some leather trainers/recipes. &nbsp Hope this gives some more info.. or refreshes what you might already know.&nbsp None of my warnings apply to the high level toons or those that have a high level toon helping them through the instance. (just to forestall anyone saying everything was sooo easy for them) -)

Basically, there's one cannon on top of the ship that you need to fire (I think it's the only one you are able to interact with).&nbsp Go on the ship and watch in the direction that the cannon aims.&nbsp About 4 waves of naga come up the path and if you fire the cannon when they appear in sight, the cannon kills them outright.&nbsp If you do this correctly, the Captain and his crew won't have to fight anything at all.
Comment3: I just finished this quest.&nbsp I talked to Shakes O'Breen and he gave me the quest that started off with 'this is bad.' ...'The Naga will be coming from the sea.&nbsp I need you to remain up here with me to fend off the attack.&nbsp Man the cannon and drive them back. Are you ready' As soon as I accepted the quest I ran up the gang-plank to the ship and ran to the cannon on the main deck (its the one to the right and slightly aft when you get on the ship facing to the rear) and manned the cannon that faces toward a slight saddle back on the hillside.&nbsp Once there you will be able to click on the cannon.&nbsp The ogre (Lolo the Lookout} that is standing on shore ran up the hill to the saddle-back where the cannon is facing and he waited there for a short time, then he ran back to his normal place.&nbsp Also several hands (sailors) repositioned to where the ogre normally stands. very shortly thereafter a Naga appeared at the saddle-back and I fired the cannon. The naga droped dead.&nbsp Following the first, more Naga appeared and each time I fired the cannon (from the deck of the ship)and they again dropped dead.&nbsp I continued to fire each time a (or group of) Naga appeared and they immediately droped dead.&nbsp I continued this until I got the message that the quest was completed.&nbsp I did not have to fight hand to hand any Naga.&nbsp I only used the cannon.&nbsp Got my ring (2 Str, 2 Agi, 10 Sta) and was finished.&nbsp Hope this helps to better explain how this quest is easily accomplished.

Once combat is intiated, the LOS issue is no longer in play and I was able to freely cast on them even though they were on the other side of a wall. Their corpses can be looted through the walls as well. The most annoying part of this quest was finding the Maiden's Folly charts. Comment4: I went in with a group last night. It wasn't easy. And we certainly had our due of dying. Before I began, here is the group breakdown. Lv41 warrior Lv38 assassin rogue (me) Lv36 assassin rogue Lv34 holy priest We had no problem clearing the Keep before reaching the final room. Both warrior and priest did an excellent job in their respective duties. Then, we reached the room where Otto and Falconcret are. And hell broke loose. There are 3 mobs (combination of syndicate rogue and magus) in that room, but outside otto and F's aggro area. So we pulled and killed these 3. Both Otto and F are lv40 elite. Standying next to them, there is one 37ish magus elite and one rogue elite guard. When you are facing them, F is standing in the middle of the platform. Otto and magus are to the left and syndicate rogue is to the right. After experimenting(dying) couple of times, we realized magus, otto and F are linked together. Any pull of one of these 3, the other 2 will respond. It is however possible to fight these 3 without aggro the syndicate rogue. (will explain this later) In term of killing difficulty, magus is the easiest. Otto is medium, F is as hard as a piece of rock. Failed attempt 1: 38 rogue sapped F. The group actually managed to kill Otto, but we could not kill magus and syndicate rogue fast enough. F woke up, joined the fight. TGW (total group wipe out). Failed attempt 2: 38 rogue on the way to sap F. Failed to sap, Otto, F and magus join the fight to slaughter poor 38 rogue. 38 rogue panicked, other group members out of team spirit joined in the fight. TGW. In this case, 38 rogue should either die or simply vanish without the entire group aggro mobs. Failed attempt 3: 38 rogue sapped F successfully. The group killed Otto and magus. And just when everybody just starts to pound&nbsp F, all roamers RESPAWN! A 4-on-1 fight turned into a 4-on-4+. The result? TGW. During this attempt, we realize F is as hard as a piece of rock and takes forever to kill. Failed attempt 4: Immediately rez in the hallway outside of room, we were detected by mobs. We actually managed to handle the mob pretty well, but we didn't anticipate the mob flee to aggro tons of other mobs. The result? TGW before even seeing Otto and F. Actually, 38 rogue managed to vanish in time to save himself. This act prompts the warrior player to claim: 'I want to be a rogue for my alt!' Successful attempt: We sent a general channel msg and got ourselves a lv36 mage. We went in again without any difficulty and clear other mobs to leave the last 4 on the platform. 38 rogue saped F. Mage sheep either magus or Otto. Sorry, i was so nervous after sapping F, i did not know who Mage sheep. The point is in this short span (sap only works for 15 sec if im not mistaken), the entire group focus the attack power on one mob. Once F wakes up, warrior and 2 rogues immediately focused on F. Boy, let me tell you it took us a lot of time to kill F. During the fight, 38 rogue realized mage was in trouble, being hit by Otto. 38 rogue left F to attract Otto away from mage. 38 rogue saved the mage and killed Otto. In the mean while, warrior and 36 rogue finished F. Summary: If you are lv50+ or have a 60 friend to watch over you, you pretty much can do whatever you want. But for a group similar to mine, here are some key points. 1. Don't aggro syndicate rogue guard. fighting 3 mobs is better than fighting 4. When you are facing mobs, keep the fight at the left half of the room or at the end of room. Because the syndicate rogue&nbsp is at the right half of the room. 2.
