Comment3: After dying three times, I was able to solo Blacklash and Hematus as a 54 shaman. If you've got the right talent spec (and 4-5 greater mana potions or better) you can take them out. [b]Some tips:[/b] - It's critical to have 5 ranks in Improved Lesser Healing Wave. 5 in Tidal Focus and Tidal Mastery will also help (think 'cookie-cutter NS build'). You'll be healing yourself a lot, and if you can't get your heals off while being struck, you're done for. - I did this with greater mana potions. 700-900 isn't a lot of mana, but two for each fight was enough for me. Having better mana potions will make your fights noticeably easier. - Knowing what to expect from the two dragonkin can help a bit, so here's the scoop: Blacklash uses a fire spell that always hits for exactly 500, while Hematus uses one that hits for 70-80 the first time and inflicts a magic effect that increases damage from each subsequent fire spell by 70-80. These effects stack, so Hematus' fire attacks will become more deadly as the fight goes on. The below strategy (necessarily) prolongs the fight by conserving mana for healing, so keep a close eye on your health as your fight with Hematus goes on. - Fire resistance totems might help you during this fight. Their effect should be more noticeable against Hematus because of the nature of his fire attack. I didn't use them because I wanted to save mana, but you might find that they pay for themselves in the form of damage prevented (and consequently, healing not needed). - I used a one-hander and shield for the fight. You might be able to use a two-hander, but keep in mind that both dragonkin have powerful melee attacks (I was taking about 250-300 damage per hit if memory serves, and that was with 45% damage reduction). [b]The strategy:[/b] Before you do anything, kill a few of the 44-45 dragonkin near the pillar so you have some room to work with. If you use LB or shocks to fight them, be sure to replenish your mana before using your runestones. When you use the runestones, back away from the pillar immediately, or Blacklash and Hematus will both spawn right on top of you. Run away at first if they start attacking you, then come back when you've shed aggro. Cast Rockbiter on your weapon. You can't afford to rely on Windfury's randomness, and Flametongue Weapon won't help at all (Blacklash and Hematus are immune to fire). Run just within aggro range of one (don't pull with a spell--save your mana) and pull him back from the pillar a short ways. Don't worry, you won't pull both of them. Now, drop a Strength of Earth totem (your only use of mana other than heals). If you want to use Fire Resistance totems, cast one now as well. Start swinging away with your weapon, and resist the temptation to use shocks to deal more damage. You don't have enough mana to kill them with spells, even combined with melee. Let your weapon deal all the damage. With Rockbiter and Strength of Earth, your damage-dealing will be solid and consistent. If you have ranks in Thundering Strikes, Flurry, and Parry, you'll do even better. When your health is knocked down to about 750, start spam-healing with LHW until you're back up to about 90%, then go back to attacking with your melee weapon. Don't fill your health back up all the way, or you'll waste mana. It's important to wait until your health gets low to start healing, because you want to regain as much mana as possible while you're swinging away with your weapon. Once you've used mana equal to the amount you can replenish with a potion (say you've used 900 and you have a greater mana potion), use one immediately, then go back to attacking. This way, you start that two-minute potion cooldown early and get the opportunity to use a second mana potion in the fight. More mana potions means more healing, since you'll be using almost all of it for LHW. Your SoE totem will probably expire two times (maybe three if you're not enhancement-specced) during the fight. When it expires, immediately recast it and heal yourself back to 90%. If you're using FR totems, recast them only when you recast SoE. FR will always disappear before SoE (at 54, your best FR should last 1 min., and SoE 1.5) but you'll still have FR down for two-thirds of the fight with this strategy. The idea is to minimize the amount of time you're not regaining mana while giving your melee attacks that extra punch you'll need to win. Follow the above, and you can pull it off. Each one will take 4-5 minutes, perhaps a bit less if you're enhancement-specced. (My Rockbiter wore off just as I killed each one, so I'm judging the length by that). Be sure to bring a few drinks with you, and 4-5 extra mana potions (just in case something goes wrong and you have to try again). Hopefully this will help someone (especially those who can't get groups together out in the Badlands--I never have luck forming groups there). -- [i]Charne, member of Charnel House, Shadow Council realm[/i]

Comment2: The Star of Xil'yeh comes from Grel'borg the Miser (https://classicdb.ch/?npc=2417), a named Ogre that patrols around the Alterac Mountains (where all the higher level elite 37-40 ogres are -- you can find him walking from the 'town hall' type building to the 'castle' building. Several quests involve killing Grel'borg, so don't be surprised to find other people also hunting him down at the same time. The Hand of Dagun comes from Dagun the Ravenous (https://classicdb.ch/?npc=2937), a named water giant that is summoned on an island to the north of Theramore. You will know it's the right island when you see a small glowy orb on an altar. To summon Dagun, you need to kill the Mirefin Oracles for a quest item called 'Enchanted Sea Kelp' -- it only drops from the oracles and may take a while (it's always taken me at least ten minutes of killing to get it on all of my alts). Once you have the Sea Kelp, you click on the altar and Dagun will rise up from the sea. Finally, the Legacy Heart comes from Mogh the Undying (https://classicdb.ch/?npc=1060), a named troll in central Stranglethorn Vale (you can find him in some ruins directly south of the Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound). I believe that he is the hardest to finish (unless in a group) since he's surrounded by many mobs that also respawn fairly quickly. Comment2: [b]The Tale of Sorrow[/b] ((spoiler alert!)) [small] Would you believe that in my darkest hour, at the apex of my being, I failed. As I fled from the wanton destruction of the forces that overwhelmed us, the only sounds I could hear were the screams of my soldiers and the rapid beat of my own heart. A short while later, I returned to the Blasted Lands in hopes of rescuing my men and restoring my honor. Instead I was captured and beaten until dead. What I found out during my inquisition and subsequent torture was horrifying. [i]Please continue, Hero...[/i] My captors were cruel beyond measure, <name>. They would alternate between Lieutenant Kirith and I, torturing one while the other watched. During a lull in the activity of an especially brutal day, Kirith told me what had happened to my men and a plan he had been formulating to free them from their masters. They suffered a fate far worse than death, or even the pain Kirith and I endured. [i]What could be worse than death?[/i] Neither you nor I could possibly imagine the pain an individual suffers when their soul is ripped from their body. They are not alive and by no means are they dead. Instead, they walk the land, servants of those that bind them to this world. Lord Razelikh, demonic overlord of all these lands, enslaved them all. Nine he took for his own, placing stones of binding near the Dark Portal. The remaining nine were divided up between his subordinates. [i]Subordinates?[/i] The archmage Allistarj of the Shadowsworn was granted three. Lady Sevine, warlock of the Shadowsworn was also granted three. The remaining three were given to Grol the Destroyer, lord of the the Dreadmaul ogres of these blasted lands. You see, <name>, without a soul, the body cannot be killed. The remnants of my men are now indestructible fighting units. Thankfully, they are bound in how far they can travel by the stones of binding. [i]What are the stones of binding?[/i] They are exactly what you need to destroy in order to free the regiment! As I had told you earlier, Kirith had a plan. Each of the servants does have a weakness. Punish their physical form in proximity of their stones until they are near the state of disintegration. It is at that point, and that point alone, that the stones of binding are vulnerable to attack. You must hurry to destroy the stones, however, as once the enslaved regain their composure, they will be invulnerable to harm once more. [i]You can count on me, Hero.[/i] I wish it were true, <name>, but it will take more than you alone to overcome the forces of Razelikh and his subordinates. Gather a suitable group of adventurers and would-be heroes and free my men of their eternal torture! Eighteen stones you must shatter. Fight hard and die with honor, <name>. [i]I shall.[/i] [/small]

Step 6: Giver: [url=https://classicdb.ch/npc=10156]Corporal Thund Splithoof[/url] Name: [url=https://classicdb.ch/quest=3515] Heroes of Old[/url] Description: Open the chest that spawns on the ground next to [url=https://classicdb.ch/npc=10156]Corporal Thund Splithoof[/url].&nbsp You'll get [url=https://classicdb.ch/item=2925]Shard of Afrasa[/url] from the chest as a reward. Step 8: Giver: [url=https://classicdb.ch/npc=61681]Spirit of Kirith[/url] Name: [url=https://classicdb.ch/quest=3636]The Cover of Darkness[/url] Description: Go back to the [url=https://classicdb.ch/npc=8449]Fallen Hero of the Horde[/url]. Step 9: Giver: [url=https://classicdb.ch/npc=8449]Fallen Hero of the Horde[/url] Name: [url https://classicdb.ch/quest=9479]The Demon Hunter] Description:&nbsp To come when I complete it! As far as I know, the remaining steps are as such: Talk to the demon hunter in Azshara, and he'll send you off to talk to some guy to get the true name of Razelikh, so he can make weapons to destroy him.&nbsp The guy who is supposed to tell you the name will have you go kill some hydra off the east coast of Azshara.&nbsp Then he'll tell you the name, which you bring back to the demon hunter.&nbsp The demon hunter will then send you off with some felhounds to collect Azsharite to make the weapons.&nbsp Once you collect it, he will make the weapons, and send you back to the Blasted Lands.&nbsp You will then have to destroy the 3 servants of Razelikh - Sevine, Allistarj, and Grol in order to collect 3 parts of an amulet which will allow you to gain access to Razelikh himself.&nbsp This can only be done with the weapons you just received.&nbsp Once you've got the amulet, you will be able to use it on the various Runes of the Defiler which can be found around the Mound of the Defiler.&nbsp This will teleport you up to the top, where you will have to destroy Razelikh himself.&nbsp End of story.&nbsp I think.

Instructions: Bring ten Basilisk Brains and two Vulture Gizzards to Bloodmage Lynnore. Basilisk Brain (10) Vulture Gizzard (2)
Progress: Have you returned with the requested organs?
Comment1: This is one of a group of quests you can get from two druids at a campfire just inside the border of the Blasted Lands. They are not difficult but I had a few problems: - You need to kill a few boars, a few Snickerfangs, a lot of basilisks, some vultures and (in my case) a whole bunch of scorpions. The boars were easy, but the drop rate on the others is about 6 to 1 or higher. I never was able to get any of the scorpions to drop anything and only completed one quest because someone else had spares. She was having no problem with the scorpions but hadn't been able to get anything from the vultures. - In the beginning (the first day), all animals but the scorpions dropped lots of junk which was nonetheless worth 3-15S at the vendor in the Keep. But there was a lot of junk, so be prepared with at least one empty 12-slot bag or you'll be commuting to the vendor every ten minutes.&nbsp Later on (the second day), most of the animals started dropping nothing. That's right - nothing niente, nada. My 47 Druid is a skinner, so it was not a total loss but those with other trades better be prepared to be disappointed. - The second day, the basilisks (there were initially about 9-10), which had been respawning almost faster than you would like (on top of you, for example), slowed down and then stopped. When you need 60 to get 10 quest items, this is a problem. When I left (I fortunately got my last quest item from the last basilisk), there were none left and none had respawned. A glitch? Maybe. Overfishing? Maybe, but I almost didn't get that quest done after 2 days. - The boars, snickerfangs, basilisks and vultures are 47-49. The scorpions are 50-52. For my 47 Druid, the scorpions were not difficult (druids can regenerate health of course) but certainly time-consuming, taking about 2-3 times as long to kill. Then they would drop nothing. Again and again. The only consolation was the scorpid scale, but if you're not a skinner, get ready for a plateful of frustration. The rewards are approximately 4400XP (not bad) and a few buffs. I abandoned two of the four quests when I just couldn't face another scorpion with no quest item. These are not awful quests but pack a bag and be prepared to spend the weekend with these mobs.

Be sure to initiate the attack while near the Servant's Binding Stone, otherwise, you will not be able to destroy it. Step 5: Giver: Fallen Hero of the Horde Name: Heroes of Old Description: Talk to Corporal Thund Splithoof, another ghost who will now spawn a few feet away, on the other side of the road from the Giver: Fallen Hero of the Horde. You'll get Shard of Afrasa from the chest as a reward. Step 7: Giver: Fallen Hero of the Horde Name: Kirith Description: Find Kirith the Damned in the cave in the eastern wall of Serpent's Coil. He's a 55 Elite freakin huge Felhound. Kill him, and the Spirit of Kirith appears. Talk to him to complete the quest and begin the next part. Step 8: Giver: Spirit of Kirith Name: The Cover of Darkness Description: Go back to the Fallen Hero of the Horde. Comment1: Posting for those of you who don't have UIs. The servants of Razelikh are found around the dark portal. Watch out for the Felguard patrol around the portal. Servants of Allistarj are all found along the eastern wall of the zone, stopping just before Nethergrade Keep. Servants of Servine are found along the wall north of the entrance to the tainted scar (which is the western wall) Servants of Grol are the most difficult to find, in my opinion. You can find one in a cave guarded by ogres in the mountain off the path to the tainted scar. Just follow the path until you begin travelling west, then go north and look for a lone mountain, Once you find ogres, you've found the one servant. The other place to find them are Grol's fort, located in the northwest corner of the zone. You'll know you found it because you'll see a tower and a base with horde banners. The servants are in there. To get there, go west along the northern wall from the entrance of the zone. A note that the servants will NOT die until you smash the crystal, and the stun effect on them wears off after around 30 seconds. If you're having trouble smashing the crystal, remember that you have to stun it (Drop around 85% of it's health) next to the crystal in order to smash it. For those who want coords, 49.7, 43.8 is where the lone Servant Of Grol is.The dark portal is around 58.8, 51.6. Frydebo provided coords to the other servents, as well as the Grol fort. Happy hunting!

Comment1: Temerus, one of the Black Dragonflight, posted as the guardian of Blasted Lands is indeed kitable. The strategy is tough though as with any mob if you get too far away from him (roughly 70 yards) he will drop agro/target and return to his ominous patrol route, so the idea with kiting him to Stormwind is to stay inside that range and keep a hold with a DoT or periodic shots. Before we continue, let’s say this is best done with a Hunter and AotC. My best suggestion is to take Teremus up through Blasted Lands, through the Swamp of Sorrows, into the Deadwind Pass, across Duskwood to the north, cross the river into Elwynn Forest, and complete the path to Stormwind. Alternatively you could drag Teremus across Duskwood, and into Westfall if you're having trouble with crossing the river or want to stay on a land-route. So Teremus is about to cross the river into Elwynn Forest, Good! You're almost there! Congratulations, you've successfully kited a dragon, nonetheless one of the malicious Deathwing following, to Stormwind. The guards should mobilize almost immediately to cull the threat and low level players should parade through the streets in utter fear. (The entire ordeal takes about 30 minutes) There should be some [url=https://classicdb.ch/?i=Flawless%20Draenethyst%20Sphere]Flawless Draenethyst Sphere[/url] on his body if you have accepted the quest: [url=https://classicdb.ch/?s=To%20Serve%20Kum'isha]To Serve Kum'isha[/url] -or- [url=https://classicdb.ch/?s=Kum'isha's%20Endeavors]Kum'isha's Endeavors[/url] If this is a repeat attempt or there is more than one of the sphere's on his body (which is HIGHLY probable) Kum'isha is located in the central area of the map in Blasted Lands, slightly northwest of The Dark Portal and southwest of Nethergarde Keep. When you complete the quest a short interlude should start with Kum'isha sending his brethren into a portal. You should be able to spot him at a small camp with many ‘Lost One’ Draenei NPC’s. So fantastic! Spheres are collected and turned in, you should have one or more of the [url=https://classicdb.ch/?i=Emerald%20Encrusted%20Chest]Emerald Encrusted Chest[/url] in your bags now, each one contains a Superior or Epic quality item ranging from level 40 to 50 the odds are endless, the first time I killed Teremus, it gave me some stuff: [url=https://classicdb.ch/?i=Wyrmslayer%20Spaulders]Wyrmslayer Spaulders[/url] [url=https://classicdb.ch/?i=Executioner's%20Cleaver]Executioner's Cleaver[/url] [url=https://classicdb.ch/?i=Serpent%20Slicer]Serpent Slicer[/url] [url=https://classicdb.ch/?i=Lei%20of%20Lilies]Lei of Lilies[/url] To our Horde brothers and sisters, I’m sorry, but I could not think of a way off the top of my head to make it easy for you to make a quick kill on this treacherous Teremus. The ‘normal’ way to get the spheres involves a party of about 5 level 60’s or a diminishing number if they are level 60+. I hope this helped someone out there, may my fellows Hunt dearly and loot daily.

Comment1: This quest at first seems pretty daunting, but it's actually quite simple and just a little time consuming once you know how to acquire all of the mats. The effort is well worth it, having a +100 hp enchant to your legs and head piece will make a big difference! First, night dragon's breath can be acquired in Felwood. Depending on whether your Alliance or Horde, you'll have to talk to the appropiate NPC to begin the cleansing of Felwood, which will involve you kill the Warpwood Shredder's in the northern part of the zone to collect shards. The Horde NPC that begins this quest is right off the road, a little further north than the druid tents and to the left. Once you've completed this first stage, you'll be given a Cenarion Beacon (hang on to this, you need it to collect corrupted soul shards!). Now you must collect six corrupted soul shards and in exchange, you'll receive two salves (And you need four to collect night dragon's breath). Corrupted soul shards have a chance to drop off any mob in the zone. Once you have four salves, you can cleanse the night dragon's breath plants. They are located at the following coords: 1st Location: 35,60 2nd Location: 50,30 3rd Location: 40,78 4th Location: 42,13 Once you've cleansed the plant, you can collect the dragon's breath (usually yields 4-5 per use). Once you've collected from a plant, it takes about a half an hour before you can collect again. The nice thing is, if you hang around and wait, you can just keep collecting, you don't need any more salve! So I'll usually just hang around and keep collecting from the same plant. The rest of the quest is easy. Hop on over to the Blasted Lands (Horde have a flight path to Stonard in Swamp of Sorrows, Alliance has Nethergard Keep right in the zone I believe). A blood elf in the ruins near the entrance gives the quest for the lung juice. The scorpids are right near the entrance with the hyena's and vultures and the drop rate is fairly high. A little further south near defiler's rise you can find the basilisks, who also have a fairly high drop rate, along with hellboars, whose drop rates are quite a bit lower (This is what you'll be grinding on for the longest time). Remember when you're grinding that the hellboars, basilisks, and felhoudnds all share the same spawn point, so kill everything, it'll keep the hellboars respawning much quicker! There's also another variety of boar further east that will drop the blasted boar lungs as well. Once you've gathered everything, hope back over to Mathredis and you're done!

Comment3: As a level 33 shadow priest, I believe it's possible to solo Eliza. I (as a level 33 shadow priest) was able to bring her to around 80% health, before a random Shaman jumped in to help and finish her off. But, to be honest, I did not need any help. Here is the synopsis of the strategy I used: 1) Run a little distance from grave after opening. 2) Shackle Eliza. 3) Mind blast Eliza. 4) repeat step 2 Here is the strategy in a little more detail. As many people have already mentioned above, Eliza does two things: She will cast frostbolt / frostnova and during the encounter she will summon three undead guardians, whom I believe are level 29. Because she will try to frostbolt you when you are out of melee range, the basic idea of my strategy was to cast a direct damage spell on her, then immediately shackle her before she can finish casting frostbolt. The shackling has the affects of interrupting her spell casting, allowing you some time to regenerate mana, and preventing her from summoning her undead friends. That's basically all there is to it. When she's shackled, she can't summon her friends. When she's casting frostbolt, she can't summon her friends. A few things to note. You want to cast a quick damage spell, like mind blast or smite. If you mind flay, you will probably not have the time to shackle her before her frostbolt finishes casting. You also don't want to use a spell like Shadow Word: Pain, for obvious reasons (You are using shackle!). You also probably want to wait for the 'Five Second Rule' http://www.wowwiki.com/Formulas:Mana_RegenFive_Second_Rule to fade so that you regenerate some mana. Else, if you decide to spam shackle / mind blast, you run the risk of running out of mana. Good luck.

Name: Mor'Ladim
Instructions: Kill Mor'Ladim, then return his skull to Commander Althea Ebonlocke in Darkshire. Mor'Ladim's Skull
Progress: I don't blame you if you're having trouble with him, <name>. Some of our strongest Watchers have been lost to Mor'Ladim.
Comment1: I was able to solo Mor'Ladim as a level 33 shadow priest, without using potions or anything special. Well, I used the Draenei racial symbol of hope, but after you read what I did, you will find that any priest is capable of soloing Mor'Ladim. The basic strategy for a priest is to 'shackle-kite' him. You want to open with a direct damage spell like mind blast or smite. Or, I suppose if you like, you could also try mind flay. Then once Mor'Ladim starts chasing you, shackle him. Get a little range, wait for some mana to regenerate, then re-open with another direct damage spell. A few things to note: If you constantly damage and shackle, you will probably run out of mana. So, you really want to wait for mana to regenerate during the shackle. Also, it might take you a little while to wear Mor'Ladim down with this strategy. But ultimately, you will able to solo him. If you have 5 talent points in shadow-weaving, you might be better off using mind blast so that the shadow vulnerability debuff stacks on Mor'Ladim. It's helpful, but not necessary. Also, since you are using shackle, I hope it is obvious that you don't want to do something like, Shadow Word: Pain Mor'Ladim. It will break the shackle for the duration. There is also a little court yard in Raven Hill Cemetary, which features a broken statue and a cobbled area around it. I found this to be relatively free from all the other monsters roaming the cemetary, and it's a good spot to shackle-kite Mor'Ladim. Just kite him to one side, shackle, and then run to the opposite side. Hope this was helpful.

Comment1: Ok, so I tried a little experiment to see if the Craftsman's Writ quests are worth repeating. I'm a L60 Warlock with 300 Tailoring/300 Skinning. The first quest I got was for tailoring (Brightcloth Pants) so that wasn't hard for me to complete and didn't cost me much to speak of. I'm sure my gains were whatever the typical first turn-ins are. For accepting the 2nd crafting quest (therby consuming the valor token), I got +11 rep (I'm currently at honored). The second quest was for Rugged Armor Kits, which I can't make so I went off to the AH to check them out. About 1.18g on my server and I needed 25. For the sake of the experiment, I bought them, having 3 kits left over owing to the way stacks were offered at the time. I used the 3 extras on my non-enchanted items for +120 armor (not bad at all for a squishy warlock). When I turned in the quest (therby consuming the 25 kits and the writ itself), I received +55 rep (and I forgot whether or not I got any gold for the turn-in, even though in retrospect, that was a pretty important detail...doh). Anyway. rep for accepting quest: +11 total cost of items: 33.04g armor gained: 120 rep for completing quest: +55 gold received for completing quest: ? (if any) So, for the sake of comparison, let's say I just used a Valor Token and bought 3 rugged armor kits... rep for using a token: +27 total cost of items: 3.54g armor gained: 120 The difference is -29.5g +39 rep or .76g per rep point Of course, all of these figures will vary depending on your current reputation level, market prices of items, and what crafting quest the guy gives you, but I'm putting this up as a 'for instance.' Conclusion: In this experiment, I ended up paying .76g for each rep point I gained over and above what I would have gained by just using the Valor Token. Now, I prefer to run around and kill monsters and sell what they drop in order to make money rather than paying gold for rep points, but some players might be happy to do that. Decide for yourself whether or not it's worth repeating, but for my money and time, I'll just be using the tokens I get for now...
Comment2: Many complain about how arbitrary the writ rewards are. After all, most of the time you're not going to get a writ for something you can make yourself. Fortunately, you can buy and sell them on the AH. They do still sell, even today, though it sometimes takes awhile. If you're looking to buy one, you can usually get them on the cheap, usually a gold or two. Whether or not they're worth the effort depends on your situation. The insignia items aren't worth much these days, but you still might want the [item=22679] or reputation from first turn-ins. If you're leveling a profession, you may have to make some of these items anyway as part of the grind. In that case, writs may be more convenient.

Other notes on this. Duo'd with a 65 frost mage and a 58 resto shaman. Once Redpath dies, [b]do not abandon the quest unless everything despawns[/b]. He died and I unknowingly abandoned the quest, thinking I'd failed, but everything continued to spawn. You will need to look for the Corrupted Redpath and defeat him when Captain Redpath despawns, as his death is scripted into the event. Keep him up until he despawns, however, as letting him get killed by the NPCs will fail the quest. The two ghost NPCs spawned after we'd killed Corrupted Redpath, and everything else despawned, leading me to believe that the quest was not failed to begin with. In fact, everything would *not* despawn until Corrupted Redpath was dead. That includes the Darrowshire Defenders; they kept spawning regardless of there only being the undead mobs around. You can heal both Davil and Redpath. If you are a shaman, you can hit either of them with Chain Heal and it will jump to members of your party. However, you cannot hit your party members with Chain Heal and expect it to jump to either Davil or Redpath. Also, you can die during this fight, and as long as Redpath or Davil are still alive when you resurrect, you should be able to finish (there was one point where both the mage and I died, but the battle continued). There are many opportunities to rest and get mana while you are completing this quest, so I would suggest taking every opportunity possible. You should, however, be careful of the Bloodletters; they hit really hard (they were hitting my shaman for about 500-700 in mail) and move rather quickly. However, they (and Corrupted Redpath) are susceptible to snares (Frost Shock, Earthbind, etc.). Edit: Upon further investigation, Chain Heal [b]will[/b] jump from party (and non-party) members to both Davil and Captain Redpath. It is still limited by the range thing, though, so if you're doing this with a bunch of ranged people, you may be better of with LHW/HW instead of Chain Heal. If it does, any bodyguards that were killed will repop. So you can't just kill a bodyguard and run off, then kill another etc. It won't work. Once the courier gets back on her horse, all escorts will respawn. Unless you have a full group, I would suggest waiting for the courier to reach Corin's Crossing, since they will attack mobs there. Wait behind them until they aggro a few mobs at once, then engage. This way you won't have to deal with all of them at once. It won't buy you much time, but trying to take on 5 is a pain.

Comment2: Was in the area as a 36/37 warrior, so I hung around the town hall and watched / helped lvl 20-25 who were doing this quest. It was raining in Hillsbrad Foothills... My observations: -- Lvl 20-25 PCs aggro in a huge (make that HUGE) radius in this area. Or more correctly, the mobs are tightly confined in a small area, and there are several places where view is obscured, and it's really easy to aggro an add in the heat of battle. -- It is not uncommon for 4-6 mobs to aggro to lvl 20-25 PCs in the town hall courtyard and in the council chamber room of the town hall. For example, just outside the entrance of the compound it's likely that at a minimum a councilman and 2-3 footmen will engage the PCs, and given the difficulty of taking them down, runners and / or patrols will probably pull in more mobs. A councilman will aggro and begin lobbing frost spells, likely locking down one or more PCs with 'frost boots' -- then you can't pursue the runners. At the doorway to the town hall there are two guards + patrols + at least one councilman who will easily aggro if any one of them is engaged. The courtyard is full of footmen and more council members who may aggro off of runners. As a lvl 24 squishy and I were leaving the town hall 6 or 7 mobs aggroed to us, and it was all I could do to keep her alive as they aggroed to her. Later a 20 and 25 engaged the two footmen at the doorway and a councilman off to the right out of view aggroed and started blindsiding the squishy with frost spells (sometimes I wish that WoW aggro would handle line-of-sight better -- it's frustrating to suddenly have frostbolts coming out of a wall at you). Inside the two rooms leading to the council chambers is a single guard in each room no problem if you take them down without allowing them to run. Lastly, the nightmarish council chamber must be dealt with. I don't have an accurate count of the mobs in the room, but I do know that there is a footman by the door, a footman + council member in the back corner, the clerk in the middle of the room, the mayor at the far podium, and I think there are a couple more footmen and another councilman in the middle. So about eight mobs. As a level 36 warrior it was not a problem since I could take three mobs at a time, hamstring, cut them down, and not aggro others in the room. When a lvl ~25 enters the room the whole place lights up, and you'll have at least six mobs on the PC. If you can't stealth, then my advice is to enlist a lvl ~35+ to help clear the mobs, or get together a big group of lvl 20-25 -- I'd suggest a party of six at that level. For the lvl 20-25 with the Battle of Hillsbrad and Dangerous quests grouping with a lvl ~35+ you might have to kill the clerk, major, and some council members off of respawns, and the XP of the lvl 20-25 may be reduced a lot, but a lot of frustration will be saved. Good luck...

Comment1: Run north through Alterac Mountains, through Strahnbrad and through the valley with all the mountain lions/Syndicate personell. You will come up on a farmhouse near the shore of the lake. The Syndicate mobs here are 39-40 and tend to be stealthed. There are two right outside the door, and you will likely have to fight both at once. Once the door is cleared, be ready to fight two more at the same time right inside the door. It's best to pull them outside so you don't aggro the other mobs in the house. Once you dispatch those, you'll have to deal with Nagaz, a level 40 orc (part of an Alliance quest). Once he's down, there should be one more stealthed mob near the stairs to deal with. Upstairs, there is one stealthed mob and one regular mob. You will have to deal with both at the same time. Pull them downstairs so you don't accidentally aggro Lord Perenolde. Once you've finished them off, charge Perenolde. If you have never fought a paladin in PvP, this is a good preview. He has bubble shields and heals, and he's not shy about using them. He also has a sleep spell, so if you are in a group, expect to occassionally be down one person until sleep breaks. He is level 41, but he's not elite. Once you get his health down fairly low, he starts to flee, but he often runs back into the bedroom, which lets you pick him off at your leisure. Talk to the girl in the bedroom to finish the quest.

Progress: You must make haste, <class>. I shudder to think what the humans might be doing to Drull and Tog'thar.
Comment1: The premise of this quest is simple. Free two orcs from imprisonment. To complete this task, you must find four key personnel. [ul] [li][url=https://classicdb.ch/?npc=2239]Drull[/url], an Orc that you need to free.[/li] [li][url=https://classicdb.ch/?npc=2238]Tog'thar[/url], another Orc that you need to free.[/li] [li][url=https://classicdb.ch/?npc=2427]Jailor Eston[/url], drops the necessary [url=https://classicdb.ch/?item=3467]Dull Iron Key[/url], used to free Drull.[/li] [li][url=https://classicdb.ch/?npc=2428]Jailor Marlgen[/url], drops the necessary [url=https://classicdb.ch/?item=3499]Burnished Gold Key[/url], used to free Tog'thar.[/li] [/ul] First, a note on freeing the Orcs. On occasion, using the key on the [url=https://classicdb.ch/?object=1722]Locked Ball and Chain[/url] will produce a 'Failure!' message. If this happens, don't worry. Just keep using it. It appears that the mechanic emulates the lockpicking mechanic, so this is pretty much expected. I cannot confirm that these can be lockpicked, but others on this page claim it can be, at ~100 skill. I would also reccomend going to Tog'thar first, as one of the spawns for Jailor Eston is nearby, and dropping down to Drull when the jailor is up near Tog'thar achives little more than a need to slaughter your way back up. Not that a slaughter is a bad thing, mind you. The Orcs are static spawns. The Jailors, however, have been switched to dynamic spawns. Each have a set of potential spots in which they may spawn. WoWHead claims three, but I've only seen them each at two. I slaughtered the poor fellows for a good hour, so I feel that these two are accurate. [b]Finding Drull:[/b] To find Drull, enter Durnholde Keep from the South. There will be a bridge in front of you. Jump the wall, right on the left side of the bridge. Be careful, however, as there are a few (Usually one or two, more if you have a pet and forget to dismiss it, as it will take the long way and bring some company.) mobs that likely will aggro when you do so. Face West, and directly ahead of you there should be two buildings. The closest one (which runs East to West, not North to South like the furthest one.) is your building of interest. Inside, at the far end, is Drull. Sometimes there's a [url=https://classicdb.ch/?object=2850]Solid Chest[/url] next to him, too. [b]From Drull to Tog'thar:[/b] To arrive at Tog'thar from Drull, exit the building that contains Drull via the doorway furthest from him, on the northern face of the building. Face East from the steps. Fight your way East, and under the bridge. Once you have passed under the bridge, follow the Northern wall until you come to a pair of steps leading up the wall. Take these steps. Once you reach the top, face Northwest, and you should see a road. Go to the road and travel along it to the South. You will eventually reach a 'T'-Style intersection. Read on in the 'Finding Tog'thar' section directly below from said intersection to find Tog'thar. [b] Finding Tog'thar:[/b] To find Tog'thar, again enter Durnholde Keep from the South. This time cross the bridge and immediately turn to the East. Fight your way along this path until you reach a 'T'-Style intersection. One path will head West and up, the other will head North, and slightly down. Take the Western path. A very short distance up this path, you will encounter the gate to the Keep itself, which is now destroyed. Fight your way through the arch. Tog'thar should be 25-30 yards north of you, easily visible. As mentioned previously, finding the Orcs is good and all, but it's rather moot if you have no way to free them. Both of the jailors appear to have a spot very close to the Orc they're holding captive, and one that takes a bit of searching. Both are listed here. [b]Finding Jailor Esten:[/b][ol] [li]Right in front of Drull. Just find Drull, and he'll be ~5 yards away.[/li] [li]Traverse to Tog'thar. Right before you reach the entrance to the Keep itself, there will be a small group of Syndicate henchmen near some trees. He can sometimes be found there.[/li] [/ol] [b]Finding Jailor Marlgen:[/b][ol] [li]Follow the directions to Tog'thar. However, once you reach the entrance to the Keep, do not enter, but continue along the path past the keep. Fight your way until you reach a defunct tower. He can often be found right in front of it.[/li] [li]Reach Tog'thar. When you pass thru the arch, he'll be right in front of you, slightly off to your right.[/li] [/ol] Congratulations! You've just committed a jailbreak! Revel in your self-worth and value to the Horde! On an added note, while you're here you can complete the following quests as well: [ul] [li][url=https://classicdb.ch/?quest=549]WANTED: Syndicate Personnel[/url][/li] [li][url=https://classicdb.ch/?quest=1066]Blood of Innocents[/url][/li] [/ul] ::EDIT:: Talk about feeling like an idiot -- I've fixed the West<->East mixup. Let's blame my parents for teaching me left was right, and right was left. Yeah. It's their fault (29-07-08). I've also updated this for the jailor's dynamic spawns (29-07-08). ...And touched it up, made it less confusing (29-07-08).

Forging ahead up the hill I found Margren (or whatever the 2nd jailer's name is) and got the gold key. He was right next to one of the prisoners. I failed the first attempt to open the ball and chain but was successful the 2nd time. Went to the edge of the upper level and moved my cursor over all the huts in the lower level until I located my prisoner. Hopped down from the edge (rather than clearing to the hut from the ramp on the south side), killed the several NPCs in the general area and found Jailer Eston again, this time standing next to my 2nd prisoner. After you turn these in, he sends you to Dire Maul library to talk to Falrin Treeshaper. What you are looking for is in short terms, tall and slender Egyptian-style obelisks standing approximately 10 meters high with a light blue gem embedded near the top, not a Runestone as we know it in Europe, or a 'Rune' as we know it in Europe. Comment3: Word of advice to hunters: tame Bellygrub, he makes an awesome pet, for MM at least and probably other specs as well. When leveling a marksman spec hunter it's extremely important for your pet to hold aggro from your ranged DPS; if your pet loses aggro, fights can go from 'afkshot for a few seconds, then loot' to 'sacrifice pet just to get away alive' very quickly. Boars are the only pets in the game at the moment with Charge, which makes the pet rush toward the target, immobilizing it for a quick second. Charge also increases the pet's attack power for the next attack by a lot, and given the way Growl works, the boar will typically charge the enemy, taunt, and instantly have around 1k-1.5k threat - basically, you wouldn't be able in most cases to pull aggro off of your pet from then on before the enemy dies. Boars can also learn Gore, which is an instant, zero-cooldown focus ability that does damage (also known as a focus dump) that will make talents like Go for the Throat well worth getting. They can also get Bite (a 10-sec cooldown damage ability) and Dash (which shares a cooldown with Charge, so it's not that great). They also have decent health and armor. Once you've got decent ranged damage, all you really need to watch for is the occasional resist on the first taunt and the mobs around you and your pet. Bellygrub comes with Charge and Gore automatically, and you won't be able to get another rank of either until around level 50. Learn Bite from a spider in Arathi Highlands around level 32 and you're set for a long time...

Comment1: You'll need to enter the keep on Fenris Isle and get to the roof. Enter through the entrance and take the following path: left->right->right->go up the stairs->left->left->go up the stairs. If you die making your way up, head right to the roof before ressing and you can bypass the gnolls. Once you reach the roof, cross it and it's in the tower - hovering your mouse over the towers on the roof will light up 'Dusty Shelf'.
Comment2: The shelf is hard to find but with a little exploration it is possible. Enter the keep and fight your way to the back where the stairs lead up to the second floor. Turn left immediately after going up the stairs, go the the hallway in front of you, kill any mobs near you, and turn left again. In front of you should be a doorway with maybe one or two mobs in there as well. Kill the mobs and enter the room. You are now in the North East tower. There should be a set of stairs in the room follow them up to the top killing any mobs you come in contact with. When the stairs end exit the tower through the doorway and you will now be on the roof. Cross the roof to the other side (west) and kill any mobs near the enterance to the South West tower. Enter the tower through the doorway, again killing any mobs, and directly to the left of the doorway (as you enter it) is the dusty shelf. Like I said kinda tricky but with some exploration you can do it.
Comment3: Just let yourself die next to the base of the south west tower - can be outside, no problem. Then - as a ghost, go upstairs untill you find the niche (three shelves). Get in to the rooftop between the two towers (the south west and south east) and - on the farthest corner, where the guards do not spot you - get ressurrected. Then - it�s easy - just get the first guard, get the second and go for the shelves. The quest it�s yours!
Comment4: I did not find the above directions to be correct. You need the SW tower, not the SE one. From the entrance, turn right, left, left, right and go upstairs, right, right, upstairs, and cross the passage to the SW tower. The niche is in the bookshelf to the left of the entrance.
Comment5: As a ghost, enlarge your minimap and find your way up to the southwest tower. The green shelves are at the very top of the tower being guarded by one mob next to the shelves and another one walking up and down the stairs. Don't resurect yet. Go onto the bridge that connects the two s.west, and s. east towers and hop onto the roof that connects the south towers to the north towers. If you died at street level at the top of the stairs before you entered the building, you should be able to res by standing on top of the roof (or well, you can res anywhere but the roof is the safest cuz there's no mobs on there). Once you res, heal, buff, kill the one mob that's walking around, and kill the one that's guarding the shelves. open the shelves and you're done.

Comment1: The amount of patrols are [b]BRUTAL[/b] in this area, inside the 'castle' grounds you can [i]easily[/i] aggro 3 or 4 different patrols in the time it takes to kill one mob just getting into the building.&nbsp Each mob has a pet or can summon a pet, so you could very easily be up against 6 mobs in a few seconds if you're not careful. Once you're in the building you will have to fight off [i]at least[/i] 4 to 5 mobs (with pets) at the same time since they will all aggro if you attack any of them.&nbsp It cannot be done solo by fighting your way through them without be an excessively high level, which would be pointless since the reward isn't worth waiting until you're high enough level to solo the area. By the time you're at a level to realistically attempt doing this quest you could be grouping up and running WC for the Leaders of the Fang quest and a much better reward. If you must do this mission follow the above advice, rush in, get into the corner of the 'stage' (not the bookcase corner, the other corner - the corner opposite the stairs leading up to the stage area) and rez there.&nbsp You'll only aggro Ataeric that way.&nbsp He shoots you with frost bolts and will freeze you in place with frost nova, but if you rez, target and start attacking him, and use a healing pot as needed, you should be able to take him down. I soloed this as a level 20 Warlock (no pet since I rezed in the corner), wasn't easy, died 3 times figuring out the lay of the land.&nbsp Finally just rushed in, died, soul stone rezed, killed Ataeric and hearthstoned out.

Comment1: This information should be accurate as of patch 1.11.2 [b]Morrowgrain quests:[/b] The Morrowgrain quests can be quite involved as there are two quest givers and turn-in locations. Also the rewards given are different for both turn-in locations. The actual process to get Morrowgrain takes several steps as well. The quest line starts with a quest called [b]Morrowgrain Research[/b] which is given out by Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm. Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm may be found at Anonymous coordinates 35,8 in Darnassas. He is located at the top level of the Druid complex (Cenarion Enclave). He asks you to take a packet of 20 [b]Tharlendris seeds[/b] to the middle level of the same complex and give them to Mathrengyl Bearwalker who gives out the next quest. That quest is also titled [b]Morrowgrain Research[/b] (Just to confuse things). The second [b]Morrowgrain Research[/b] quest has you take a special pouch called an [b]Evergreen Pouch[/b] (Provided when you receive the quest) and put into it 2 [b]Un'Goro Soil[/b] (Collected in Un�Goro Crater) and 1 of the [b]Tharlendris seeds[/b] from the packet (First 10 seeds given to you with the quest). With 2 Un'Goro Soil in your backpack along with 1 Tharlendris seed, you right click the Evergreen pouch. The pouch will plant the seed into the soil and grow an [b]Evergreen Herb Casing[/b]. When you right click the casing, out will pop a random herb. One of the herbs grown may be [b]Morrowgrain[/b]. When you have 10 of them you turn them in to complete the quest. You can repeat this quest as many times as desired. You can grow a new Evergreen Herb Casing once every 10 minutes. There is a second parallel quest line involving Morrowgrain as well. This chain of quests starts with either Innkeeper Shyria in the Inn of Feathermoon Stronghold in Feralas or with Tannysa the Herbalism trainer in the Mage Quarter of Stormwind. Talking to either of these two people will give you a quest titled [b]Jonespyre's Request[/b] which asks you to go talk to Quintis Jonespyre in the Feathermoon Stronghold in Feralas. Quintis Jonespyre will then give you the repeatable quest titled [b]The Mystery of Morrowgrain[/b]. This quest is identical to the above quest (Use the Evergreen pouch to grow an Evergreen Herb Casing from 1 Tharlendris seed and 2 Un'Goro Soil and out pops a random herb) except you only need to turn in 5 Morrowgrain. In the end, you now have two locations to turn in Morrowgrain: Turning in [b]5 Morrowgrain[/b] to Quintis Jonespyre in the Feathermoon Stronghold in Feralas will give you [b]25 reputation with Darnassas[/b]. In addition he also gives you another packet of 10 Tharlendris seeds so you can go out and grow more. Turning in [b]10 Morrowgrain[/b] to Mathrengyl Bearwalker at the Cenarion Enclave in Darnassas will earn you [b]50 reputation with Darnassas[/b]. In addition he also gives you a [b]Cenarion Circle Cache[/b]. Opening this will provide a random number of items as loot. Typically there are 4-8 items in the bag although I have seen only 1 before and as many as 14 per Cenarion Circle Cache. The Cenarion Circle Cache typically contains food, drinks, scrolls, potions, herbs etc. For a list of the types of items found in each Cache please see the following link: https://classicdb.ch/item=5533 You can get a lot of really good stuff in these caches. [b]Where to get Un�Goro Soil:[/b] Un�Goro Soil is found in Un�Goro Crater (Southern end of Kalimdor). Un�Goro Soil is dropped (from Dinosaurs) throughout the crater. Just run around the zone (Avoiding being stepped on or eaten by the dinosaurs) and right click the dirt piles you see laying on the ground. Un�Goro Soil is often found in the AH as well. Un�Goro Soil stacks up to 100 units per stack now. [b]Where to get Tharlendris seeds:[/b] Tharlendris seeds may be purchased from either of the two turn-in NPCs or you can get them as part of your turn-in reward when you turn in Morrowgrain to Quintis Jonespyre in the Feathermoon Stronghold in Feralas. [b]Where to get an Evergreen pouch:[/b] An Evergreen pouch is given to you when you receive the second Morrowgrain Research quest. Replacements may be purchased (For around 1 Gold) from either of the two turn-in NPCs. [b]The rewards:[/b] Once you have grown Evergreen Herb Casings and retrieved the herbs out of the casings you can either turn in the Morrowgrain for reputation, sell it on the AH or use it to make Cenarion Herb Bags (Manufacturing 20 slot herb bags requires 8 Morrowgrain as one of the materials to make 1 bag). In addition the loot from the Cenarion Circle Cache is typically valued at several gold and may be used or sold as needed. In addition to growing Morrowgrain, the Evergreen Herb Casings often contains other herbs which may be used or sold as needed. How much Morrowgrain or other herbs you grow and which types depend on your Herbalism skill. As an example, I dropped the Herbalism profession completely and grew 65 Evergreen Herb Casings. Out of those casings I received the following: Morrowgrain 50 Kingsblood 6 Gromsblood 3 Earthroot 9 Briarthorn 8 Liferoot 7 Mageroyal 5 Sungrass 2 For a total of 90 herbs averaging 1.48 herbs per Evergreen Herb Casing. For the most part these are lower-end herbs. I relearned Herbalism and worked it up to 300 skill level. I then grew 65 more Evergreen Herb Casings. This is what I received from those: Morrowgrain 75 Kingsblood 22 Gromsblood 2 Liferoot 6 Sungrass 5 Stranglekelp 13 Blindweed 5 Goldthorn 22 Firebloom 2 For a total of 152 herbs averaging 2.34 herbs per Evergreen Herb Casing. For the most part these are higher-end herbs. The maximum  of herbs out of any single casing is 5. As I went up in skill level, the numbers and types of herbs increased steadily. All in all 300 Herbalism will result in a 50% increase in Morrowgrain output and a 70% increase in the number of herbs grown as well as large increase in the value of the herbs. Most people performing the Morrowgrain quests keep the pouch, seeds and soil in their backpack and as they run around Azeroth they pop out a new batch of herbs once every ten minutes. For an Alchemist this results in a steady supply of herbs for use in potions and for others it results in a steady supply of cash from the sale of those herbs. The hardest part is having enough space in your bags for all those herbs!

Comment1: This quest is easily soloable as lvl 34, regardless of your class. I've done it as rogue, druid, warrior and hunter. As rogue and druid it's of course easier, since you have stealth, but the way you do it is basically the same: Enter the ruins from the WEST, not on the road. Go to the Growless cave (38,68) and continue around the ruins clock-wise. There are some lvl 32-34 yetis roaming there, no big deal. Avoid or crush. When you are directly west of the ruins you will see a part of the wall with a hole in it. Enter there and very very carefully negotiate the ogres in there. They are 38-39 elites. I walk along the northern-most mountainside inside the compound. Your goal is *not* the main building, but the smaller house with a belltower. There is one ogre that'll probably aggro on you. If he does, run behind the target building and continue along the mountainside until he drops, or simply stand behind the house and let him smash you. Resurrect on that spot, behind the house. From above, the house looks like a 'T' with a short base. X marks the spot you're looking for. Move the cursor along the wall until you see it shift into the 'use'-cursor. That's the bookshelf you're looking for. Simply right-click it to get the book, right through the house wall! Negotiate your way out from the compaund the way you came. If you get aggro, make a run for it and die in a good spot (there is a space in the wall you got through at its northen-most end where you can exit and the ogres won't follow you outside) Still works with 1.12 as of Sep 20th 2006.

When you go to find Marshal Windsor, also [b]make sure the General is there on horseback[/b], and there are NO kneeling guards to be seen. Not sure whether it makes any difference, but you might also want to [b]ensure that ALL members of the group are actually on the quest.[/b] I'm guessing that if this is the case, you should be able to complete the quest without a hitch. BACKGROUND After having Ony freeze as a dragon (and her guards freeze as SW guards) on our first attempt, we all abandonned this quest and met Marshal again. Half of us finished a few days ago on our second attempt. I just watched the other half FAIL the first time, but complete it on their THIRD try. Here's what happened for these last two runs: We walked all the way through the city and arrived in the Keep, only to find that Lady Prestor was GONE, as were her guards, and the Highlord was standing around in his Battle Stance. Marshal had nobody to talk with... no dragon to conjure... and nothing changed for several minutes... so they were forced to abandon yet-again, and walk through town for their third time. But this time I stayed in the Keep (I had completed the quest, so I was not in the group), and used guild chat to let the others know when Lady Prestor re-spawned and the entire Keep had reset to normal. They made sure to wait until I gave the Say So before accepting the quest. And it worked! My theory is that this bug has something to do with others being on the quest at 'almost' the same time. In the failed attempt I described above, someone had obviously just failed this quest, leaving the Keep in a very weird 'half-spawned' state. And in retrospect, I do remember seeing the guards kneeling at the city entrance a few minutes prior to our very first failed attempt that time we waited until the General showed back up on horseback before running to get Marshal (and the quest), but maybe that wasn't long enough..? Maybe there was still another group in the Keep at that time..? Can anyone out there please test my theory and provide some results here? It'd sure be nice to have a workaround for this one!

Comment5: She's not level 500.&nbsp Two things: 1.&nbsp If she were actually 500, skinning her would require 2500 skill.&nbsp It doesn't. 2.&nbsp When something is labeled 'Boss', its effective level for hit-chance and spell-chance purposes is defined as '3 levels higher than you.'&nbsp That means your base chance for, say, a hunter, is 92% (95% for a 60 Hunter to hit a 60 mob, -3% for 3 levels difference).&nbsp When the expansion comes out, and you hit 61, it'll still be 92%.&nbsp (Yes, this means a 60 Hunter with +8% to-hit on his gear *cannot miss*.)&nbsp Spell resistance works the same way -- so you see, even if Onyxia WERE actually level 500, it wouldn't make her invincible.&nbsp It would just make her un-skinnable, because her Boss status overrides several level considerations.

Comment1: This was how I accomplished this quest for my level 19 gnome twink, without any help from friends or multiple accounts: 1. First, I moved my 70 main and twink out to the arena in STV. 2. Secondly, I logged out my main on the edge of the arena so that he was not in neutral mode and could not be attacked by members of the same faction. I logged out my twink in the center of the arena. 3. I set an alarm for every 3rd hour when the arena starts. 4. Approximately five minutes before the arena started, I logged in my main and sweeped the edges of the arena with perception to catch any horde in the area before the arena even started. 5. When the chest was dropped, I ran into the arena and immediately began opening the chest. If there were any stealthers or other 70s nearby, they would challenge me and I would kill them (most of the time, anyway). After clearing all visible opposition, I opened the chest and took all items but the trinket itself. 6. I jumped on top of the chest and force quit WoW (Alt+f4). This had the advantage of leaving my 70 in the arena for approximately 45 seconds (your main will actually be in-game during step 7), deterring any ninjas or late arrivals from taking the chest. Simply logging out will leave ninjas with an easy grab. 7. I restarted wow and logged onto my twink. Having the advantage of being a tiny gnome female, I was able to actually log inside the chest, being invisible from the outside. If you are a different race, this may be more difficult, but hopefully your 70 main will be enough of a deterrent to allow you enough time to grab the trinket. 8. I logged out my twink, moved my main up to the edge again and waited another 3 hours to do it all over again. Using this method, I was successful 12 of 14 tries, which is an incredible success ratio considering the amount of competition from both 70s and lowbies. Happy hunting!

Comment3: Have just soloed as 42 Rogue, thought I'd leave comments for those who want to do same. Overall, not too difficult, though hard to say for other classes, since by stealthing I was able to move quickly past the lower level guys. There are a few things I haven't seen anyone mention, so I'll note them: The Kurzen Elite, despite the name, are regular mobs who die easily. Dispatch at will. The Shadow Hunters are more dangerous. If you aggro one while fighting someone else, they will shoot you from afar, probably with their ridiculous poison that does 38 nature damage per second. Watch out for that. They are fragile, so engage them first when possible. The Witch Doctors are shamans and don't pose much threat. They drop fire totems that do nothing. Bleh. The Subchiefs are weird. Sometimes they roll over, other times they mysteriously took me near death. They occasionally deploy a red aura around themselves. If you see this, back away it does dps to you if you are near it quite quickly. they can't move when using it, so just back off until it goes away. Other than that, they die fairly quickly. Finally Kurzen himself: the room he is in has several subchiefs and a hunter in the corner, near him. There is little chance of fighting Kurzen 1v1, as one subchief stands near him at all times. The others can be pulled, though I don't know how other classes would handle the hunter without aggroing Kurzen. For rogues, just kill all others and go to the back corner stealthed, wait for the hunter to get sufficiently far from Kurzen, and kill him. Make sure to use your Crippling Poison in here (but you should know that by now, right?). Here's how I killed Kurzen: Stealth, Cheap Shot, Blade Flurry, Evasion, Riposte when possible. I ignored the subchief with him and concentrated on Kurzen, the Blade Flurry pretty much killed subchief without my needing to actually target him (love that talent!). Something you need to know about Kurzen that only 1 other poster has seen fit to mention: KURZEN CAN VANISH. Took me by surprise. Twice he vanished on me. The first time was ok, gave me a chance to finish off the subchief. 2nd time was annoying cause he was almost dead. Anyway, be aware of that, he'll disappear and try to run off. The quest reward is pure souveneir, as usual, but vendors for 80s. The exp reward is quite good, and kurzen himself gave me about 575 exp. Not bad. A lot of fun and a real challenge to your soloing skills, as the mobs, while kind of weak, are numerous and close together. Enjoy yourselves!

The Kurzen elite have some type of red aura that afflicts you with either a DOT or a debuff. But they are just regular NPC's not 'Elites'. There is a treasure chest about 3/4 of the way down on the right on a platform behind some crates. There are quite a few NPC's in this area and I pulled two several times. Kill everything in this area and beyond to Kurzen because the respawn rate is incredibly fast. I DoT'd the second guard and pulled aggro away from her with searing pain and SB then feared him and left her fighting Kurzen. Kurzen vanished and she then attacked and we finished off the second guard. I DOT'd the first guard, life tap, health funnel and Kurzen reappeared. and I feared him. Used mana potion. Spammed 2-3 shadowbolts and first guard was down. Succubus ran after Kurzen but was almost dead. Kurzen vanished again and I used healthstone and summoned VW. Kurzen reappeared and attacked VW, I use CoElements and hit him with searing pain x 2, and bandaged (runecloth), then wanded (fire). He again disappeared, life tap x 2-3, health funneled VW. And make sure you keep them a safe distance from the others when you agro them because they do this frostblast spell that freezes you so they can step back and attack from a short distance. Sometimes when I wasn't paying attention, the guy would step back and get too close to the next kobold and agro him as well, but atleast they don't do the frostblast thing until they're down to about 20% of their health. Comment3: This is a small straightfoward guide that doesn't use locs. --- There are 4 tablets. These are interactable objects on the ground in the troll ruins. You get a gear when you pass over them even through walls so you will be able to tell when you're close. - 1 is in Bal'lal Ruins which are just east of the basalisks on the coast and south of Zul'Kunda. The tablet is in the southwest corner of thse ruins. The easiest way here is just to clear your way to it as best you can. - 2 is in the Vile Reef, filled with elite murlocks. Scary huh! Well, it's almost due west of Bal'lal. Swim out until you see a ruin. It'll be on the north edge of the northeast corner on the outside. Swim down from the outer edge and no murlocs will even notice you. The 3rd & 4th Tablets are in the Ruins of Zul'Kunda in the northwest most corner of STV. - 3 you can reach by going to the beach on the west side of the ruins and going up a path in the back. It is in the corner behind a wall from that angle. Going in through the front, it is in the SW most corner of Zul'Kunda. There are alot of closely-packed mobs near it so unless you're a powerhouse I'd bring friends. - 4 is on the north side of Zul'Kunda. It is the hardest part to reach. I did it by clearing my way down the middle of the ruins, where it makes something like a road. You will reach a hairpin turn. Get up onto the divider and clear the mobs at the top of the second path where you're walking back towards the front of the ruins. After those are dead, you can walk along the top of the wall (northward) and get singles if you're careful. Walk to the end of this wall towards a pool and the 4th tablet is right at the corner of the wall and this pool. I hope that helps people who don't like to use locs.
Comment4: You can solo all of these if you're careful. I did it on my lvl 37 warrior. The first two are easily done. With some thought you won't have any trouble at all. The third one is the hardest to solo in my opinion. There are a lot of closely packed mobs around it (it's at the soutwest corner of the Zul'Kunda ruins, btw). Approaching from the south I was able to clear a path to the legend with some delicate pulls. Just take your time and don't be afraid to run off if you aggro too many mobs. 4 can be gotten pretty easily if you know where to sneak. As you go into the Zul'kunda ruins from the east, go up the big hill to the right of the main entrance. Follow that hill north until it gets close enough to let you jump onto (not over) the outer wall. Hop on that wall and follow it all the way north. Then follow the wall west to the upper level of the waterfall. To your left you should see the legend. Pull the mobs closest to it carefull and you'll get it no problem.
Comment5: These aren't drops, lest there be confusion.&nbsp There are big stone tablets leaning up against the walls in the ruins, that you can interact with.&nbsp You right-click on 'em, and it gives you a loot box, and voila! :)

Comment1: Now worth 8300 xp post-2.3. To be honest, I think they went a little overboard with the nerf bat on this one. It was more like a nerf jackhammer ..... -.-
Comment2: This quest is very very easy. From booty bay run up to about 31,68 when you find Mistvale Gorilla's. Clear a path through them up to 35,61 (By then you should have obtained a Gorilla Fang) then talk to Witch Doctor Unbagwa. He won't have a yellow ? above his head for some reason, but is easy to find inside his cave. Once you speak to him, you will have a gap of about 10 seconds then a Enraged Silverback Gorilla (Level 43) will attack you. After him, another gap till Konda comes, another Level 43 Gorilla. Then you will have another gap till Mokk the Savage comes up (Level 44). Kill him and loot the Heart of Mokk. Return to Booty Bay and job done. Bearing in mind i was level 47 at the time, might be a bit harder for you. I didn't even have to heal/drink/eat throughout the quest. [Edit]: If Witch Doctor Unbagwa or you die before Mokk is dead, you will have to re-collect the Gorilla fang and start over.
Comment3: This quest can be started at level 40. You will find Fin Fizracket lying on the ground on the lowest level of Booty Bay. He is under an upturned, broken in half boat. He'll request the 'Heart of Mokk', and will lead you to speak with Witch Doctor Unbagwa in Stranglethorn. If you haven't done the 'Scaring Shaky' quest yet, get it from 'Sea Wolf' McKinley in Booty Bay, because that quest requires you to collect 'Mistvale Giblets' from the Elder Mistvale Gorillas in the area. You will also need to collect 10 Gorilla Fangs for *Each* attempt you make at the Stranglethorn Fever quest. SO, its a good idea to stock up and kill a lot of these gorillas for the giblets and gorilla fangs. To find these gorillas, head north from booty bay along the trail. Not far from the entrance, on the east side of the road, you should see some of the elder gorillas running around in a field. This is your home for the quest. Slaughter gorillas until you get the required number of Fangs (and giblets if you're doing that quest). If you have a group for this quest, you only need one person to have the 10 fangs and follow the quest. The only point for everyone in the group is to get the heart of Mokk, and the only way to spawn him is to go through this veritable 'gauntlet'. Witch Doctor Unbagwa can be found in a cave to the northeast of 'Mistvale Valley', the place where you fight the elder gorillas. Once you click the 'complete quest' button in the quest entry box, Unbagwa will begin spawning gorillas that will run up the hill at you. The first wave is 3 enraged gorillas (level 42), the second wave is 4 enraged gorillas and a named gorilla (level 43). The third, and final wave, is 5 enraged gorillas and Mokk himself (level 44). Kill Mokk the Savage, loot the heart, and you're done. Well, you'll have to kill his buddies too, but the important part is killing him and looting the heart. If you die after looting, you still win =o) The reward for the quest is 5850 XP (at level 40-43), and a 30 armor, 4 stamina, 9 spirit cloak, called 'Medicine Blanket'.
Comment4: You only need to kill and loot Mokk to complete the quest, so make sure to focus your fire on him for the final wave since you can still complete the quest if you die after killing him. Between waves you have a couple seconds in which you can eat and drink. If you have a pet or ally, you can send him out to attack to give you a bit of extra time as all the gorillas will turn to attack them.

It's the area in the north-northeast of the zone. I found that the Draeni character models blend VERY well with the surrounding swamp, so what looks like an easy one-on-one kill can become two-on-one or even three-on-one. It doesn't help that the mobs are level 37-38. If you have the patience and want to play it extremely safe, you will usually find one or two crystal formations with only one nearby mob. Just loot those and wait on a respawn. Due to the fact that the Draeni blend in, and they tend to run when their health is low, you can end up with some very nasty fights, so it's not a bad idea to bring one or two friends for backup. You can accomplish much more than this quest in this area, though. If you are allied with the Gelkis centaur in Desolace, one of their later quests sends you to retrieve a gem from Ongeku, who is found in the northwestern part of the village. Near him you can find a caged human that starts an escort quest. Finally there is a rare spawn chieftan that tends to spawn near Ongeku.

Comment5: The direct route from Swamp of Sorrows to Badlands is through Alliance territory (on non PvP servers theres still guards to deal with) and 50+ zones.&nbsp The simple way for Horde is to start out in Undercity. Walk/fly to Hammerfall (pick up the Sep and TM FPs if you don't have them), from Hammerfall go south into Wetlands, south again until you find Dun Algaz, into and through Loch Modan until you get near Thelsamar, skirt around Thelsamar on the lake side and when you get to the southern tip of the Loch (lake) go south into Badlands. From the Loch Modan/Badlands border go south past the Uldaman meeting stone then stay within sight of the western mountains and follow them all the way to Kargath.&nbsp The trick to making this work is to avoid getting too close to Angor Fortress, being prepared for the stealthed cats to jump you between Angor and Lotwil's camp and avoiding the rock elementals between there and Kargath. The Kargath FP is also the keystone FP that will connect all your UC area FPs to the Stonard/Grom'gol/BB FPs.

See, there's a chance every time kill a spider that it will drop the item in question.&nbsp Let's say that chance is 5%, or 1/20. Now, it's probable that you'll get the drop within the first 20 times you do the quest -- probable, because you receive 20 chances to roll the 1/20.&nbsp And the average of all people doing the quest will average out to about 20 kills. That doesn't mean you'll get it within 20, though.&nbsp On that 21st try, regardless of the fact that you've already killed 20 spiders to no avail, the chance is still only 5%.&nbsp And on that 22nd try, it's STILL only 5%.&nbsp It's not impossible that you'd kill 100 or more spiders, still never having hit that percentage.&nbsp Call it luck if you like, but extended periods of 'improbable' missing are to be expected. All you can do is keep trying.&nbsp It's not Blizzard's fault that the computer rolled you up a long streak of &*!@ty numbers.&nbsp And keep in mind: it's that same random number generator that just might you a sweet blue weapon drop from a worthless quillboar. Comment3: Expect to spend a couple of hours doing this one, unless you bring a big and/or overpowered group with you. The mobs are level 46-50 elites, and you have to take down 80 of them total. Just work your way to the top of Jintha'alor and you will find all your mobs. You may have to backtrack in places to pick up respawns since you need so many kills. The Soul Eaters and Blood Drinkers are on the last two levels. Soul Eaters have an ability very similar to Mana Burn, so watch out casters. Blood Drinkers tend to hit hard and often, so be ready with heals. My level 55 shaman, with about 3800 armor, was getting hit for about 150 a pop. The Berserkers and Shadow Hunters are on the two levels preceding the Soul Eaters/Blood Drinkers. The Blood Drinkers are similar to Fury Warriors, while the Shadow Hunters will use ranged attacks unless you close to melee range. For some reason, the Hunters can also cast Shadow Word: Pain. The quest is long but you can stack this with several other quests out of Revantusk Village. If you just make your way to the altar at the top, you'll likely end up getting about a quarter of the 80 kills you need. The trinket reward is great for all melee classes, but casters not so much. You do get over 2g for completion though, so unless you wipe a bunch you should come out ahead. Not to mention all that xp from killing 80 elite mobs. For the record, I completed this with a 51 and 55 shaman. Easy to pull the mobs one at a time. Just watch for patrols.
Comment4: Took a long time to do this one, but it was worth it. Because all 80 of the mobs that you need to kill for this quest are Elite and between level 46 and 51, we had a group of 5 to do the Vile Priestess Hexx quest, and when we finished one person left. With only about 15 of the necessary mobs killed for Job Opp, the remaining 4 people continued on to grind them out. Here's the group makeup: 49 Rogue (me) 50 Mage 49 Shaman 47 Shaman 60 Mage (who left after the Priestess) With us four, it took about another hour and a half to do it. About 1/3 of all the mobs in Jintha'Alor are not for the quest, but you will end up having to kill them too, if you are going to be able to pull the others. Some form of crowd control is preferable, since this is basically an outdoor dungeon. Sap/Polymorph work fine. The quest rewards are nice, and make sure you have all the quests before going in. After over 2 hours in Jintha'Alor, the entire group had 5 finished Elite quests resulting in a Rare item reward and several Uncommon item rewards, plus around 40k exp. Well worth it, but make sure you have a good group.

Comment3: Seeing as how the quest description is quite vague, here's a bit of info on it. Shadra is found inside the walled city of Shadra'Alor, in the south central area of the Hinterlands. The altar that is needed to summon Shadra is on the southeast side of the lake, so don't bother climbing any of the temples. Once you summon her, the parchment is used up, and if you fail, you'll need to talk to Gadrin to get another shot at this quest. However, if you summon Shadra and don't have anyone to help you, or are waiting on people to arrive, you can keep her from despawning by keeping her engaged in combat, just slow her run speed and swim to the north side of the lake until she de-aggros, then do it again after a minute or two. As a well-geared lv.51 prot warrior with about 5100 armor (roughly 54% mitigation) Shadra hit me for between 160-400 damage with 300 or so being the average. She does quite a bit of damage, even when compared to other elites at and above her level. We had a paladin (50) and hunter (54), but in order to win, we had to let the hunter's pet take aggro for the majority of the fight, (hunter was using Mend Pet constantly) and I taunted it off right before the pet died so we could finish Shadra. Because it's difficult to solo, this will probably be one of the last quests you finish in the Hinterlands, and I highly recommend you do it; the cash, xp, and item rewards are worth the effort. Good luck! -Titaniumtoro

Comment2: ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ Dearest Yvette, I will entrust this letter to our fastest runner. I pray he can find a way through the forces surrounding us. And I pray you read these words, for they are the last you will hear of me. My only comfort in these dark days is the relief I feel, knowing that you are free of my fate. I fear my father made a grave error when he decided to remain and defend our home. The forces of the Scourge rage through Tirisfal Glades, and although we are well fortified and well stocked, after the betrayal of my brother Devlin we lack the strength and numbers to withstand their continued assault. If you receive this letter, Yvette, then know that Devlin is a traitor. Devlin despaired and sought an escape from our ill fortunes, and in doing so he made a pact with the Scourge. I do not know what price was promised him for his betrayal, but I'm sure it was laced with lies. If you see my brother, then flee from him. He is a fiend. A few nights ago he murdered two of our watchmen and let a small group of Scourge through the breach. Leading them to where many more of us slept. Their ambush was brutal. They slew a third of us before we could take them down. Now, we barely have enough men to watch our borders. It is only a matter of time before our wearying guard drops and the Scourge attack. And although I saw Devlin's face amidst the desperate men and gaunt-faced Scourge on that cursed night, he slipped away before I could catch him. He might be dead, or he might still live as an agent of the Scourge. Either way, he is a monster. Devlin warned us that if we tried to face the Scourge, then we were doomed. He told us this when they first entered Tirisfal Glades, well before they encircled our home. Perhaps he was pleading with us to leave, or perhaps he was gloating. It was always hard to understand Devlin's motives. Since he was a child, he was a mystery to us. But he was right. We are doomed. The Agamand family line will end. Although I still live, I know I will soon be dead. I am not afraid, and I do not regret remaining with my family. But my last thoughts will be of you. Live on, my beloved Yvette, and I will find peace. - Thurman ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~
