Name: A Reliquary of Purity
Instructions: Travel to Silithus and search for a Reliquary of Purity within the ruins of Southwind Village. If you are able to find it, return with it to Rabine Saturna in Nighthaven, Moonglade. Reliquary of Purity
Progress: A Reliquary of Purity is an artifact unto itself. Few were ever made, and almost all of them were thought to have been lost over time.I admit I have known about the one in Southwind for a little while now. Honestly, with the rising turmoil in Silithus, I thought to keep our secrets just that - a secret. To poke and prod would only cause suspicions of our enemies to rise.Alas, the time for complacency is at an end, especially with the situation in Eldre'Thalas.
Comment1: The Dusty Reliquary is located in the lodge structure located at the top of the hill towards the north end of of the village. It's located in the SE corner of the building, so you'll be able to see it from the entrance. The village is populated by Tortured Druids (lvl 54-55) and Tortured Sentinels (lvl 56-57). These guys are all single pulls and don't have any special attacks. In the lodge, 1 druid guards the door, 2 sentinels are inside the lodge, and a 3rd sentinel stands out on the east balcony. The balcony sentinel is close enough to aggro when you open the reliquary, so you'll probably have to kill her, too. The mobs themselves aren't hard, but each one you kill a chance to spawn 1-3 wasps on death. I got no wasps about half the time and typically 1 the rest. I think out of ~20 kills, I may have pulled 2 wasps three times and 3 wasps once. The wasps hit harder than the spirit mobs, so it's nice to have a group for this. If you solo it (as I did as a level 58 mage), here are some tips that might save you a few fights. First, there appears to be shortcut into the village from the east side. The lodge balcony overlooks a cliff, but the outer stone wall has a broken path leading down to the valley floor. I did not walk all the way down it since there were sentinels I could aggro below and I'd already fought my way in from the main west entrance. However, I walked sufficiently far down that path that I think it likely that you could use to get up to the east side of the village. As such, it might be worth your while to circle the village until you get to the east side. When at the east side of the lodge, DO NOT attack the balcony sentinel if you're not on the balcony. She won't jump over the railing, but will instead run through the building and around the outside to get to you. In so doing, she'll aggro the other three mobs on the way, which makes for a lot of potential wasps. To attack her on the balcony, circle from the east side to the north side of the balcony. You can climb up the rock outcroppings to the north and then jump south onto a stone ledge (the top of the lodge's foundation) that runs around the edge of the building. From there you'll be able to run back around to the balcony and climb over the railing to attack the balcony sentinel. You then have to kill the sentinel closest to the balcony. With those two down, you can open the reliquary without agrroing the the sentinel at the west end of the building as well as the druid in the doorway. As a mage, here's a way to avoid the fight altogether. Jump up to the stone ledge. Run around to the balcony. You'll aggro the sentinel on the balcony. Run far enough inside to aggro the sentinel on the east side of tbe building. Run back onto the balcony. When you've got the both out there, Frost Nova them in place. Run over to the Relquary and shift+right-click it to open and automatically collect the reliquary. You have enough time to pick up the item before the Nova breaks. Run back to the balcony, ignore the mobs, and jump off the east side. Head towards the stone path. If you run about midway down it and don't attack pursuers, you'll escape their chase range. They'll most of the way to you, but should turn around and head before they close to melee range. At that point, you can mount up and leave however you choose. Much simpler than fighting them head-on.

Comment1: This is a terrible attempt at a walkthru by me. I'm doing it because I couldn't find any information about the quest anywhere. So please forgive the massive inaccuracies. 1. Enter Dire Maul from the Feralas road, go up the ramp, past the patrolling dogs. Kill the ogres along the way to the T-junction. Turn left then Right thru the small doorway which takes you to a large open area columned area. 2. Head thru the large area, again killing dog patrols and ogres heading right to the Eastern Instance and enter. 3. Once inside it's easy to avoid the patrol from the right by hugging the wall the left. Follow it around a short way to where the floor drops to the area below. Take care when jumping down - about 1500 health loss and the possibility of a plant guard down there. Time it for when he's not there then fight him when he gets back. 4. The door you need to go thru is just ahead but it won't open till you talk to the big tree-man in the middle of the room. You can't talk to him until you've killed a satyr. Hugging the wall will avoid having to fight. Follow the wall anti-clockwise to a pink stone doorway with a stealthed patrolling satyr. 5. Go thru the doorway, again hugging the right wall past satyrs and plants you won't have to fight, to a large swimming pool containing a Hydrosphere - water elemental. This guy is very tough so get ready. 6. When he is dead go across the pool and you will see a pink passageway on each of the oposite walls, one leading up and the other leading down. You need the one leading up. Kill the plant in the way and go up to where you'll find a named satyr next to a pulpit and an altar. Comment5: Depends on how you've spec'd your hunter as to which pair of gloves would be better. If you have not put many points into the Beast Mastery tree, then the Beaststalker's gloves would be the better choice. However, if you have put a lot of points into BM (as I have), then the Beastmaster's gloves would probably be better for you. Frenzy rank 5 gives your pet a 100 percent chance to gain 30 percent haste after landing a critical strike. Ferocity rank 5 gives your pet plus 15 percent to its chance to land a critical strike. With a fast pet (1.0/1.3 attack speed or so), you land crits pretty darn often, which gives that haste effect pretty frequently. An additional 2 percent is nothing to scoff at. For hunters like myself who solo or duo a lot, you find that making your pet more effective greatly increases your survivability/chances of completing quests, etc. For me, the Beastmaster's gloves would be a better choice, but as I said earlier, it's very dependent on how you have spec'd yourself.

Name: The Ashenvale Hunt
Instructions: Speak with Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post, Ashenvale.
Progress: N/A
Comment1: It is divided into three seperate parts that are not connected in a series. It is up to you which part you wanna do first, second, or last. However, the usual approach is by easiest: Part 1 (the easiest): Kill Ursangous the Bear. Ursangous roams a small area slightly west of Talondeep Path among a bunch of other Ashenvale bears. He is lvl 24-25, named boss, not Elite, and is not very difficult to kill at that level. Part 2 (slightly harder): Kill Shadumbra the Stalker. Shadumbra is a cat who prowls around the small area south of Raynewood Retreat. She can be found among the Laughing Sisters nearest to the road. She is lvl 28, named, not Elite, and is extremely easy for her level. Less life/dmg than even Ursangous, just attacks faster so watch out if you are a caster. Part 3 (the hardest): Kill Sharptalon the Hippogryph. Sharptalon has the largest roaming area and he can be seen flying as close as right beside the entrance to Splintertree Post all the way to the bridge that leads to Warsong Lumber Camp. He is a hippogryph as it says, lvl 31, named, not Elite, and is relatively hard, but can be easily done at his level or even 2 levels below. Anything lower than that and you need a group. Anonymous does not mention the reward for this quest as it really is not listed as a pure quest, just three seperate smaller quests. The reward is a cape that I can't seem to find on Anonymous (mispelled probably) but it has 22 AC, +2 Stamina, and Equip: +22 Attack Power when fighting Beasts. Also, there is massive exp involved in each. I handed all three in at same time as a lvl 29 Hunter and got well over 7000 xp. (1000+ for Ursangous, 2500+ for Shadumbra, and 3500+ for Sharptalon)
Comment2: [b]Ursangous at 40,47[/b] [b]Shadumbra at 57,56[/b] [b]Sharptalon at 71,70[/b] After each kill right click on unique item and completed quest will generate.&nbsp Return to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post, Ashenvale and hand in each quest [b]Ursangous 775xp[/b] [b]Shadumbra 2200xp[/b] [b]Sharptalon 2450xp[/b] When all handed in Senai Thunderheart generates a new completed quest 'The Hunt Completed' giving [b]3050xp[/b] and [b]'Wildhunter Cloak'[/b], details are on Anonymoust. Nice quest - my Druid didn't do this until lvl 32, but breezed through eezy-peezy in about 15 mins thanks to travel form...&nbsp More like this please Blizzard!
Comment3: Alright, now that I finally put the pieces of the puzzle together, I'll share with those still clueless each step. Step 1: Talk to either [b]Bluff Runner Windstrider[/b] in [b]Thunder Bluff[/b] or [b]Warcaller Gorlach[/b] in [b]Orgrimmar[/b] to start the quest. Both NPCs wander around the cities so run all around the pathways looking for them or wait on one main pathway for them to pass by. Comment2: I've reached revered so far, ugh.... Summoning the Lesser Wind Stones requires the full set of Twilight Gear (Mantle, Cowl, Robe) and at least friendly faction with Cenarion Cirlce. The Stones are located at three of the camps, two in each camp. The loc of the 3 camps are: (39,44) (26,33) (18,84). The mobs at these 3 camps give 1 faction point until half way through friendly if I recall. The Abyssal elementals from the Lesser Wind Stones give 5 faction up until half way through honored. There are 4 types of elements that can be summoned randomly from any of the 6 Lesser wind stones. Air, Fire, Water, and Earth/Rock. They all do MAGIC based damage, so armor doesn't help here. Fire is Immune to Fire based, Water is Immune to Frost based ect... Though all can do a nature based root spell. Some can do an Earth shock that will cancel a spell, also it does damage (like Shaman spell). They are all soloable mobs with experienced players or easier with some perfessions, though suggested duo so you don't waste your twilight set which you lose on summoning. If everyone that is in combat with the mob dies, or goes out of range, the mob disappears and the Lesser Wind Stone is gone until respawn. As a frost mage, all are easy solo's except the Water based mob, which is Immune to frost, though constant arcane missiles with ice barrier and cold snap does the trick. The first turn in is only 1 Abyssal Crest which is always given by the Lesser Wind Stone kills. The second Turn in requires 3. Both of these give 50 faction points even with revered faction. This goes for all the rest of the quests with this particular NPC, all the way through even the Abyssal Scepter. First turn in requires 1, the rest require 3. Good luck, I hope this explains anything that hasn't been posted.

A complete Twilight Cultist set of armor consists of a cowl, mantle, and robes. All of these items have a chance of dropping off the various Twilight Cultists at the camps, although the mantle (shoulder pieces) seem to have a lower drop rate than the other two pieces. Comment1: 1st off you need to complete the Field Duty quests as many times as you can manage.&nbsp This will allow you to pick up multilpe Combat, Tactical, and Logistics quests.&nbsp Once you have several quests to complete go do them, and turn them in for a badge and additional quest.&nbsp The followup quests have a better chance to get a quest that you can't access from the Field Duty only. Remember that Field Duty can be soloed by a healer, you only need to keep Captain Blackanvil healed and alive throughout the battle.&nbsp If he dies you must do it all over again. If you have an Epic mount you can actually do this twice in a row.&nbsp Mount up right as the wasp drops, click to get papers signed and make a run for the Hold in the straightest path possible.&nbsp get you assignment, re-accept the Field Duty quest and head back asap.&nbsp He will either have despawned memonets before you get there, or moments after.&nbsp Use the Twilight camp and rock formations as guidlines to make a straight path.&nbsp Even with only 1 trip per you get 20 reputation every time you do this, which is one of the quickest ways to gain rep. Most of the Combat assignments require you to kill 30 of a certain bug in one of the Hives, this will usually require 2-3 people, and full group of 5 will make it faster for everyone.&nbsp Beware of Hive'Regal Slavemakers as they have a nasty poison and can Mind Control a person of the party, keep it stunned when possible. One of the quickest ways to get the Logistics badges is to keep doing Field Duty until you can get a couple of them that require items you can make, or buy in the AH.&nbsp For example Logistics Task Briefing X - is 30 of three types of bandages, very easy to do. Tactical Task Briefings require you to do some easier task such as finding a scout in one of the 3 of the Silithus Hives.&nbsp Or summoning and defeating a Templar at a Twilight camp.&nbsp Generally you will only get Task  1, 3, 7, & 9, maybe the occasional 6.&nbsp In order to get any others you must complete one and turn it in for a follwoup assignment.&nbsp With a good group the Templar assignments can go very quickly.&nbsp If you have collected a set of the 3 Twilight Cultist pieces, Robe, Mantle, Cowl, put them on and click on the Lesser Wind Stone to get a random elemental Templar.&nbsp Rinse and repeat to get the Templar tasks complete and collect Abyssal Crests to either turn in for faction, or eventually use to summon a Duke of the Council. The main thing to remember is to keep 3-8 quests for badges in your quest log so you have a variety of things you can do.&nbsp It also allows you to go with most any group to kill stuff you need.&nbsp You do not need to pick up any quests for class gear or battlegear until you actually have what is required.&nbsp The other class gear available in the form of three more quests will require Scarabs, Idols, and more from the Ahn'Qiraj 20 man instance.

Comment3: This now gives 350 reputation. Also you get 25 rep for killing one of the dukes. Process is as follows: STEP 1: Obtain 4 sets of Twilight Trappings http://classicdb.ch/?itemset=492 (head, shoulders, and chest) by killing the any of the humanoids at the twilight camps. Drop rate on each piece is 4%, so on average you will get one set every 25 kills. That's 'on average', so expect to have lucky streaks and unlucky streaks. STEP 2: Wear a set of Twilight Trappings. Click on a LESSER WIND STONE. A dialogue box opens with only one option. Before you click on it, equip you normal head, shoulder, and chest gear as you will soon be fighting. Click on the dialogue option. In a couple secconds, a flash of lighning will strike you (does no damage) and one set of Twilight Trappings will disapear from your inventory. A Templar will appear at the stone. For about 5 seconds it will just sit there and can't be attacked yet. Then it goes aggressive on the person who did the summoning. Kill the Templar, and loot the Abyssal Crest. STEP 3: Repeat step 2, and then repeat it again. You should now have 3 Abyssal Crests, and you should still have one set of Twilight Trappings. STEP 4: You will now need 1 Large Brilliant Shard, and you must be friendly with Cenarion Circle to continue. Do the 'Aurel Goldleaf' quest from Huum Wildmane if you haven't done it already. Complete that quest by talking to Aurel Goldleaf. For the follow on quest, give her the 3 Abyssal Crests and the Large Brilliant Shard, for which she will give you 1 Twilight Cultist Medallion of Station. STEP 5: Go back to one of the Twilight camps and find a WIND STONE (not a 'lesser' and not a 'greater'). Clear the area around the stone. Put on a set of Twilight Trappings and also put on the Twilight Cultist Medallion of Station. Click on the Wind Stone. You will see a dialogue box, just like in step 2. Switch back into your normal gear. Click on the dialogue option. One set of Twilight Trappings and the Twilight Cultist Medallion of Station will disapear from your inventory, and one of the 4 DUKEs will be summoned. As before, there is a 5 second pause before the Duke will go agro. Kill the duke and loot the Abyssal Signet. Note, if you fail to kill the Duke, or it evades for any reason, it will despawn and you have to start all over from step 1. You do not get any of the materials refunded to you. STEP 6: Go back to Bor Wildmane and turn in the Abyssal Signet for your reward. REPEATING FOR MORE TURN INS: You can turn in more Abyssal Signets to get more rewards, but each turn in after the first requires 3 Abyssal Signets. You have to repeat steps 1 - 5 for each Abyssal Signet, so that's 3 full repetitions to get another Sack of Spoils. Is it worth it? My first time doing this was solo as a 70 BM hunter. The randomly summoned duke was the Duke of Shards, who I downed with no trouble. The duke dropped Abyssal Plate Legplates of Restoration http://classicdb.ch/?item=20671 I turned in the quest, opened my Sack of Spoils and got Lord Alexander's Battle Axe http://classicdb.ch/?item=13003 From wowhead's loot tables: Getting a BoE blue drop from a duke is about a 25% chance. Getting a BoE blue drop from the Sack of Spoils is also about a 25% chance. It can be a fairly time consuming process to go through and the odds of getting nothing are fairly high, so weigh the cost before you set out on this venture.

Progress: It's in our best interest to keep our most loyal allies well geared, <name>.
Comment1: 1st off you need to complete the Field Duty quests as many times as you can manage.&nbsp This will allow you to pick up multilpe Combat, Tactical, and Logistics quests.&nbsp Once you have several quests to complete go do them, and turn them in for a badge and additional quest.&nbsp The followup quests have a better chance to get a quest that you can't access from the Field Duty only. Remember that Field Duty can be soloed by a healer, you only need to keep Captain Blackanvil healed and alive throughout the battle.&nbsp If he dies you must do it all over again. If you have an Epic mount you can actually do this twice in a row.&nbsp Mount up right as the wasp drops, click to get papers signed and make a run for the Hold in the straightest path possible.&nbsp get you assignment, re-accept the Field Duty quest and head back asap.&nbsp He will either have despawned memonets before you get there, or moments after.&nbsp Use the Twilight camp and rock formations as guidlines to make a straight path.&nbsp Even with only 1 trip per you get 20 reputation every time you do this, which is one of the quickest ways to gain rep. Most of the Combat assignments require you to kill 30 of a certain bug in one of the Hives, this will usually require 2-3 people, and full group of 5 will make it faster for everyone.&nbsp Beware of Hive'Regal Slavemakers as they have a nasty poison and can Mind Control a person of the party, keep it stunned when possible. One of the quickest ways to get the Logistics badges is to keep doing Field Duty until you can get a couple of them that require items you can make, or buy in the AH.&nbsp For example Logistics Task Briefing X - is 30 of three types of bandages, very easy to do. Tactical Task Briefings require you to do some easier task such as finding a scout in one of the 3 of the Silithus Hives.&nbsp Or summoning and defeating a Templar at a Twilight camp.&nbsp Generally you will only get Task  1, 3, 7, & 9, maybe the occasional 6.&nbsp In order to get any others you must complete one and turn it in for a follwoup assignment.&nbsp With a good group the Templar assignments can go very quickly.&nbsp If you have collected a set of the 3 Twilight Cultist pieces, Robe, Mantle, Cowl, put them on and click on the Lesser Wind Stone to get a random elemental Templar.&nbsp Rinse and repeat to get the Templar tasks complete and collect Abyssal Crests to either turn in for faction, or eventually use to summon a Duke of the Council. The main thing to remember is to keep 3-8 quests for badges in your quest log so you have a variety of things you can do.&nbsp It also allows you to go with most any group to kill stuff you need.&nbsp You do not need to pick up any quests for class gear or battlegear until you actually have what is required.&nbsp The other class gear available in the form of three more quests will require Scarabs, Idols, and more from the Ahn'Qiraj 20 man instance.

Comment2: After handing in this quest, grab some popcorn, sit back and be prepared to learn about the lore behind Silithus, Ahn'Qiraj, the Titans and the Old Gods, and the reason behind the night elf Arch Druid's stinking attitude. Or you could just read the story here: [quote][url=http://classicdb.ch/?npc=15183]Geologist Larksbane[/url] says: I will do my best to translate and describe what I see. It is history.. A history of [url=http://classicdb.ch/?zone=1377]Silithus[/url]... of [url=http://classicdb.ch/?zone=3428]Ahn'Qiraj[/url]... of Titans and Old Gods... I read from the prophecy of [url=http://classicdb.ch/?npc=15727]C'Thun[/url] as written by the Qiraji [url=http://classicdb.ch/?npc=15263]Prophet Skeram[/url]. A prophecy that portends a cataclysm... In the time before time, when the world was still in its infancy, a battle between a Titan and a being of unimaginable evil and power raged on this very soil. The prophecy is unclear about whether or not the Titan was vanquished in this battle but it illustrates that a Titan fell. An Old God had also fallen - or so it was thought. For millennia this being lay dormant beneath the world - biding its time. From its prison it waited for the exact moment at which to strike back at those that would see it harmed. The land of eternal starlight, Kalimdor, was a nurturing mother to all of its creatures. The magic of the Well of Eternity permeated the land and empowered the multitude of flora and fauna that would make the world their home. From this magical ether were born the silithid. It was throught the silithid that the brooding Old God would reach and attempt to sunder the world that it once held in its unmerciful grasp. The Old God would create avatars from the silithid in its own image. These avatars were to be known as Qiraji. Sentient and with purpose, the Qiraji would name their creator: C'Thun was born... For many thousands of years the Qiraji worked feverishly to build a force capable of laying waste to the world that would betray their god. The great fortress city of Ahn'Qiraj was created to house their growing armies and prepare for the coming of C'Thun. This can't be right. An Old God could never be allowed to enter this world. The results would be... Oh dear! [i]Geologist Larksbane regains her composure.[/i] Gelogist Larksbane says: There is more. The moment that C'Thun had so patiently waited for had finally arrived. His children had spent thousands of years building an army capable of exacting revenge upon the whole of Kalimdor and now the prize was within their grasp. The Titans had long since vacated this world. Only the night elves that once inhabited this area were here to defend. Oh my! The next passage is fascinating! A mighty Qiraji known as [url=http://classicdb.ch/?npc=15341]General Rajaxx[/url] would command the initial incursion into Silithus. Only one would stand in his way: A night elf known as [url=http://classicdb.ch/?npc=3516]Staghelm[/url]. They refer to him as Khar'sis or 'hand of the earth' in the native Qiraji tongue. Staghelm and his armies were clearly overwhelmed as the endless flow of Rajaxx's troops poured into Silithus. It would seem as if Staghelm, however, was more than just a nuisance to the Qiraji. Under Staghelm, the whole of the night elf armies had come together to defend Kalimdor, greatly slowing the Qiraji forces. Unfortunately, the night elf defense was untenable and Rajaxx knew that they could not hold out much longer. Their tenacity, however, was causing great frustration to Rajaxx and causing even more frustration to his king. Wait, kings? Incredible... [url=http://classicdb.ch/?npc=15275]Vek'nilash[/url] and [url=http://classicdb.ch/?npc=15276]Vek'lor[/url], known as the Twin Emperors of Ahn'Qiraj, watched the war from the sanctuary of their temple. The clever brothers devised a plan to demoralize and divide Staghelm's forces. Valstann Staghelm served as the right hand of Fandral. A proud and noble warrior, his dedication and adoration for his father unyielding... and the Twin Emperors sensed this as weakness. A weakness that could be exploited. The Qiraji forces were commanded to fall back and hide the bulk of their numbers beneath the sands of the desert. A small attack was ordered upon Southwind Village while the front lines of Staghelm's army were kept occupied. Valstann, eager to please his father, convinced Fandral to allow him to take a small battalion to the defense of Southwind. Surely with the tide of battle turning their way, no harm could come to his beloved child. The trap was missed. Valstann was capture by the hiding Qiraji and Southwind Village obliterated. Rajaxx himself would take the captive Valstann to the front lines of the battle where - in front of Staghelm and the night elf forces - he would brutally execute the young night elf. The war continued but the will of the great leader was sapped. The whole of Silithus was soon engulfed by the silithid and their Qiraji hosts. Poor man, this explains much. The night elf army was pushed back through [url=http://classicdb.ch/?zone=490]Un'Goro[/url], the the borders of the [url=http://classicdb.ch/?zone=440]Tanaris[/url] desert. Something in Un'Goro prevented the Qiraji from being able to take the land. I do not quite understand this word but I believe it to mean 'God Lands.' It is stated that they could not 'take the God Lands.' Fascinating, this coincides with theories of Un'Goro being the home of the Titans when they inhabited Kalimdor. Perhaps Aman'thul himself watched over 'The God Lands.' Hrm, curious... This ends abruptly. In Tanaris the Qiraji document facing a bronze dragon. There is much missing from this... More information must be found! Surely they are planning to invade Kalimdor once more! [i][url=http://classicdb.ch/?npc=15180]Baristolth of the Shifting Sands[/url] shifts uncomfortably.[/i] Baristolth of the Shifting Sands says: When the time is right, my lady. All will be clear when the time is right. The master stirs even now. Look to the skies for the Brood of Nozdormu have returned.[/quote]

Progress: This ain't no smash and grab job, <name>. You're gonna need to bring friends.
Comment1: This is a single-part quest that was introduced in the 1.10 patch the NPC is in Cenarion Hold, inside the inn, to the left of the innkeeper. As said in the quest text, you need to gather two venom sacs: one from Kurinnaxx, first boss in AQ20, and one from Venoxis, one of the easiest bosses in ZG. Kurinnaxx is not hard, but if you don't know what to expect, he will give you a bit of trouble. Everybody in the raid needs to keep moving around to avoid sand traps if the damage they inflict isn't much, and can be resisted (and absorbed with nature protection potions), the main issue is the silence effect, definitely a problem for casters (can't cast anything), and even warriors (you can't taunt or shout when silenced). Tanks will get tagged by him, the debuff increases damage taken and it stacks it's crucial that when one tank has 5 or 6 debuffs, another tank picks him up until the former tank has lost the debuffs (30 seconds or so). So, warriors taunt and keep Kurinnaxx moving around to avoid sandtraps, and share the job as debuffs rain on them, melee DPS keeps moving along and burn him down. Avoid standing -behind- him at all cost, his tail does a very nasty cleave, hit his sides instead don't stand infront of him if you're not a warrior, his frontal attack is even worse. Kurinnaxx isn't hard, and you don't need epic gear to win this, it's just basic group coordination and communication. Venoxis is the easiest boss in ZG, found on the south side of the instance past the nook where the bat boss/Jek'lik is (ZG is all nooks, there's no order in which you kill the bosses). 4 serpent adds, one priest that turns into a big snake. Have mages sheep and/or druids sleep 3 of the adds, the main tank picks up Venoxis and drags him to a corner secondary tank picks up the non-sheeped/sleeped snake, everybody kills it, repeat with the 3 other adds. When all 4 adds are dead (they're easy), everybody moves on to the main tank and help him burn down Venoxis the only real hassle with Venoxis is the poison clouds he spreads around (acid green clouds, hard to miss them), they hurt a lot if you stand in them. The main tank will need to move Venoxis out of those clouds, melee follows out and keep burning the big snake down. And that's pretty much it, hence why Venoxis is called the easiest boss in ZG (if you want a real fight, head over to Jin'do lol).

Venoxis is the easiest boss in ZG, found on the south side of the instance past the nook where the bat boss/Jek'lik is (ZG is all nooks, there's no order in which you kill the bosses). 4 serpent adds, one priest that turns into a big snake. Have mages sheep and/or druids sleep 3 of the adds, the main tank picks up Venoxis and drags him to a corner secondary tank picks up the non-sheeped/sleeped snake, everybody kills it, repeat with the 3 other adds. When all 4 adds are dead (they're easy), everybody moves on to the main tank and help him burn down Venoxis the only real hassle with Venoxis is the poison clouds he spreads around (acid green clouds, hard to miss them), they hurt a lot if you stand in them. The main tank will need to move Venoxis out of those clouds, melee follows out and keep burning the big snake down. And that's pretty much it, hence why Venoxis is called the easiest boss in ZG (if you want a real fight, head over to Jin'do lol).

Comment1: 1st off you need to complete the Field Duty quests as many times as you can manage.&nbsp This will allow you to pick up multilpe Combat, Tactical, and Logistics quests.&nbsp Once you have several quests to complete go do them, and turn them in for a badge and additional quest.&nbsp The followup quests have a better chance to get a quest that you can't access from the Field Duty only. Remember that Field Duty can be soloed by a healer, you only need to keep Captain Blackanvil healed and alive throughout the battle.&nbsp If he dies you must do it all over again. If you have an Epic mount you can actually do this twice in a row.&nbsp Mount up right as the wasp drops, click to get papers signed and make a run for the Hold in the straightest path possible.&nbsp get you assignment, re-accept the Field Duty quest and head back asap.&nbsp He will either have despawned memonets before you get there, or moments after.&nbsp Use the Twilight camp and rock formations as guidlines to make a straight path.&nbsp Even with only 1 trip per you get 20 reputation every time you do this, which is one of the quickest ways to gain rep. Most of the Combat assignments require you to kill 30 of a certain bug in one of the Hives, this will usually require 2-3 people, and full group of 5 will make it faster for everyone.&nbsp Beware of Hive'Regal Slavemakers as they have a nasty poison and can Mind Control a person of the party, keep it stunned when possible. One of the quickest ways to get the Logistics badges is to keep doing Field Duty until you can get a couple of them that require items you can make, or buy in the AH.&nbsp For example Logistics Task Briefing X - is 30 of three types of bandages, very easy to do. Tactical Task Briefings require you to do some easier task such as finding a scout in one of the 3 of the Silithus Hives.&nbsp Or summoning and defeating a Templar at a Twilight camp.&nbsp Generally you will only get Task  1, 3, 7, & 9, maybe the occasional 6.&nbsp In order to get any others you must complete one and turn it in for a follwoup assignment.&nbsp With a good group the Templar assignments can go very quickly.&nbsp If you have collected a set of the 3 Twilight Cultist pieces, Robe, Mantle, Cowl, put them on and click on the Lesser Wind Stone to get a random elemental Templar.&nbsp Rinse and repeat to get the Templar tasks complete and collect Abyssal Crests to either turn in for faction, or eventually use to summon a Duke of the Council. The main thing to remember is to keep 3-8 quests for badges in your quest log so you have a variety of things you can do.&nbsp It also allows you to go with most any group to kill stuff you need.&nbsp You do not need to pick up any quests for class gear or battlegear until you actually have what is required.&nbsp The other class gear available in the form of three more quests will require Scarabs, Idols, and more from the Ahn'Qiraj 20 man instance.

Comment1: Both quests are easy enough if you know when and where to pull.&nbsp I did both of them by myself.&nbsp If you are a druid or rogue, the best thing to do is prowl around the areas so you can get a good idea of where people are, where the plans and letters are, and where to run. Covert Ops Alpha - The wagon is in front of the mill on a small hill.&nbsp It sits by itself and has some firework looking things on top.&nbsp For those with Cosmos or map coordinates, the mill is at 66,50.&nbsp There are two loggers close to it, so take them out.&nbsp Then attach the explosives, blow it up, and run along the bottom of the hill towards the mill.&nbsp Not all of the Venture guys will leave, but that's okay.&nbsp The plans are on the west/left side of the mill, on a tree stump.&nbsp It looks like a piece of rolled-up parchment.&nbsp I shifted to cat from as soon as it blew, prowled over to the parchment, shifted up, grabbed it, and ran out with only 1 aggroed Deforester to take care of behind the mill. Covert Ops Beta - This is a little more difficult than Alpha.&nbsp The wagon for this one is on a small hill in front of the mine.&nbsp The mine is located at about 74,58 or so.&nbsp There are no guards on this wagon, just an operator, and he's far enough away where he won't aggro.&nbsp Slightly behind the wagon there is a small hill.&nbsp You can blow the wagon if you stand on that hill and keep the wagon to your right. The letters for this one are on the right/east side of the mine entrance, on a tree stump.&nbsp They look like a stack of books. Here's the trick for Beta...the kobolds don't run when you blow the wagon.&nbsp So, you need to kill some of them before setting the explosives.&nbsp On the west side of the mine, there is another small hill with three kobolds wandering.&nbsp Take them out.&nbsp On the east side of the mine, along the ridge, there are two other kobolds.&nbsp Take them out too.&nbsp There is another kobold closer to the letters, but if you attack him you'll draw the attention of everyone else, so leave him alone. Run over to the wagon (don't let anyone see you!) and set the explosives.&nbsp Get over to the hill and set them off, then take off running.&nbsp Head over the hill where you killed the first kobolds, then turn to the mine and get the plans.&nbsp Then run AWAY from the mine (I went to the east, along the cliffs).&nbsp The kobold you didn't kill will most likely aggro, but if you stop to kill him the rest of the Venture guys will be back and aggro.&nbsp Just make sure your health is full and run along the cliffs.&nbsp He stops giving chase soon. Good luck, and I hope this helps!
Comment2: When you accept this quest a black bag will be placed in your inventory. This bag contains the instructions, as well as explosives and detonators for both Covert Ops A and Covert Ops B quests. To get these out of your bag you click on them, and accept the question asking if you want to bind them to you. This takes them from the bag and places them in your regular inventory to be used. The wagon is on a hill south of the mill. You place the explosives on the wagon by getting close to it, then right-clicking on them. Progress: How'd it go, <name>?
Comment1: Both quests are easy enough if you know when and where to pull.&nbsp I did both of them by myself.&nbsp If you are a druid or rogue, the best thing to do is prowl around the areas so you can get a good idea of where people are, where the plans and letters are, and where to run. Covert Ops Alpha - The wagon is in front of the mill on a small hill.&nbsp It sits by itself and has some firework looking things on top.&nbsp For those with Cosmos or map coordinates, the mill is at 66,50.&nbsp There are two loggers close to it, so take them out.&nbsp Then attach the explosives, blow it up, and run along the bottom of the hill towards the mill.&nbsp Not all of the Venture guys will leave, but that's okay.&nbsp The plans are on the west/left side of the mill, on a tree stump.&nbsp It looks like a piece of rolled-up parchment.&nbsp I shifted to cat from as soon as it blew, prowled over to the parchment, shifted up, grabbed it, and ran out with only 1 aggroed Deforester to take care of behind the mill. Covert Ops Beta - This is a little more difficult than Alpha.&nbsp The wagon for this one is on a small hill in front of the mine.&nbsp The mine is located at about 74,58 or so.&nbsp There are no guards on this wagon, just an operator, and he's far enough away where he won't aggro.&nbsp Slightly behind the wagon there is a small hill.&nbsp You can blow the wagon if you stand on that hill and keep the wagon to your right. The letters for this one are on the right/east side of the mine entrance, on a tree stump.&nbsp They look like a stack of books. Here's the trick for Beta...the kobolds don't run when you blow the wagon.&nbsp So, you need to kill some of them before setting the explosives.&nbsp On the west side of the mine, there is another small hill with three kobolds wandering.&nbsp Take them out.&nbsp On the east side of the mine, along the ridge, there are two other kobolds.&nbsp Take them out too.&nbsp There is another kobold closer to the letters, but if you attack him you'll draw the attention of everyone else, so leave him alone. Run over to the wagon (don't let anyone see you!) and set the explosives.&nbsp Get over to the hill and set them off, then take off running.&nbsp Head over the hill where you killed the first kobolds, then turn to the mine and get the plans.&nbsp Then run AWAY from the mine (I went to the east, along the cliffs).&nbsp The kobold you didn't kill will most likely aggro, but if you stop to kill him the rest of the Venture guys will be back and aggro.&nbsp Just make sure your health is full and run along the cliffs.&nbsp He stops giving chase soon. Good luck, and I hope this helps!

Instructions: Additional requirements to obtain this quest: Your reputation with Brood of Nozdormu must be at least Neutral Narain Soothfancy in Tanaris wants you to bring him 20 Arcanite Bars, 10 Elementium Ore, 10 Azerothian Diamonds, and 10 Blue Sapphires. Arcanite Bar (20) Elementium Ore (10) Azerothian Diamond (10) Blue Sapphire (10)
Progress: Arcanite buoys don't just make themselves, <name>. And NO, you cannot borrow some money.
Comment1: This quest is part of the AQ Gates openning questline. You have to gather these materials so the gnome can make you an arcanite buoy that you can use to summon the shark boss in Azhara. The boss is easily killed by a 25man and it drops the blue scepter shard.
Comment2: Once the gates of AQ have been opened on your server, the farthest anyone else can conceivably go is this: Red Line - Vaelstraez Complete the entire Red Line and get the Shadow Resist reward (5 hour clear of BWL is all it requires and that should be easy for the guilds with it on farm status). Green Line - Eranikus LAWL - Don't even bother starting this quest. The only potential rewards are at the very end (both are Nature Resistance armor) and you have two major cockblocks: Getting the Fragment of the Nightmare's Corruption and disabling Eranikus himself. THREE fragments drop from 61+ Elite Green Dragonkin near the portals. These require a 5 man party, have very very low drop rates, and on top of it all, only ONE may loot the fragment when it does eventually drop. It'll take a long ass time to get these drops and it requires a balanced party. The last fragment drops off of a Twilight Corruptor, which is a 40 man raid boss. The second cockblock is to 'kill' Eranikus in Moonglade. This fight requires more than a 40 man raid (it required two full raids of BWL equipped people from our server ... two end-game guilds basically) to defeat Eranikus. Blue Line - Azuregos One COULD conceivably complete the Draconic for Dummies, as only one of them requires an out-of-the-way raid to Alcaz Island for Dr. Weavil (who is harder than he looks by the way ... he's a gnome who uses a wrench for a weapon ... but he'll wtfpwn you if you aren't careful). The reward for that is a cloth helm with 17 stam, 31 int, 9 mp5, and 10% resistance to silence. One could conceivably raid the 500-lb Lord Chicken on the Isle of Dread. The rewards for this raid are very good: 20 Chimerlok Tenderloins (+25 stam for 15 minute food) and the recipe for the Tenderloins. This might be worth it for a guild who needs the food for MT's in Naxx or C'thun (etc.). And now, you reach yet another cockblock. I can't imagine a guild bank supplying ONE member with 10 elementium ore to allow him to go further on the quest. The elementium would much better be used for Thunderfuries or for the Blessed Qiraji Armaments. Also, the other mats are nothing to laugh at either, especially 20 arcanite bars. Good luck with your quest.

Comment2: If you're a first-time player, this quest will certainly cause a lot of pain. I came back to do it as a 12 druid (my first character) and it was still mildly challenging even then. The greatest challenge is the sheer number of Grells inhabiting the place � getting anywhere to explore the cave is a challenge for anyone under level 8 or so. In this cave, there are two 'major' spawns � Melenas and Threggil. Melenas the level 8 satyr is up on one of the ledges � yes, there are actually two ledges, nearly identical to each other. Go figure. It's not true that he keeps spawning on different places, it's just that the whole cave is really, really confusing � until you memorize it. Just go in, and after the 90 degree turn to the left, go right, and keep to the right wall. The tunnel will start turning left, and you will end up in a chamber...If I do remember correctly (it's been such a long time) you want to turn right, and then juke left at the first turn � don't keep on going, it'll just put you on the wrong ledge. Melenas is like the purloined letter � in plain sight. He's just way up there in the haze with his accomplice. First, kill the two blue Grells, and then take out Melenas' bo9dyguard, and finally Melenas. Melenas transforms into a Nightsaber-like beast after you hit it. You can jump off the ledge into the Grell welcoming party down below in the first (or was it second?) chamber. While you're in there...Threggil is a level 6 rare-spawn that runs around the first chamber � the one that you go into if you keep walking forward after the first turn. Threggil has a nearly-guaranteed drop, the Keen Machete (2.5 DPS main hand sword, if you are so inclined to find out). Be aware that you will most likely get one or two adds, since all the Grells are placed very regularly throughout the chamber. I tried soloing this as a level 5 (level 5 for the most part, took out Melenas after I hit 6) rogue, and although the Grell are annoyingly perceptive, I was able to kill Melenas after two ungraceful deaths � one after killing the two blue-colored Grells and one after killing Melenas' accomplice Grell. I don't know if it's been confirmed or not, but I didn't seem to be able to even hurt the satyr unless I took out his Grell-servant. *sigh* Wasted two pots and three bandages for some cruddy XP and rewards...Say...If I can do this at level 6 (No, half the time I wasn't in stealth and I was usually handling two level 7s at once) it really shouldn't be a problem for most of you � and I am definitely not a very good WoW player.

Comment2: This is the last in a line of quests that had you killing centaur and centaur leaders the Barrens over. This final quest spawns a battle between Horde forces and Centaur forces. The Horde forces are typically overrun by the Centaur, unless you help. In order to get Warlord Krom'zar to spawn, a number of centaur must be defeated. Krom'zar is no pushover though, he's a level 20 elite and comes with a pair of bodyguards, and there's also the rest of the centaur to worry about. Best to do this with others, and the Horde forces can also be counted on to help.
Comment3: These are the tricks: Don't let the defenders fall.&nbsp If you see the NPCs fighting the centaurs, support them don't let them die.&nbsp I think (not positive) that if too many defenders die, you lose the battle and Krom'Zar doesn't come. Otherwise, stay at the fringes of the battle so you don't get overwhelmed. When Krom'Zar shows up, mark him (a Hunter is good for this).&nbsp He's in the middle of a pool of centaurs.&nbsp Ignore them concentrate all your ranged firepower just on him. If he's killed, it doesn't matter if you die -- though don't Release Spirit until _after_ he dies! After the battle, he won't leave a corpse.&nbsp Instead, look for a banner.&nbsp It's tall but thin, and easy to miss.&nbsp Right-click on the banner to get a piece of it.

Comment2: The control panel is at coordinates: 52x,11y in The Barrens. -Kbizzle
Comment3: As the single most frustrating (next to the voidwalker quest) in the game.&nbsp Since pretty much every Horde ends up in the Barrens, I have now done this quest as six different classes and it never gets less frustrating, though I have the method down pat and no longer pull my hair out after forgetting a step. The location has been confirmed several times.&nbsp Go north out of XR and past the road to Durotar.&nbsp Before it curves left heading for Ashenvale, head northeast and you'll see a house up on a hill and a smaller structure with three tanks to the west of it (an identical version is in Ratchet in the shop where you get the Freebooters quest.&nbsp Do the following in this exact order. Approach from the south of the 3 tank thingy.&nbsp The control console should be in front of you.&nbsp Kill the five mobs nearest the console and DON'T LOOT ANYTHING.&nbsp The respawn rate is bad enough without speeding it up by looting.&nbsp Loot only what is left after you're ready to get the key.&nbsp Right-click on the console and you'll get a Quest 2 to turn off the 3 valves.&nbsp The valves are on the other three sides of the three tank thingy.&nbsp they are near the ground and look like little wheels with steam coming out from them.&nbsp You'll have to kill the 3-5 mobs around each one and there will most likely be a couple of them right next to each other that spawn after you kill all the mobs in step one.&nbsp I prefer going counterclockwise to turn off the east, north and west valves, but you can go the opposite way if it turns you on.&nbsp Once all the valves are off you get to head back to the control console again. By the time you turn off all three valves all the mobs by the console will have respawned.&nbsp Deal with it.&nbsp Also, you might want to keep a slowing spell or an instant cast kill spell handy for when the mobs are about 1/4 life, because that's when they bolt and get help.&nbsp I kept pulling 10 mobs in sequence as a Warrior because I kept forgetting to get in Battle stance to use Hamstring, and kept getting adds this way.&nbsp Keep an eye on that health bar, and as it approaches 25%, use your most powerful cast and then an insta-kill spell to fry that sucker.&nbsp You'll be glad you did. Back to our story: step three is to go back to the control console, killing the same five mobs you already killed, only to find out upon right-clicking the console that you need the key. What can I say? Blizzard is full of sadistic bastards that were probably laughing their asses off while programming this.&nbsp So accept part three of the quest: 'I am going to kill the whole QA department by drowning them in my accumulated bile'. The key is held by a level 16 goblin in the little house on top of the hill to the east.&nbsp You will have to take care of the 5-6 mobs on the hill and in front of the house first.&nbsp You can either charge in the house as a warrior or blast him from outside as a mage, but just kill him and get the key. The key DOES NOT SHOW UP IN YOUR INVENTORY, so make sure you've got it or get a mod that tells you so.&nbsp Run back to the control console and kill the same five mobs a third time to access it.&nbsp Then right-click on the console to remove the samophlange.&nbsp You'll need to click twice to open the panel with the key and then remove the samophlange.&nbsp Then loot anything still sparkling and get the hell out of there.&nbsp You may want to yell: 'I FINISHED YOUR STUPID QUEST YOU SONS OF A MOTHERLESS OGRE'.&nbsp It made me feel better.&nbsp Your mileage may vary.

Comment1: This quest is a bit complex to complete, and even with the information here, it took me a while to figure out. First, go to the Smokestack at about 53,10.&nbsp This is NOT the larger apparatus which is a ways farther to the east, in the Sludge Fen.&nbsp The Smokestack is a smaller installation, though it is also surrounded by a lot of guards, workers, peons, etc.&nbsp It is just east of the road that leads north from Crossroads.&nbsp It is a fair distance up the road, and sits up against a hill, on the south side of the hill. You will need to kill about 20 guards on this one.&nbsp They will probably regenerate before you are done.&nbsp If there are any other people nearby, doing the same quest, you really should consider grouping with them.&nbsp The grouping won't matter so much on the first tasks, but, unless you group, only ONE person will be able to get the key at the end (fron Tinkerer Sniggles) and you will need to wait for him (and the guards) to regenerate. Okay, here is the order of tasks: 1.&nbsp Kill enough guards to get to the control panel.&nbsp It is is in the area in front of the smokestack (next to the smokestack, on the south side), under the canopy. 2.&nbsp Go the the control panel, to the left side, under the canopy.&nbsp Stand next to it and right click.&nbsp After it opens, click, 'Complete Task.' 3.&nbsp Go turn off the 3 valves.&nbsp One is on the protrusions from the east side of the smokestack.&nbsp One is on the pipe that comes out of the ground behind, on the north side of the smokestack.&nbsp One is on the west side of the smokestack, near the base.&nbsp The order in which you do this is not important, except that it can only be completed AFTER you have opened the control panel the first time (above). 4.&nbsp Go back to the control panel again, and open it again.&nbsp This is the second time.&nbsp 'Complete' that task. 5.&nbsp Now, you need to go up the small hill to the east and kill Tinkerer Sniggles.&nbsp If you are with a group, you MUST get grouped by this point, or only one of you will get the key.&nbsp Tinkerer Sniggles is in the little house, up the hill.&nbsp When he dies, you should find a key in his possestions.&nbsp Take it. 6.&nbsp Final task.&nbsp Go back down the hill and open the Control Panel one more time (the 3rd time).&nbsp Complete that.&nbsp Now take the Samophlange device to Sputtervalve in Ratchet. I hope this helps make the whole thing clear.

Comment1: Bleh, it looks like all of the old comments are gone. Here's where the Quest NPCs are located (sorry don't have Coords to give): From the Quest Starter, run north until the roads ends in a 'T-Intersection.'&nbsp It will go West to Astranaar or East to Azshara.&nbsp Don't make the mistake of taking the Y-Intersection that you first come to after leaving the Quest Starter. First One: From the T-Intersection, run East about 200 yards.&nbsp The first NPC at the Splintertree OUTPOST - pretty much right on the road (not the Splintertree Post, which is just slightly more East and a bit North (you can see it from the road).&nbsp This NPC will wander up and down the tower there. Second One: From Splintertree Outpost, run East to Azshara.&nbsp This next NPC wanders the road between the Warsong Lumber Camp and Shadowsong Shrine in Azshara.&nbsp The boundry between Ashenvale and Azshara is the river.&nbsp The NPC will wander across the river 200-300 yards into Azshara.&nbsp (There is an Alliance Flight Path here and much higher level mobs so be careful and don't stray from the road).&nbsp Run back and forth from the bridge to the Warsong Lumber camp and you should find this NPC.&nbsp She rides a wolf. Third One: Run West, then run west some more, then keep running until you hit the beach.&nbsp Seriously. It's a long run - you might want to make yourself a snack for this one.&nbsp Go back past the Splintertree Outpost, past the T-Intersection mentioned above and continue West to Astranaar.&nbsp This is an alliance town, so skirt the town to either side (south seems the most direct).&nbsp Soon after you leave the town, you will descend some hills and see a tower on your right.&nbsp When the ground levels off head west off the road (you may find the faint path the heads to the beach, it doesn't matter).&nbsp This will take you between a gap in the mountain range that empties out onto the beach.&nbsp Head south along the beach to the Zoram'strand Outpost.&nbsp There is a Horde flight path here.&nbsp Get the route and fly back to Crossroads.&nbsp Or, get a group and do Blackfathom Depths.&nbsp There are a few quests here where you can grind out some XP, but no Inn at which to log out. Hope this helps.

Comment2: Ratchet is a neutral town on the east coast of The Barrens. I know of two reasonable means of getting there: 1. Overland -- get to Auberdine in Darkshore. Take this, and you find a gate to The Barrens, which is, unfortunately, guarded by horde NPCs. Luckily for us, if you exit the road and go a little further east (basically just around the hill that marks the east side of the Horde gate) you will find a broken gate you can safely pass through. Once into The Barrens, start making your way east until you hit the coast, then follow the coast down into Ratchet. Nothing will be high enough level to worry you. 2. By sea -- if you have already managed to get to Booty Bay in Stranglethorn Vale, there is a boat from there to Ratchet. Note: If you take the overland route to Ratchet and have NOT already been to Booty Bay, make sure to catch the boat there from Ratchet. Booty Bay is another neutral city, has a hippogryph connection which reaches Stormwind, Darkshire and Westfall, and also has a bank. It's well worth taking the boat ride over now to get the flight connection for later use.

Comment1: Getting to Badlands is a stinker as Horde, because you have to cross Alliance territories. The way to get there that I have found so far is to go through: 1. Silverpine Forest 2. Hillsbrad Foothills 3. Arathi Highlands (Watch out for Stormwind Guards on the road - there are both Undercity and Stormwind guards as random spawns on the roads in this zone.) 4. Wetlands (There are Alliance NPC's spotted along the roads in this zone, and an Alliance city, Menethil, in the SW corner of the zone. This is a 20-25ish level Alliance zone.) 5. Loch Modan (This is the stinker, since Loch is totally Alliance controlled, and the only way in is through tunnels. If you have a map of Wetlands you will see a fort called Dun Algaz in the SE corner of the zone. This is the beginning of a series of 3 tunnels that go to Loch M from Wetlands. The first tunnel has level 18-ish dwarf mobs guarding it - these you can whack. The next tunnel has a wandering level 30 dwarven guard in it and a second at the far end of the tunnel. These guys give no experience, as they are Alliance guard mobs, and they have elite-range HP. I could kill one as a level 34 shaman, but it took all my mana and left me at 25% HP. The third tunnel has the same type mob (one) guarding it as well, so there are 2 level 30 guards to deal with as you leave tunnel 2 and enter tunnel 3. If you have a group, no problem. If you are solo, as I was, you need invisibility, probably from potions, to pass these guards because killing them will flag you PvP, which you do NOT want going into Loch Modan, a completely Alliance-controlled zone. I haven't made it to the end of tunnel 3 yet, so I don't know how many guards there are there. I assume once you're inside Loch M you can run like heck and get to Badlands from there. There is a pass into Badlands in the south-central edge of Loch M zone.) 5. Badlands (Will post on this when i make it in there. Once there as Horde you can get a flight path that connects between Undercity and Booty Bay this is a big one.) 6. The other flight path, to Swamp of Sorrows (SoS): I know this is the only route to Badlands because I tried going another way, in from Stranglethorn and Duskwood from the south, into Redridge Mountains and Burning Steppes. The Steppes are a 50-plus zone don't go there unless you like graveyards. I spent over 5 gold in repair costs once I got out of there. Duskwood has an Alliance town named Darkshire in the NW corner, blocking the roads to Deadwind Pass (DW) zone, which you need to get to Swamp of Sorrows (SoS) for the other flight path Horde has on the south end of this continent. If you can slip up along the east edge of Duskwood, there's a tunnel into DW south of the road through Darkshire that goes to DW. Stay on the road in DW - it's a 50-plus zone. Once in SoS, stay on the roads, which are patrolled by Horde guards. Once you hit the Horde outpost at Stonard (take the right fork), get the flight path there that connects to Booty Bay. Comment4: This quest sucks as a frost mage. As in, every talent point you have is basically useless, and the traditional frost mage methods of snare and kite are impossible as this is immune to frost. However, after several tries, I came up with a strategy that works well to solo this, even as a 0/0/x pure frost mage (for all the good those talents do you here, you might as well be 0/0/0...). This is of course just my opinion, but this worked very well for me and I completed the quest with little difficulty after adopting these methods: 1. First, you must use Dampen Magic. It reduces all damage dealt by the elementals. 2. Second, before you pull, cast Fire Ward on yourself. This will absorb the damage, and Dampen Magic's effect will cause this to last longer. If you want to be extra safe, you can cast this 15 seconds before the pull, so the 30 second cooldown will be up at about the time your ward collapses. 3. When you fight the elemental, make sure you're facing a direction that's clear. The reason being, you can and should Blink out of its stun, but as you're stunned, you can't change direction. Make sure you're facing a good direction to Blink into. Don't burn Blink before it stuns. 4. Always pull with Fireball (or pyroblast if you have it). After this, you're using Arcane Missiles or Arcane Explosion only -- it's fire resist is high enough that you don't want to cast fire spells, at the same time, being as you can cast fireball/pyroblast before it aggros you, it just acts as a little bonus opening damage. Always open at max range to get as much DPS in before it reaches you. 5. Don't try to use Mana Shield, it really doesn't work very well; these things hit hard enough that you'll deplete your mana pool very rapidly.

Comment2: Neltharion the Earth-Warder was one of the five dragons who the Pantheon empowered with immortality, in the hopes that they would protect the world from any interference. Neltharion was forever loyal to his queen, Alexstrasza the Life-Binder, and his friends and kinsmen, Ysera the Dreamer, Malygos the Spell-Weaver and Nozdormu the Timeless. Nelthation fought valiantly alongside his draconic brethren during the War of the Ancients and finally banished them to the Great Dark Beyond, hopefully forever. Exactly where he went wrong is still uncertain. But soon, the creature that was once Neltharion became the evil, insidious force that became known to the mortal races of Azeroth as Deathwing. The Death Aspect. One of the greatest evils ever to breath the air of Azeroth, Deathwing, or Xaxas, as the elves would call him, is the hellish embodiment of all things chaotic and evil. Deathwing's career of treachery began long ago. Being one of the five Aspects, he asked the other four to 'join' him in diverting some power into an artifact that would come to be known as the Demon Soul, telling them that it could be used to protect the world from the Legion when all the dragons had gone, but he did not transfer his power into it and so weakened the others considerably. The resulting war rendered his race all but extinct, and the Demon Soul was made untouchable to him. During the Second War, Deathwing ensured that the orcs would come across the Demon Soul, and they used it to subjugate Alexstrasza, the Red Dragonqueen, and commandeer her progeny to their bidding. Deathwing, too, pledged his loyalty to the Horde, and in return, Goblin alchemists placed adamantium armour over the entire and considerable frame of Deathwing, rendering him almost invincible. After the war's end, Deathwing found solace at Blackrock Spire, where a clutch of renegade dragons were feeding on any humans who strayed too close to their lair. Ner'zhul suggested an alliance, and Deathwing agreed, taking his followers through the portal to roost on a mountainous island across the Devouring Sea from Zeth'kur. Deathwing was believed to be killed, but he instead was simply working to consolidate his power once more. Disguising himself as a human - Lord Prestor - he infiltrated the politics of the Alliance, and seemed set up to take over the nation of Alterac and marry into the royal family of Lordaeron. Meanwhile, he used his many pawns to maneuver the mage Rhonin, who his rival Korialstrasz had been using to attempt to free his lover Alexstrasza, into Grim Batol. Deathwing tried to frighten the Orcs into believing that the Humans were attacking, so that they would move Alexstrasza, and, more importantly, her eggs, north to Dun Algaz, leaving her open for attack and her eggs open to be stolen. Deathwing wished to hatch a fertile female dragon, with whom he could repopulate his dead race of Black Dragons. His attack, however, failed, the Demon Soul was destroyed, and Deathwing was sent retreating with the four other Aspects on his heels. The few survivors of his dragonflight, believing him to be missing or dead, have made their homes in the Barrens of Kalimdor.

Comment3: POOR RICHARD'S ALMANACK: The Un'Goro Pylons By Richard Saunders, Philomath (Silver Hand) If you're of a level to go to Un'Goro Crater, the first thing you will probably do is die. It's a dangerous place, and the first time I was there I fell in from Tanaris, not a good way to live through an initial encounter. So, when you exit the graveyard, you will have found the Eastern Pylon and will have wondered about it, if you are the sort with wonder in their hearts, and not just playing this game to get to max level as fast as possible so you can PvP with all the other ten-year-olds. But I digress. A series of quests, initiated by J.D. Collie in Marshal's Refuge (she is at 41, 2 inside the crystal caves that are behind Dadanga) lead to your rewards. You can however begin harvesting the coloured power crystals much sooner by level 44 I had a fair stock of them, as they often pop up in untenanted areas. You will probably meet her when going through the Linken series of quests. The first crystal-related quest requires you to give her seven of each colour of the power crystals. Then you need to find the three pylons, yes, even if you've found them before. She will then give you a User's Manual to the pylons, which you may discard as your humble & obedient Servant, Poor Richard, has expanded upon it herein. Pylons give up 6 of each item when you activate them. Sale price is 10s for each one. (So I guess the power crustals are worth 3s each-- not bad for dodging dinosaurs!) The effect crystals will be soulbound, but not the coloured power crystals The crystal effects can be grouped roughly as defensive and offensive. Each pylon will give you one from each category. With the exception of Spire, which is a sort of Thorns, the offensive ones are instants and the defensives last a reasonable duration. In the offense group are Charge (fire damage, North pylon) Spire (damage shield, East pylon) and Yield (lower opponent AC, West pylon). More defensive are Force (Spirit bonus, East pylon) Ward (Armor increase, West pylon) and Restore (healing aura, North pylon). One VERY nice thing about Restore is that it doesn't get interrupted while it's working, so you can cast it on yourself in the middle of a fight and it won't get bumped, unlike bandaging and eating. It's saved my hash in close fights more than once and is, I think, my favorite, though I use up an awful lot of the decent flash-bang Charges. Undisputably the hardest pylon to get to is the Western one,guarded as it is by not only higher level opponents (level 53-55) of all stripes but also the elite stegosauri. Stick to the wall and run when the coast is clear, or use your stealth. The North poylon, though it has a few Pterrordaxes flying about, isn't too hard to access and the Eastern one is safe as houses. You may run into a few level 48 Ravasaurs around it but after you die, talk to the Spirit Healer and get the 25% gear damage res, you can wander to it and fill up on ceystals while waiting for resurrection sickness to go away. And of course there are always the Devilsaurs wherever you go. (How exactly does a twenty story tall prehistoric monster sneak up on you? Created by the Martians to destroy the human race, no doubt. The FBI is helpless.) Synopsis: Fill up on Ward and Yield whil you're in the West it may be a while before you get back to it. The crystals themselves can be found scattered liberally throughout the Crater. I can see no rhyme nor reason to their layout, and they regenerate quickly. A rule of thumb: If it looks dangerous to get to the area, don't. Another one will be in a safer area. Oh, yes, they also stack to more than 20, so happy collecting! East pylon 77, 49 CRYSTAL FORCE: Increase Spirit by 30 for 30 minutes. Requires 10 blue, 10 green. CRYSTAL SPIRE: Damage shield, 12 damage to anyone who hits the user. Lasts 10 minutes. Requires 10 blue, 10 yellow. West pylon 23, 59 CRYSTAL WARD: Increase Armor by 200 for 30 minutes. Requires 10 red, 10 green CRYSTALYIELD: Lower opponent's armor by 200 for 2 minutes. Requires 10 red, 10 blue. North pylon 56, 12 CRYSTAL CHARGE. Does 383-517 fire damage in a 3-yard radius. Requires 10 yellow, 10 red. CRYSTAL RESTORE: Heal one target for 670 points over 15 seconds. Requires 10 yellow, 10 green.

Comment1: Here's how it works... You start Neutral and receive .0166% rep bonus for each quest turned in.&nbsp The only quest available is the Frostsaber Provisions one where you have to collect meat from the Chimera and Bears.&nbsp Half way through Neutral (exactly 30 quests), the NPC unlocks a second quest for you.&nbsp This is the Winterfall Intrusion quest.&nbsp 30 more of either quest will get you into Friendly. Once you work your way through Friendly (.0083% rep bonus) and get to Honored (.00415% rep bonus), the NPC unlocks a third quest for you.&nbsp This is the Giants quest in south Winterspring.&nbsp You are required to kill only 8 of the lvl 59-60 elite giants but they're further away and most likely can not be soloed.&nbsp There's really no point in taking the extra time and effort to do this one unless you want to try for some nicer items (Yes, they drop much nicer than the furbolg). Each bar of reputation that you earn cuts the reputation bonus in half.&nbsp [b]60[/b] quests to get Friendly, [b]120[/b] to get Honored, [b]240[/b] to get revered.&nbsp All-in-all, you'll have to do [u]420[/u] of the quests to get ELIDGIBLE for the mount. None of the quests offer a larger rep bonus upon turn in and none of the mobs offer rep bonus upon killing.&nbsp The only way to get rep bonus is at quest turn in. So if that isn't enough of a kick-in-the-pants, just think that you won't even be 1/2 done with the quest until you're 25% into Honored.&nbsp :) Most don't even start, a lot quit after a while, but I'm in it for the long haul.&nbsp Cya on my new mount.

Comment1: The other night I (57 mage) did this with a 54 druid friend, but what surprised me was how far back we had to stay from Ranshalla. The first try we followed at maybe 5-10 yards, but every time Ranshalla drew aggro, the wildkin went right through her and aggro'd the druid. It didn't go well, the druid died, and I escaped to the road with only 5% health remaining. While I was healing up, I got the message that the quest had failed, so this one is not like the standard escort quests. Most likely what happened is that Ranshalla went to the next torch and casted her strange spell, but neither of us were there to click on the torch so it did not light. So very likely that's what failed the quest and not too much distance which normally causes escort quests to fail. The next time we tried it we both kept back from Ranshalla at the limit of my casting range and that worked very well - Ranshalla became the tank and we just nuked any wildkin that wanted to fight. Another note - only one party member needs to light the torch for everyone to keep advancing the quest, so if you bring a group, select one to go with Ranshalla, everyone else can just kill the wildkin to keep the area clear. The ending animation for this quest is very cool and something that I wish WoW had more of. FFXI was full of great cutscenes like this and something that I've missed since departing from that game. Maybe BC will bring more of these kinds of animations, but who knows ...
Comment2: On the surface this can appear quite daunting but theres an easy way round it for the right classes... To start with she can be found by simply riding the road to south and looking to the left side of the road when you reach the 'owl wing thicket'. Now she just walks to each cave in turn ignoring the beasts, but, if you let her get attacked first (shock horror!) then she will fight back and you can then take the aggro off her and she'll help you fight the target.&nbsp Also you can heal and buff her so dont forget to use this. Make sure you get her to help as much as you can, it slows her up and makes things easier on you. Also note her threat area is quite small so stay back and let her lead to ensure you dont pull first. If you do by accident, dont panic, she's quite tough and can take a good few hits herself before you need to step in. Soloed at 56 druid without one potion. good luck.

If you equip this item in your trinket slot, it will drain both your mana and your hp until you either remove the item or you die. The number it drains both by is random, so sometimes it will only drain a low amount of hp/mana every second (100 of each), or it will drain a large amount of hp/mana (500 of each). Usually the numbers will fall inbetween the two extremes. Although you are technically supposed to turn this in to complete the questline it is involved with, you might want to hold onto it for it's special lethal properties When a character is killed by equipping this item, that character will not suffer any armor damage. This is useful if one needs to kill themself in order to speak with ghost characters, such as the ghost in BRD in order to get the Shadowforge Key quest. Also, if you get stuck in a location that you cannot easily get out of and your hearthstone's cooldown is not up yet, you can use this item to kill yourself so that you can be sent to the nearest graveyard. Personally, if you are not going to be benefited by any of the rewards, experience, or money, you might want to hold onto this unique, suicidal item instead of turning it in.

Comment5: The objectives here list Ghak Healtouch, who is the Alliance questgiver for this quest. Aside from that difference, the quest is the same for both sides. Though this is an elite quest, it can easily be soloed. First, you have to have done the Badlands Reagent I and the Uldaman Reagent quests. Second, this appears to be a quest for Artisan Alchemists only. Now maybe it was a bug, but I came by this questgiver 3-4 times from my mid-late 40s and at alchemy skill levels ranging from 170-210, but the first time the quest was available was after I'd achieved Artisan status and skilled up to 230. So my guess is that you either have to be at or above 225 or have gotten Artisan training. Once you get the quest, go to the Badlands and head towards Lethlor Ravine in the East end of the zone where the dragon whelps hang out. Keep heading east as the path winds south and then north till you hit large open area populated by several Scorched Guardian Dragons. Open up the box and take out the Thaumaturgy Vessels. (They bind on pick-up.) To drain the blood, simply target one of the dragons and use one of the vessels on it. (You have to do this with a live dragon.) You can drain from range (`20-25 feet), which is a good thing because the dragon will attack as soon as you start. The draining procedure is like a channeled spell, so you can't do anything else until the draining stops. If you drain at range, the dragon will probably only get 2-3 hits on you before you can respond. The dragons are all elites, so they're tough to solo if you're near their level (44-45 mostly). However, the quest doesn't require you to kill them, so simplest thing is to cut and run as soon as you finish draining them. A guardian won't follow you very far beyond that big open area. Just be careful that you don't run into a couple of dragon whelps back in the ravine. (I avoided this by running up the rock wall just to the E of the southern entrance to the guardians' area the whelps don't hang out here, but you can run far enough along the wall to lose the guardian.) After you complete the quest, you will be taught how to make the Elixer of Restoration. Edited, Fri Mar 4 13:09:01 2005

In this area, the mobs are more manageable, since most groups are between one and three monsters. Simply pull to where you came out off (the drop gate) and fight each group there. Move towards the ziggurat. If you look to the right of the ziggurat, you will see a side street, some boxes and a set of plans on the floor. Comment2: To start with, kudos to Huntn for posting a relatively comprehensive 'walkthrough' for this quest. The following post is an add-on to his post and will be borrowing liberally from some of his notes. If you wish to go down the path of Armorsmith, ensure that you have the following items: (1) Patience (2) More Patience (3) Lots of Cash or (4) More Patience. My attempts at irony aside, to be an Armorsmith: (1) It is *advisable* (meaning its not crucial) to have your Blacksmith skill at 220 or thereabouts as you have to learn some recipes from a goblin in Booty Bay and he will only teach you if your skill is 230 or thereabouts. However, bear in mind that your skills will be rising when you craft some of the items involved in this quest. (2) Talk to Expert Blacksmith Trainer in Ironforge at 210 skill in blacksmith. (3) He will direct you to Grumnus Steelshaper standing by the Great Forge in Ironforge who gives you a quest to make the following items: (a) Ornate Mithril Helmets X 4 (16 Mithril Bars X 4, 2 Truesilver Bar x 4, Solid Grinding Stone X 4, 4 Black Pearls X 4) (b) Ornate Mithril Boots X 2 (14 Mithril Bars X 2, 2 Truesilver Bar x 2, 4 Thick Leather x 2, Solid Grinding Stone x 2, Aquamarine X 2) (c) Ornate Mithril Breast Plate X 1 (16 Mithril Bars, 6 Truesilver, Heart of Fire, Solid Grinding Stone) At which point you will be stumped as you neither have the recipes/know how to craft them nor do you know where to head to...till Anonymous's guides came along. (4)Take the griff/train to Stormwind City ('SW') to look&nbsp for an NPC by the name of Hank the Hammer in the Dwarven District right by the forge area in SW. He will give you a quest called 'The Origins of Smithing' which requires you to craft 6 Golden Scale Bracers [30 Steel Bars, 12 Heavy Grinding Stones (translates to 36 Heavy Stones)]. Once completed, he will give you a quest to see another NPC by the name of McGavan in Booty Bay. (5) Talk to McGavan who then gives you a quest called 'The Mithril Order' to talk to Galvan the Ancient. ('Galvan') Galvan is between Zul Gurub and the Mosh'Ogg Ogre mound in STV. Cosmos locs are 50,21. NOTE : Before you start tramping out of Booty Bay, try and learn the following recipes from Brikk Keencraft - Mithril Coif and Heavy Mithril Breastplate. (230 blacksmith skill pre-requisite) (6) Once you meet Galvan, he will give you 3 quests: (a) Bring 40 Mithril Bars, 5 True Silver to him. ('The Great Silver Deceiver') (b) Bring 40 Mithril Bars, 40 Iron Bars to him. ('Smelt On, Smelt Off') (c) Bring 40 Mithril Bars, 4 Citrine to him. ('The Art of Imbue') Completing each quest will allow you to learn more recipes needed to complete your ultimate quest. Once all quests are done, speak to Galvan again and he will then direct you to see another NPC by the name of Trenton Lighthammer in the town of Gadgetzan in Tanaris. ('Galvan's Finest Pupil') Trenton is by a forge in the town of Gadgetzan. (7) Once you meet Trenton, he will give you 3 quests: (a) A Good Head on Your Shoulders which requires crafting Mithril Coifs X 2 (10 Mithril Bars x 2, 6 Mageweave x 2), Ornate Mithril Shoulder x 1. (12 Mithril Bars, 1 Truesilver, 6 Thick Leather) (b) The World at Your Feet which requires crafting Heavy Mithril Boots X 2 (14 Mithril Bars x 2, 4 Thick Leather x 2), Ornate Mithril Pants X 1. (12 Mithril Bars, 1 Truesilver, 1 Solid Grinding Stone, 1 Aquamarine) (c) The Mithril Kid which requires crafting Heavy Mithril Breastplate X 2 (16 Mithril Bars X 2), Ornate Mithril Gloves X 1. (10 Mithril Bars, 6 Mageweave Cloth, 1 Truesilver, 1 Solid Grinding Stone) When you complete each quest, you will be taught more recipes wherein one of it is the ornate mithril helmet recipe. (8) Armed with all the recipes, then its back to Ironforge to complete 'The Art of the Armorsmith'. Read note (3) again for ingredients required to craft the items. If you have the items, craft away and voila quest is complete. (9) Turn in the quest. Congratulations! You are an Armorsmith and will be able to learn 2 more recipes Truesilver Breastplate and Truesilver Gauntlet. (Blue Items but cost wise are pretty expensive to craft) Well, hope this helps. Niz
